Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or till set. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Greek comfort food - similar to lasagna but with macaroni
Ground lamb is traditional but beef works well too
Can be assembled ahead and refrigerated; add 10-15 minutes to baking time if cold

recipes.title: Tomato Juice Cocktail
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 199 (Freezing & Canning section)
recipes.description: Homemade tomato juice cocktail seasoned with celery, onion, and spices. Can be canned or frozen.

instructions.text: Thoroughly wash tomatoes. Remove stems. Cut tomatoes into pieces. In an 8- or 10-quart kettle or Dutch oven combine tomatoes, celery, and onion.
Bring to boiling, stirring frequently. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes or till soft, stirring often.
Press through a food mill or sieve to extract juice. Discard solids. Return juice to kettle.
Stir in lemon juice, sugar, Worcestershire sauce, horseradish, salt, and hot pepper sauce. Bring to boiling.
Pour hot juice into hot, clean pint jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace.

notes: Pressure Canning: Process pints for 15 minutes at 10 pounds pressure (adjust for altitude)
Freezing: Cool juice. Pour into wide-top freezer containers, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Process pints for 15 minutes. Seal, label, and freeze.
Note: Tomatoes should be ripe but still firm. Start with the smaller amount of horseradish and add more until you get the zest you like.

recipes.title: Macaroni and Cheese (BHG)
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 160
recipes.description: Classic baked macaroni and cheese with shredded American cheese.

instructions.text: Cook macaroni according to package directions (see chart, page 278); drain well.

Meanwhile, for cheese sauce, in a saucepan cook onion in margarine or butter till tender but not brown. Stir in flour and pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till slightly thickened and bubbly. Add shredded cheese; stir till melted.

Stir macaroni into cheese sauce. Transfer to a 1-quart casserole. Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or till bubbly. During the last 5 minutes of baking, arrange tomato slices atop macaroni, if desired. Let stand 10 minutes.

notes: Microwave directions: Cook macaroni as above. For cheese sauce, in a 1-1/2-quart casserole micro-cook onion and margarine or butter on 100% power (high) for 1 to 2 minutes or till onion is tender. Stir in flour and pepper. Stir in milk. Cook on high for 3 to 5 minutes or till slightly thickened and bubbly, stirring every minute. Stir till cheese melts. Stir in cooked macaroni. Cook on high for 2-1/2 to 3-1/2 minutes or till heated through, stirring once. If desired, place tomato slices atop macaroni during the last minute of cooking. Let stand 10 minutes.

Vegetable Macaroni and Cheese: Prepare as above, except stir 2 cups frozen mixed vegetables, thawed, or one 16-ounce can mixed vegetables, drained, into cheese sauce with macaroni. Transfer to a 2-1/2-quart casserole.

Shortcut Macaroni and Cheese: Prepare as above, except immediately return the drained macaroni to the saucepan it was cooked in. Pour the cheese sauce over the macaroni; mix well. Cook over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes or till heated through, stirring frequently. Let stand for 10 minutes.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Welsh Rarebit Breakfast
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 160
recipes.description: The tangy cheese sauce also is good served over broccoli, cauliflower, and burgers.

ingredients.item: English muffins, split and toasted, or slices bread, toasted
slices Canadian-style bacon, warmed, or 4 poached eggs

instructions.text: For English muffin or toast stacks, place muffin halves or toast slices on plates. Top each with a slice of Canadian-style bacon, then a tomato slice; or, if using poached eggs, top muffins or toast with tomato slices, then eggs. Set aside.
For cheese sauce, in a heavy medium saucepan combine cheese, milk, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and red pepper. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, till cheese melts.
Slowly stir about half of the hot cheese sauce into beaten egg; return all to the saucepan. Cook and stir over low heat till cheese sauce thickens slightly and just bubbles.
Serve cheese sauce immediately over English muffin or toast stacks. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Beer Rarebit: Prepare as above, except substitute 8 slices crisp-cooked bacon, drained and halved crosswise, for the Canadian-style bacon or poached egg. Substitute beer for the milk.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Meatless Red Beans and Rice
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 161
recipes.description: Adjust the amount of ground red pepper to give this dish the zing you like.

ingredients.item: dry red beans or dry red kidney beans

instructions.text: Rinse beans. In a large saucepan combine beans and 3 cups water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Cover and let stand 1 hour. (Or, soak by placing beans and 3 cups water in a bowl. Cover and set in a cool place for 6 to 8 hours or overnight.)

Drain beans in a colander and rinse. Return beans to the saucepan. Stir in onion, garlic, bay leaf, salt, fennel seed, red pepper, and 3 cups fresh water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 2 1/2 hours or till beans are tender, adding more water, if necessary, and stirring occasionally.
Uncover and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 15 to 20 minutes more or till a thick gravy forms. Discard bay leaf. Serve over rice. Serves 4.

notes: Meaty Red Beans and Rice: Prepare as above, except omit salt and fennel seed. Add 1/2 pound smoked pork hocks or meaty ham bone with onion. When beans are tender, remove hocks or ham bone. Cut meat from bones or bone. Discard bones or bone and return meat to bean mixture along with 1/2 pound smoked sausage, cut into bite-size pieces.
Red Beans and Corn Bread: Prepare as above, except omit rice and spoon bean mixture over squares of corn bread.

missing_inputs: Not in database: fennel seed, crushed

recipes.title: Meatless Tacos
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 162

ingredients.item: tofu (fresh bean curd), drained and finely chopped

instructions.text: Rinse lentils; drain. In a medium saucepan combine lentils, onion, and 1 1/2 cup water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 30 minutes or till tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir tomato sauce and seasoning mix into lentils. Simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Stir in tofu; heat through. Spoon into taco shells. Top with lettuce, tomato, cheese, and salsa. Serves 4.

notes: Bulgur Tacos: Prepare as above, except substitute bulgur for lentils. Cover and simmer bulgur, onion, and 3/4 cup water about 10 minutes or till tender and liquid is absorbed.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Garbanzo Sandwich Spread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 162
recipes.description: Serve this spread for lunch in pita bread or on bagels, or as appetizer on party rye bread.

instructions.text: In a blender container or food processor bowl combine beans, tahini, juice, oil, garlic, paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cover; blend or process till smooth, scraping sides as necessary. Transfer to a bowl.
Stir in parsley and pimiento. Cover; chill 2 to 24 hours.

notes: Mediterranean Sandwich Spread: Spread about 1/3 cup cold Garbanzo Sandwich Spread on 1 slice whole wheat bread. Top with 2 tomato slices, 1 slice Swiss or brick cheese, and another slice bread. Makes 1 serving.
Tahini Substitute: Stir together 3 tablespoons creamy peanut butter and 1 tablespoon sesame oil till well combined. Makes 1/4 cup.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Fried-Rice Supper
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 162
recipes.description: The rice is chilled to keep it from sticking. A quick and easy one-pan meal.

instructions.text: In a large skillet melt the 1 teaspoon margarine. Add beaten egg. Cook egg without stirring till set. Invert skillet to remove egg; cut into strips.
In the skillet cook onions and garlic in the 1 tablespoon margarine till tender. Add rice; cook and stir for 3 minutes.
Stir in beans, soy sauce, sherry, oil, and red pepper. Cook and stir till heated through.
Toss with nuts and egg strips.

notes: Tip: Chilling the rice keeps it from sticking and clumping when stir-fried
Quick meal - marked as FAST in cookbook

recipes.title: Bean and Cheese Burritos
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 162

instructions.text: Stack six 8-inch flour tortillas and wrap in foil. Heat in a 350° oven for 10 minutes to soften. In a skillet cook 1 cup chopped onion in 1 tablespoon cooking oil till tender. Add one 16-ounce can refried beans. Cook and stir till heated through.

Spoon about 1/4 cup bean mixture onto each tortilla just below center. Divide 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar cheese among tortillas. Fold edge nearest filling up and over just till mixture is covered. Fold in 2 sides just till they meet; roll up.
Place on a baking sheet. Bake in a 350° oven about 10 minutes or till heated through. Serve with shredded lettuce and salsa. Serves 3.

notes: Bean and Cheese Chimichangas: Prepare as above, except use 10-inch flour tortillas and omit baking. Secure rolled-up tortillas with wooden toothpicks. In a 3-quart saucepan fry tortillas, 2 or 3 at a time, in 1 inch hot cooking oil (375°) about 1 minute on each side or till golden. Drain. Keep warm in a 300° oven. Remove picks. Pass dairy sour cream and guacamole.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Marinated Salmon Steaks
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 167

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen salmon (or halibut) steaks, cut 1 inch thick
finely shredded lemon, lime, or orange peel

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut steaks into serving-size portions. For marinade, in a shallow dish combine juice, oil, lemon peel, Worcestershire sauce, rosemary or thyme, and garlic.
Place fish in marinade. Pour marinade over fish. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, turning fish once.

Place fish on the greased unheated rack of a broiler pan. Brush with half of the remaining marinade. Broil 4 inches from the heat 5 minutes. Turn fish. Brush with remaining marinade. Broil for 3 to 7 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 167)

recipes.title: Herbed Sauce for Fish
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 167
recipes.description: A quick herbed butter sauce to brush over fish during baking or broiling.

ingredients.item: dried dillweed, basil, rosemary, or oregano

instructions.text: In a small saucepan melt margarine or butter.
Stir in lemon juice, dried herb of choice (crushed), and pepper.
Brush over fish during baking or broiling (see fish cooking chart, page 185).

notes: Marked as FAST in cookbook
Choose your herb based on the fish: dillweed pairs well with salmon, basil with white fish, rosemary with heartier fish

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 167)

recipes.title: Halibut with Sherry Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 168

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen halibut (or other fish) steaks, cut 1 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Place fish on the greased unheated rack of a broiler pan. Brush with half of the margarine, melted. Broil 4 inches from the heat 5 minutes. Turn fish. Brush with remaining margarine. Broil for 3 to 7 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

Meanwhile, in a small saucepan cook onions and garlic in the 4 tablespoons margarine or butter till tender. Stir in flour. Add sherry and broth all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Add cheese and beer. Cook and stir till cheese melts. Spoon over fish. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 168)

recipes.title: Teriyaki Shark
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 168

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen shark steaks, cut 1 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut fish into 1-inch cubes. Place fish, mushrooms, onions in a plastic bag; set bag into a bowl. Combine oil, wine or orange juice, garlic, orange peel, and marinate at room temperature for 2 hours, turning bag occasionally. Drain fish cubes.

On eight 12-inch skewers alternately thread fish cubes, mushrooms, and onions, leaving about 1/4 inch between pieces. Place on the greased unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from the heat for 4 to 5 minutes. Turn kabobs over. Broil for 4 to 6 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork. To serve, add a tomato to each skewer. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 168)

recipes.title: Dijon-Mustard Fish Fillets
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 168
recipes.description: Broiled fish fillets topped with a creamy Dijon mustard sauce.

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish.
Place fish on unheated rack of broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from heat till fish flakes easily with a fork. Allow 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness. Turn once if more than 1 inch thick.
Meanwhile, in small saucepan stir together sour cream, milk, mustard, and chives.
Cook and stir over low heat till heated through (do not boil). Spoon sauce over fish.

notes: Marked as FAST in cookbook
Do not boil the sauce or it may curdle

recipes.title: Swordfish Kabobs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 168
recipes.description: Marinated swordfish, tuna, or shark cubes on skewers with mushrooms and green onions.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen swordfish, tuna, or shark

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut into 1 inch cubes. Place fish, mushrooms, and onions in a plastic bag set in a bowl.
Combine oil, wine, garlic, orange peel, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and pepper. Add to bag. Seal bag and marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes (or in refrigerator for 2 hours), turning occasionally.
Drain fish cubes, reserving marinade. On eight 12-inch skewers, alternately thread fish cubes, mushrooms, and onion pieces.
Place on greased unheated rack of broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from heat for 4 to 5 minutes. Turn kabobs. Brush with marinade.
Broil 4 to 5 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

notes: Swordfish's firm flesh makes it ideal for kabobs
Grill directions: Assemble and marinate kabobs as above. Add a cherry tomato to each skewer. Grill, uncovered, directly over medium-hot coals for 8 to 12 minutes, turning once.

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Fish Kabobs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 169

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen swordfish, tuna, or tuna steaks, cut 1 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut fish into 1-inch cubes. Cook carrots in a small amount of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes or till almost tender; drain.
For the sauce, in a small saucepan combine preserves, lemon juice, and oil. Cook over low heat till preserves melt, stirring constantly.

Alternately thread fish cubes, carrot slices, and pineapple chunks on four 8-inch kabobs, leaving about 1/4 inch between pieces. Place kabobs on the greased unheated rack of broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from the heat for 4 to 5 minutes. Turn kabobs. Brush with sauce during the last 2 minutes of broiling. Brush again with sauce before serving.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 169)

recipes.title: Blackened Thai Catfish
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 169
recipes.description: Cajun-spiced catfish fillets cooked in a very hot cast-iron skillet until blackened.

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish.
Combine garlic powder, white pepper, red pepper, thyme, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Sprinkle spice mixture evenly on both sides of fish fillets.
In a 12-inch cast-iron or heavy skillet, melt 1 tablespoon margarine over medium-high heat.
Add fish fillets. Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side for 1/2-inch thick fillets (or 4 to 5 minutes per side for thicker fillets) or till fish flakes easily with a fork.
Add remaining margarine during cooking. Drizzle melted margarine over fish before serving.

notes: Stand back! This Cajun specialty really smokes up as it cooks. That's why it's best to grill.
To cook outdoors: Turn on exhaust fan or cook outside. Place a cast-iron skillet on the grill rack directly over hot coals. Heat until drops of water sizzle.

recipes.title: Dill Smoked Cod
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 169
recipes.description: Whole dressed cod slow-smoked on the grill with dill and wood chips.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen dressed cod or other fish

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Soak wood chips in enough water to cover for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, cut 1/2-inch-deep diagonal slits 1 inch apart into both sides of fish.
Rub oil into slits. Then press a piece of dillweed into each slit. Use wooden toothpicks to hold fish together if needed.
Drain chips. In a covered grill, arrange preheated coals around a foil drip pan. Test for medium coals.
Place chips on coals. Place foil on rack above drip pan. Place the fish on foil.
Grill fish, covered, 50 to 60 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

notes: Cherry or apple wood chips add a mild, sweet smoke flavor
The diagonal slits help the dill flavor penetrate the fish

recipes.title: Fish with Beer-Cheese Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 170

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen fish fillets or steaks

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish. In a large skillet cook fish in hot oil, uncovered, for 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness or till fish flakes easily with a fork (turning fish once if fish is 1 inch thick or more). Keep warm.

For sauce, in a saucepan cook onion in margarine till tender. Add flour and, if desired, mustard. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Add cheese and beer. Cook and stir till cheese melts. Spoon over fish. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 170)

recipes.title: Citrus Baked Halibut
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 170

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen halibut steaks, chopped on thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Arrange in an 8x8x2-inch baking dish. Cook orange and garlic in margarine. Stir in parsley and lemon juice. Pour over fish.
Bake in a 400° oven for 20 to 25 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 170)

recipes.title: Fish Potpies
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 170
recipes.description: Individual fish potpies with vegetables and Swiss cheese in marinara sauce, topped with pastry.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen haddock, cod, or orange roughy fillets

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. In saucepan combine marinara sauce, vegetables, carrot, cheese, parsley, and pimiento. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly.
Cut fish into four pieces; stir into cheese mixture.
Spoon into four greased 8 or 10-ounce casseroles.
Cut pastry into 4 wedges. Place one pastry wedge on each casserole. Trim to fit. Cut slits into pastry.
Place on a baking sheet. Bake in a 400°F oven for 20 to 25 minutes or till golden brown. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 170)

recipes.title: Fish Stacks
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 170
recipes.description: Fish fillets topped with creamy vegetable mixture and crescent roll dough.

instructions.text: Thaw fish fillets. Cut into 4x3-inch portions. Place in a shallow baking dish.
Cook onion, carrot, and mushrooms in margarine, covered, about 5 minutes. Uncover; simmer 2 to 4 minutes more or till excess liquid evaporates.
Remove from heat. Stir in cream cheese, dillweed, and pepper. Spoon vegetable mixture over each fish portion.
Separate crescent rolls into 2 rectangles. Pinch perforations to seal. Cut each rectangle in half.
Place one rectangle atop each fish portion. Brush dough with milk, if desired.
Bake in a 350°F oven for 20 to 25 minutes or till fish is done and dough is golden.

notes: The cream cheese and vegetable topping keeps the fish moist

recipes.title: Broccoli-Stuffed Sole
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 171

ingredients.item: frozen cut broccoli (or other fish fillets)
cream cheese with chives and onion
white wine or dry white wine

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. For stuffing, cook broccoli according to package directions. Drain. Cut up any large pieces. Combine broccoli and cheeses.
Place stuffing at one end of each fillet. Roll up fish. Secure with wooden toothpicks, if necessary.
Place fish rolls with stuffing side up in a 1-quart casserole; sprinkle with crumbs. Set aside.
In a saucepan cook milk and wine over medium heat, stirring often. Serve over fish. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 171)

recipes.title: Baked Fish with Mushrooms
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 171

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen fish fillets or steaks, cut 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Arrange fish in a 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. Sprinkle with mushrooms, onion, and tarragon. Dot with margarine. Sprinkle with salt and paprika.
Bake, covered, in a 450° oven for 6 to 10 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 171)

recipes.title: Wild-Rice-Stuffed Fish
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 171
recipes.description: Whole dressed fish stuffed with a wild rice, mushroom, and vegetable mixture.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen dressed whitefish or other fish

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Rinse rice thoroughly.
Cook mushrooms, celery, onion, and garlic in margarine till tender.
Stir in broth and wild rice. Cover and simmer 45 to 50 minutes till rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in pimiento, sherry, parsley, and lemon peel.
Spoon stuffing into fish cavities, pressing lightly with back of spoon so fish lies flat.
Place stuffed fish in a large baking dish. Cover loosely with foil.
Bake in a 350°F oven for 30 to 40 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Use two large spatulas to transfer fish to serving platter.

notes: Tip: Spoon stuffing into fish, then press lightly with the back of the spoon so the fish lies flat
Use two large spatulas for transferring the stuffed fish

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 171)

recipes.title: Fish en Papillote
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 172
recipes.description: En papillote (pah-pee-YOHT) is French for 'in paper.' It's a simple yet elegant way to cook fish.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen skinless pompano, perch, sole, or flounder fish fillets

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut 4 pieces of parchment paper or brown paper into heart shapes, 12 inches wide and 9 inches long.

In a large skillet bring water, lemon slices, bay leaf, and bouillon granules to boiling. Add fish. Simmer, covered, for 4 to 6 minutes or till fish flakes easily. Using a slotted spoon, carefully remove fish.
In a saucepan melt margarine; stir in flour and mustard. Add milk; cook and stir till thickened.

To assemble each packet, place one fillet on half of each parchment heart. Top with one-fourth of the sauce. Fold the other half of the heart over fillet. Starting at the top, seal by turning up edges of heart and folding in twice. At bottom, twist the tip of heart to seal. Place packets on a large baking sheet. Bake in a 400° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or till slightly puffed. Transfer to dinner plates. To serve, cut an X in top of each. Pull back the paper. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 172)

recipes.title: Chilled Salmon Steaks
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 173

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen salmon steaks, cut 1/2 to 3/4 inches thick
chicken bouillon cube or 1/2 tsp instant bouillon granules

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Place steaks in a 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. Add bouillon to boiling water. Pour over fish.

Bake in a 450° oven 8 to 12 minutes or till fish flakes. Remove fish. For marinade, stir in oil, parsley, sweet red pepper, onion, and mustard. Pour over fish. Cover; chill 4 to 24 hours. Shake well. Pour marinade over fish. Serves 4.

flags.issue: Several ingredients reconstructed from instructions (bouillon, water, red pepper)

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 173)

recipes.title: Poached Fish with Dill Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 173

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. In a fish poacher or a large roasting pan that has a wire rack with handles, add enough water to almost reach the handles. Remove the rack. Add 3 lemon slices, bay leaf, 1/4 teaspoon dried tarragon, crushed, and grease rack; set aside. Add 3 lemon slices over pan top. Cover pan, set over two burners on range; bring to boiling. Reduce heat. Lower fish on rack into pan. Simmer, covered, 35 to 40 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Remove fish; keep warm. Reserve 1 cup of cooking liquid for the sauce.

For dill sauce, in a saucepan cook 1/4 cup dillweed, snipped; 1/2 teaspoon dried dillweed; 1/4 teaspoon sugar. Cook in 4 tablespoons margarine or butter. Stir in 4 teaspoons all-purpose flour; 1/2 teaspoon dried dillweed. Add reserved liquid, stir about 1/2 cup of the mixture into 1 beaten egg yolk; return to saucepan. Cook and stir till bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Pass sauce with fish. Serves 6.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 173)

recipes.title: Vegetable-Topped Fillets
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 173
recipes.description: Colorful fish fillets topped with sauteed summer squash, zucchini, and tomatoes.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen skinless sole or other white fish fillets

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish.
Place fish in a greased baking dish. Bake in a 450°F oven till fish flakes easily (4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness).
Meanwhile, in a skillet cook zucchini, summer squash, and garlic in margarine till nearly tender.
Add tomatoes and basil. Cook and stir 2 minutes more.
Spoon vegetable mixture over baked fish.

notes: A colorful, healthy topping for mild white fish
Microwave directions: Cook vegetables in margarine in a microwave-safe dish on high for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring once. Add tomatoes and basil; cook 1 minute more.

recipes.title: Trout Amandine
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 174
recipes.description: The perfect recipe for freshly caught trout. The fillets in your freezer also taste great pan-fried your catch of the day.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen dressed rainbow trout or other fish fillets (about 8 oz each)

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Bone fish if desired. Combine flour and salt.
Coat fish with flour mixture. Dip in egg mixture, then coat with flour mixture again.

In a 12-inch skillet heat oil. Fry fish on one side for 5 to 6 minutes or till golden. Fry fish on the other side for 5 to 6 minutes more or till fish flakes easily. Remove fish; keep warm in a 300° oven while frying remaining fish.
For almond sauce, in a medium saucepan stir together almonds, margarine, and lemon juice over fish. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 174)

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Fish
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 174
recipes.description: The crispy coating seals in the fresh fish flavor.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen fish fillets (1/4 to 1 inch thick)
cornmeal or fine dry bread crumbs
shortening or cooking oil for frying

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish. Cut into serving-size portions. Pat dry. In a shallow dish, mix egg and 2 tablespoons water. In another dish, mix cornmeal or bread crumbs, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and dash pepper. Dip fish into egg mixture, then coat with cornmeal mixture.

In a large skillet heat 1/4 inch melted shortening or oil. Add fish in a single layer. (If fillets have skin, fry skin side last.) Fry fish on one side till golden. Allow 3 to 4 minutes per side for 1/2-inch-thick fillets (5 to 6 minutes per side for 3/4-inch-thick fillets). Turn carefully. Fry till golden and fish flakes easily with a fork. Dry on paper towels. Keep fish warm in a 300° oven while frying remaining fish. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Curried Pan-Fried Fish: Prepare as above, except add 1 tablespoon lemon or lime juice and 2 teaspoons curry powder to cornmeal mixture. Serve with chutney.
Potato-Chip Pan-Fried Fish: Prepare as above, except substitute finely crushed potato chips or saltine crackers for the cornmeal.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 174)

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Stir-Fried Fish
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 175

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen monkfish steaks, cut into pieces or cubed

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut fish into 1-inch pieces. Combine pineapple, reserving 2 tablespoons juice.

In a large skillet or wok, combine sugar, cornstarch, reserved pineapple juice, sherry, 3 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1/4 cup water. Add pineapple, cook and stir till bubbly. Stir in fish and green onions. Cook, uncovered, for 3 to 5 minutes or till fish flakes easily. Stir frequently. Remove fish and vegetables.
Serve over hot cooked rice. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 175)

recipes.title: Fish and Chips
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 175

ingredients.item: shortening or cooking oil for deep-fat frying

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. For chips, cut 3 peeled medium potatoes lengthwise into 3/8-inch-wide sticks. Pat dry.

In a heavy saucepan or deep-fat fryer heat 2 inches shortening or cooking oil for deep-fat frying to 375°. Fry potatoes in hot fat, about one-third at a time, for 4 to 6 minutes or till lightly browned. Remove from fat. Drain on paper towels. Keep warm in a 300° oven while frying fish.

Pat fish dry with paper towels. Cut into serving-size pieces. For batter, combine 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 cup beer or milk, beat till smooth. Dip fish into batter. Fry fish in hot fat, 2 or 3 pieces at a time, about 2 minutes or till golden brown, about 2 minutes on each side or till golden brown. Drain; keep warm in oven while frying remaining fish. Serve with malt or cider vinegar, if desired. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 175)

recipes.title: Hot Tuna Cups
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 175
recipes.description: Creamy tuna filling baked in biscuit cups topped with cheese and tomato.

instructions.text: Separate biscuits. Grease the outside of six 6-ounce custard cups.
Press one biscuit over bottom and halfway down sides of each custard cup.
Place cups, dough side up, on a 15x10x1-inch baking pan. Bake in a 400°F oven 7 minutes or till lightly browned. Remove biscuits from cups immediately.
Meanwhile, cook celery and onion in margarine till tender. Stir in mustard, tuna, peas, and half of the cheese.
Spoon tuna mixture into biscuit cups. Top with tomato slices and remaining cheese.
Return to oven and bake 7 minutes or till cheese melts.

notes: A creative way to serve tuna salad in edible biscuit cups

recipes.title: Creamed Tuna
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 175

instructions.text: In a saucepan cook onion in margarine till tender. Stir in flour, 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly.
Stir in tuna. Heat through. Serve over English muffin halves. If desired, sprinkle with almonds. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 175)

recipes.title: Tuna-Noodle Casserole
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 176
recipes.description: Homestyle cooking at its best.

ingredients.item: can condensed cream of mushroom soup
can chunk-style tuna, drained and broken into chunks

instructions.text: Cook noodles according to package directions; drain and set aside. Meanwhile, in a saucepan cook celery and onion in margarine or butter till tender. Stir in tuna or salmon; pimiento. Gently stir in cooked noodles. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Transfer to a 1 1/2-quart casserole. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake in a 375° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or till bubbly. Garnish with parsley sprigs, if desired. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Vegetable Tuna-Noodle Casserole: Prepare as above except stir in 1 cup cooked vegetable (such as peas, carrots, or green beans) with the tuna.

Extra-Creamy Tuna-Noodle Casserole: Prepare as above except substitute one 8-ounce carton dairy sour cream or substitute one 8-ounce carton plain yogurt for the milk. Stir 1 to 2 tablespoons milk into mixture, if necessary, to obtain desired consistency.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 176)

recipes.title: Tuna-Broccoli Crepes
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 176
recipes.description: Special enough for company.

ingredients.item: can tuna, drained and flaked or one 7 1/2-ounce can salmon, drained, flaked, and skin and bones removed

instructions.text: Cook broccoli according to package directions. Drain. Cut up any large broccoli pieces. Set aside.

For cheese sauce, in a medium saucepan cook onion in margarine or butter till tender but not brown. Stir in flour, mustard, and pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Add cheese. Cook and stir till melted and blended. Remove from heat.

Combine broccoli and 3/4 cup of the tuna sauce. Spoon about 3 tablespoons of the tuna mixture onto the unbrowned side of each crepe; roll up. Place crepes, seam side down, in a 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. Bake, covered, in a 375° oven for 20 to 25 minutes or till heated through.

Reheat the remaining cheese sauce. Stir in additional milk, if necessary, to obtain desired consistency. To serve, spoon remaining cheese sauce over crepes. Sprinkle with paprika and, if desired, top with toasted almonds. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 176)

recipes.title: Tuna-Biscuit Casseroles
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 177
recipes.description: Biscuits are refrigerated biscuits.

instructions.text: Cook onion in margarine till tender. Stir in flour, bouillon granules, thyme, and pepper. Add milk. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in vegetables, tuna, and parsley. Heat through.

Spoon mixture into six 10-ounce casseroles or custard cups. Quarter each biscuit. Arrange 6 to 7 pieces atop each casserole. Place on baking sheet. Bake in a 400° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or till biscuits are lightly browned. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 177)

recipes.title: Salmon Loaf
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 177
recipes.description: No time for the sauce? Cook a package of frozen peas and onions to take over the loaf.

ingredients.item: can pink salmon, bones removed, drained and flaked
cans tuna, drained, flaked, and two 6 1/2-ounce cans American cheese slices

instructions.text: In a saucepan cook onion, dillweed, and a dash pepper in margarine till onion is tender. Combine onion mixture, milk, and egg. Stir in salmon, bread crumbs. Shape mixture into a 6x3-inch loaf in a greased shallow baking pan. Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes. Top with Cheese Sauce or 2 American cheese slices, if desired. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 177)

recipes.title: Fast Fish Fix-Ups (Quick Sauces)
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 177
recipes.description: Three quick sauces to dress up baked fish fillets, fish portions, or fish sticks.

ingredients.item: Note: Choose one of the three sauce recipes below

instructions.text: DILLY-BUTTER SAUCE: Melt 1/4 cup margarine or butter in a saucepan. Stir in 1 tablespoon flour and 1/4 teaspoon dried dillweed. Add 3/4 cup milk. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in one 2-1/2 oz jar shredded process Swiss cheese. Makes 1 cup.
TEX-MEX SAUCE: Cook one 8-oz can tomato sauce, one 4-oz can diced green chili peppers, 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander, a pinch of sugar, and 1/4 teaspoon bottled hot pepper sauce till heated through.
SWEET-SOUR SAUCE: Cook one 10-oz can pineapple tidbits, one 8-oz jar sweet-sour sauce, and half of a green or sweet red pepper (cut into strips) till heated through.

notes: Marked as FAST in cookbook
For a delicious dinner in a hurry, put frozen breaded fish portions or fish sticks in the oven and top with one of these easy sauces

recipes.title: Salmon-Pasta Skillet
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 177

ingredients.item: pitted ripe olives, cut into cubes

instructions.text: In a large skillet bring chicken broth to boiling. Add pasta. Cook, covered, 15 to 20 minutes or till pasta is tender, stirring frequently. Add broth and salmon. Cook, covered, about 3 more minutes. Stir in cheese, peas, and olives. Cook, covered, about 3 minutes more. Gently stir in salmon. Heat through. Sprinkle with lemon peel. Pass Parmesan cheese. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 177)

recipes.title: Macadamia Meltaways
recipes.description: Buttery cookies with macadamia nuts that melt in your mouth.

instructions.text: In blender at medium speed, blend 1 cup nuts until finely ground; place in large bowl. Reserve remaining nuts for tops.
Into bowl with ground nuts, measure remaining ingredients. Knead until blended and dough holds together. Preheat oven to 300°F.
With hands, shape scant tablespoonfuls of dough into balls. Place 1 inch apart on ungreased cookie sheets; press reserved nuts into tops.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until lightly browned. Remove to wire racks; cool.

notes: 96 cals per cookie
Begin 2 hrs or up to 1 wk ahead

recipes.title: Poppy-Seed Pinwheels
recipes.description: Elegant pinwheel cookies with a poppy seed filling.

instructions.text: In large bowl with mixer at high speed, beat sugar and butter until light and fluffy. Add flour, vanilla, salt, and egg; beat until well blended, occasionally scraping bowl with rubber spatula.
Shape into ball, wrap and refrigerate 1 hour, until firm enough to handle.
Meanwhile, stir remaining ingredients and 4 tablespoons butter until dough mixed.
On waxed paper, roll half of dough into an 8" rectangle; spread with half poppy-seed filling. Starting at narrow side, roll jelly-roll fashion; wrap and refrigerate 1 hour, until firm.
Repeat with remaining dough and filling.

Preheat oven to 375°F. Slice one 1/2 inch apart onto ungreased cookie sheets; place 1 inch apart on ungreased cookie sheets; bake 10 to 12 minutes, until lightly browned. Cool on wire rack; repeat with remaining roll.

notes: 65 cals per cookie
Begin early in day

recipes.title: Filbert Cookie Rafts
recipes.description: Delicate hazelnut cookies shaped like rafts with decorative lines.

instructions.text: In blender at medium speed, blend filberts and 2 tablespoons sugar until very finely ground.
Into medium bowl, measure remaining ingredients, 2 tablespoons sugar, and ground filberts. Knead until blended and dough holds together.
Preheat oven to 325°F. On waxed paper with floured rolling pin, roll out half dough into a 6" by 6" square. Cut into sixteen 1-1/2" by 1-1/2" squares.

With metal spatula, place on ungreased cookie sheet. With dull edge of knife, lightly mark each with three parallel lines. Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until lightly browned. Remove to wire racks; cool. Repeat with remaining dough.

notes: 53 cals per cookie
Begin 1-1/2 hrs or up to 2 wks ahead

recipes.title: Christmas Tree Cookies
recipes.description: Traditional holiday sugar cookies shaped like festive Christmas tree ornaments.

instructions.text: Into a large bowl, measure all-purpose flour, sugar, margarine, baking powder, salt, almond extract, and egg. With electric mixer at low speed, beat the ingredients until well blended, occasionally scraping the bowl with rubber spatula. Dough may be crumbly. With hands, gently knead the dough until the mixture holds together.
Reserve 1/2 cup dough; wrap in plastic wrap or aluminum foil and refrigerate. With hands, roll remaining dough into three 6-inch-long rolls.
Roll up each roll in sugar crystals to coat. Form each roll into triangle-shaped log by pressing to flatten bottom, then pinching sides together to form a point.
Wrap each log in plastic wrap and refrigerate 2 hours or until the dough is firm enough to slice (refrigerate up to 1 week).
Preheat oven to 350°F. Slice one log crosswise into 1/4-inch-thick slices; place slices, 1-inch apart, on large ungreased cookie sheet.
For each cookie, with fingers, shape 1/4 teaspoon reserved dough to resemble tree trunk; carefully attach to bottom of each slice.
Lightly sprinkle each cookie with some confetti decors. Bake the cookies 10 to 12 minutes until lightly browned.
With pancake turner or metal spatula, remove cookies to wire racks to cool. Repeat with remaining logs and confetti decors.

notes: 55 cals per cookie
Begin 3-1/2 hrs or up to 1 wk ahead
Use them as festive Christmas tree ornaments by making a small hole in the top of the cookie before baking; use ribbon to tie onto the branches

missing_inputs: Not in database: container confetti decors

recipes.title: Frosted Snowmen
recipes.description: Adorable snowman-shaped cookies with oats, decorated with frosting.

instructions.text: Into large bowl, measure first 7 ingredients. With mixer at low speed, beat until blended. With wooden spoon, stir in oats and walnuts.

Preheat oven to 375°F. With floured hands, shape mixture into thirty-six 1-inch balls and thirty-six 3/4-inch balls. Place 1-inch balls, 2 inches apart, on ungreased cookie sheets; place 3/4-inch balls 1/2 inch above 1-inch balls.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until golden. With metal spatula, remove to wire racks to cool.
Prepare frosting: In medium bowl with mixer at low speed, beat confectioners' sugar, cream of tartar, and egg whites until blended. Increase speed to high and beat 1 minute.
Dip front of each cookie into frosting to cover. Place frosted-side up, on wire racks; decorate quickly. Let frosting dry, about 1 hour.

notes: 135 cals per cookie
Begin 2-1/2 hrs or up to 1 wk ahead
Decorate with candies for eyes, nose, and buttons before frosting sets

recipes.title: Cookie Chalets
recipes.description: Tiny house-shaped spiced cookies decorated with almond roofs and red-hot cinnamon doors.

instructions.text: Into large bowl, measure all the ingredients except almonds and candies. With mixer at low speed, beat ingredients until well blended, occasionally scraping bowl with rubber spatula. Shape the dough into a ball, wrap with plastic wrap or foil and refrigerate 1 hour or until dough is firm enough to handle. (Or, place dough in freezer 30 minutes.)
Meanwhile, from cardboard, with scissors, cut a 2-1/2" by 1-1/2" house-shaped pattern.
On lightly floured surface with lightly floured rolling pin, gently roll out half of dough to 1/4-inch thick.
Using pattern, cut as many cookie houses as possible. With pancake turner, place cookies on ungreased cookie sheet, about 1/2 inch apart.
Press almonds along top of each cookie to resemble a roof.

Press cinnamon red-hot candies into each cookie to resemble a door. Bake cookies 5 to 6 minutes or until set (do not overbake or candies will melt). With pancake turner or metal spatula, remove cookies to wire racks to cool. Repeat with the remaining dough, trimmings, almonds, and candies. Store cookies in tightly-covered container to use up within 1 week.

notes: 125 cals per cookie
Begin 3 hrs before serving
These tiny houses are fun to decorate with almond roofs and red-hot cinnamon doors

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for sliced blanched almonds
Assumed 1 unit for cinnamon red-hot candies

recipes.title: Orange Rye Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 41
recipes.description: A variation of rye bread with orange peel and caraway.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Rye Bread, except increase brown sugar to 1/2 cup, omit the caraway seed, and add 4 teaspoons finely shredded orange peel to the flour mixture.

notes: Variation of Rye Bread

recipes.title: Molasses Rye Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 41
recipes.description: A darker rye bread using light molasses instead of brown sugar.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Rye Bread, except reduce water to 1-1/2 cups and substitute 1/2 cup light molasses for the brown sugar.

notes: Variation of Rye Bread

recipes.title: Peasant Rye Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 41
recipes.description: A hearty rye bread with whole bran cereal and yellow cornmeal.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Rye Bread, except reduce rye flour to 1 cup. Stir in 1/2 cup whole bran cereal and 1/2 cup yellow cornmeal with rye flour.

notes: Variation of Rye Bread

recipes.title: Raisin Sourdough Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 42
recipes.description: A sweeter variation of sourdough bread with raisins and cinnamon.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Sourdough Bread, except stir 1-1/2 cups raisins into yeast mixture along with the flour-soda mixture. Before baking, brush loaves with milk.
Combine 2 tablespoons sugar and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Sprinkle over loaves.

notes: Variation of Sourdough Bread

recipes.title: Cherry Filling
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 43
recipes.description: A tart cherry filling for coffee cakes.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen unsweetened pitted tart red cherries

instructions.text: Bring 1-1/2 cups fresh or frozen unsweetened pitted tart red cherries to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in 1 tablespoon lemon juice.
Combine 1/2 cup sugar and 2 tablespoons cornstarch; add to cherry mixture.
Cook and stir till bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Cool completely.

recipes.title: Cornmeal-Cheese Bubble Ring
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 45
recipes.description: A cheesy variation of the cornmeal bubble ring.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Cornmeal Bubble Ring, except add 1 cup shredded cheddar or American cheese to saucepan with milk mixture.

notes: Variation of Cornmeal Bubble Ring

recipes.title: Streusel Topping (for Chocolate Swirl Bread)
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 45
recipes.description: A crumb topping with chocolate and nuts for Chocolate Swirl Bread.

instructions.text: Stir together 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup sugar, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
Cut in 1/4 cup margarine or butter.
Stir in 1/4 cup chopped nuts and the remaining chocolate pieces.

recipes.title: Prune Kuchen
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 47
recipes.description: A variation of Kuchen using prune filling.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Kuchen, except omit apples, peaches, plums, or cottage cheese.
While dough is rising, make prune filling. In a saucepan combine 1-1/2 cups coarsely snipped pitted prunes and enough water to come 1 inch above prunes.
Bring to boiling. Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes; drain.
Spoon cooked prunes atop raised dough. Carefully spoon cream-sugar mixture over fruit.
*Note: If using apples, simmer the sliced fruit, covered, in water about 2 minutes or just till tender. Drain well; place atop dough.

notes: Variation of Kuchen

recipes.title: Whole Wheat English Muffins
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 48
recipes.description: English muffins made with whole wheat flour.

instructions.text: Prepare as for English Muffins, except substitute 1-1/4 cups whole wheat flour and 1/2 cup cracked wheat for 2 cups of the stirred-in all-purpose flour.

recipes.temperature: 325°F electric skillet or low heat griddle
notes: Variation of English Muffins

recipes.title: English-Muffin Loaves
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 48
recipes.description: A baked loaf version of English muffins - no kneading required.

ingredients.prep_note: reduced from base, do not knead

instructions.text: Prepare as for English Muffins, except reduce flour to 5 cups. Do not knead. Batter will be stiff.
Grease two 8x4x2-inch loaf pans. Sprinkle lightly with cornmeal.
Spoon batter into pans. Sprinkle tops lightly with cornmeal.
Cover; let rise till nearly double (about 45 minutes).
Bake in a 375° oven about 35 minutes or till done. Remove from pans immediately. Cool on wire racks.

notes: No-knead variation of English Muffins

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Pita Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 48
recipes.description: Pita bread made with whole wheat flour.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Pita Bread, except substitute 2 cups whole wheat flour for 2 cups of the stirred-in all-purpose flour.

notes: Variation of Pita Bread

recipes.title: Herb-Onion Dinner Rolls
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 50
recipes.description: Dinner rolls with dried herbs and minced onion.

ingredients.item: dried basil, oregano, or Italian seasoning

instructions.text: Prepare as for Dinner Rolls, except add 1 tablespoon dried minced onion and 1/2 teaspoon dried basil, oregano, or Italian seasoning, crushed, to milk mixture.

notes: Variation of Dinner Rolls

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Dinner Rolls
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 50
recipes.description: Dinner rolls made with whole wheat flour.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Dinner Rolls, except substitute 1-1/2 cups whole wheat flour for 1-1/2 cups of the stirred-in all-purpose flour.

notes: Variation of Dinner Rolls

recipes.title: Hamburger or Frankfurter Buns
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 50
recipes.description: Homemade hamburger or hot dog buns from dinner roll dough.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Dinner Rolls, except divide dough into 12 portions. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
For hamburger buns, shape each portion into an even circle, folding edges under. Press flat between your hands.
Place on a greased baking sheet. Press into a 4-inch circle.
For frankfurter buns, shape each portion into a roll about 5-1/2 inches long, tapering ends.
Place on a greased baking sheet. Let buns rise. Makes 12 buns.

notes: Variation of Dinner Rolls

recipes.title: Brown-and-Serve Dinner Rolls
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 50
recipes.description: Make-ahead rolls that are partially baked, then frozen for later browning.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Dinner Rolls, except bake in a 325° oven for 10 minutes; do not brown.
Remove rolls from baking sheets or pans; cool. Wrap in moisture- and vaporproof material. Seal, label, and freeze.
To serve, thaw frozen rolls in open packages at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes.
Unwrap completely. Place on ungreased baking sheets. Bake in a 375° oven about 10 minutes or till golden.

notes: Variation of Dinner Rolls - freezer friendly
Can be frozen and baked later

recipes.title: Batter Dinner Rolls
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 50
recipes.description: No-knead dinner rolls - reduced flour makes a softer batter that's spooned into muffin cups.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Dinner Rolls, except reduce stirred-in flour to 1-1/4 cups. (Use a total of 3-1/4 cups all-purpose flour.)
Spoon batter into greased muffin cups, filling half full. Cover and let rise in a warm place till nearly double (about 45 minutes).
Brush roll tops with milk, and, if desired, sprinkle with poppy seed or sesame seed.
Bake in a 375° oven for 15 to 18 minutes or till done. Makes 18 rolls.

notes: No-knead variation of Dinner Rolls

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 50)

recipes.title: Wheat and Cottage Cheese Rolls
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 50
recipes.description: Whole wheat rolls enriched with cottage cheese.

instructions.text: Drain cottage cheese, reserving liquid. Add milk to reserved liquid to measure 3/4 cup. Set aside.
Combine 1-1/2 cups flour and the yeast. Heat and stir cottage cheese, reserved milk mixture, brown sugar, margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt till warm (120° to 130°) and margarine almost melts.

Add to flour mixture along with eggs. Beat with an electric mixer on low speed for 30 seconds, scraping bowl constantly. Beat on high speed for 3 minutes. Using a spoon, stir in as much of the remaining flour as you can.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead in enough remaining flour to make a moderately stiff dough that is smooth and elastic (8 to 10 minutes total). Shape into a ball.
Place in a greased bowl; turn once. Cover; let rise in a warm place till double (30 to 45 minutes).
Punch dough down. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface. Cover; let rest 10 minutes.
Shape into 24 smooth balls. Place in greased muffin pans. Cover; let rise in a warm place till nearly double (about 20 minutes).
Bake in a 375° oven for 12 to 15 minutes or till done.

recipes.title: Light Rye Bagels
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 52
recipes.description: Bagels made with rye flour and optional caraway seed.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Bagels, except stir 1 teaspoon caraway seed, if desired, in with the yeast. Substitute 1-1/2 cups rye flour for 1-1/2 cups of the stirred-in all-purpose flour.

notes: Variation of Bagels

recipes.title: Herb Bagels
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 52
recipes.description: Bagels flavored with basil and dillweed or garlic powder.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Bagels, except stir 1-1/2 teaspoons dried basil, crushed; 1-1/2 teaspoons dried dillweed; or 1 to 1-1/2 teaspoons garlic powder in with the yeast.

notes: Variation of Bagels

recipes.title: Onion Bagels
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 52
recipes.description: Bagels with dried minced onion and optional bacon.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Bagels, except stir 2 tablespoons dried minced onion and, if desired, 2 tablespoons cooked bacon pieces into the flour with the yeast.

notes: Variation of Bagels

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Bagels
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 52
recipes.description: Bagels made with whole wheat flour and optional raisins.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Bagels, except substitute 1-1/2 cups whole wheat flour for 1-1/2 cups of the stirred-in all-purpose flour. Stir 3/4 cup raisins, if desired, in with whole wheat flour.

notes: Variation of Bagels

recipes.title: Caramel-Pecan Rolls
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 53
recipes.description: Sticky sweet rolls with caramel and pecan topping.

instructions.text: While dough is rising, combine 2/3 cup packed brown sugar, 1/4 cup margarine or butter, and 2 tablespoons light corn syrup. Cook and stir till combined.
Divide between two 9x1-1/2-inch round baking pans. Sprinkle each pan with 1/4 cup chopped pecans. Set the pans aside.
Roll half of the dough into a 12x8-inch rectangle. Melt 3 tablespoons margarine or butter; brush half of margarine over dough.
Combine 1/2 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon; sprinkle half of mixture over dough.
Roll up from one of the long sides. Seal seams. Slice dough into 12 pieces. Repeat with remaining dough, margarine, and sugar mixture.
Place rolls in pans. Cover; let rise till nearly double (about 30 minutes).
Bake in a 375° oven for 20 to 25 minutes. Invert onto a serving plate.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 53)

recipes.title: Cinnamon Rolls
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 53
recipes.description: Classic cinnamon rolls with optional raisins and powdered sugar icing.

instructions.text: Roll half of the dough into a 12x8-inch rectangle. Melt 3 tablespoons margarine or butter; brush half of margarine over dough.
Combine 1/2 cup sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon; sprinkle half of mixture over dough.
If desired, measure 3/4 cup raisins; sprinkle half of raisins over dough.
Roll up from one of the long sides. Seal seams. Slice dough into 12 pieces.
Repeat with remaining dough, margarine, sugar mixture, and raisins. Place rolls in two greased 9x1-1/2-inch round baking pans.
Cover; let rise till nearly double (about 30 minutes).
Bake in a 375° oven for 20 to 25 minutes. Cool slightly; remove from pans.
Drizzle with Powdered Sugar Icing (see recipe, page 88).

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 53)

recipes.title: Filled Croissants
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 54
recipes.description: Croissants filled with cream cheese, orange peel, or chocolate.

ingredients.item: semisweet chocolate pieces or fruit preservers

instructions.text: Prepare as for Croissants, except cut each 16x8-inch rectangle into four 8x4-inch rectangles.
Combine one 8-ounce package cream cheese, softened, 1/4 cup sugar, and 2 teaspoons finely shredded orange peel.
Fill center of each rectangle with 1 tablespoon cream cheese mixture. (Or, fill center of each rectangle with 1 tablespoon semisweet chocolate pieces or fruit preserves.)
Brush edges with egg mixture. Fold short sides in over filling to overlap in center (you'll have approximately 3-1/2x4-inch bundles).
Pinch edges to seal. Place on ungreased baking sheets, seam side down.

notes: Variation of Croissants

recipes.title: Cheese Nut Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 57
recipes.description: Nut bread with cheese and herbs.

ingredients.item: shredded Swiss cheese or shredded cheddar cheese

instructions.text: Prepare as for Nut Bread, except reduce sugar to 3/4 cup, and add 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano, crushed, or dried basil, crushed, to the flour mixture.
Add 1 cup shredded Swiss cheese or shredded cheddar cheese (4 ounces) to batter with the nuts.

notes: Variation of Nut Bread

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 57)

recipes.title: Cranberry Nut Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 57
recipes.description: Nut bread with cranberries and orange peel.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Nut Bread, except add 2 teaspoons finely shredded orange peel to the flour mixture.
Add 1 cup coarsely chopped cranberries to batter with the nuts.

notes: Variation of Nut Bread

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 57)

recipes.title: Apricot Nut Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 57
recipes.description: Nut bread with dried apricots and citrus peel.

ingredients.item: finely shredded orange peel or finely shredded lemon peel

instructions.text: Prepare as for Nut Bread, except add 2 teaspoons finely shredded orange peel or finely shredded lemon peel to the flour mixture.
Place 1 cup snipped dried apricots in a small bowl; pour boiling water over apricots. Let stand 5 minutes; drain well.
Stir apricots into batter with the nuts.

notes: Variation of Nut Bread
Rehydrate dried apricots before adding

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 57)

recipes.title: Blueberry-Banana-Walnut Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 58
recipes.description: Variation using whole blueberries instead of mashed berries.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Berry-Banana-Walnut Bread, except omit strawberries or raspberries and stir in 1 cup fresh or frozen whole blueberries with the nuts.

notes: Variation of Berry-Banana-Walnut Bread

recipes.title: Blueberry Muffins
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 60
recipes.description: Muffins with fresh or frozen blueberries.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Muffins, except fold 3/4 cup fresh or frozen blueberries and, if desired, 1 teaspoon finely shredded lemon peel into muffin batter.

notes: Variation of Muffins

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 60)

recipes.title: Cranberry Muffins
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 60
recipes.description: Muffins with cranberries and extra sugar.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Muffins, except combine 1 cup coarsely chopped cranberries and 2 tablespoons additional sugar. Fold into muffin batter.

notes: Variation of Muffins

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 60)

recipes.title: Rhubarb-Strawberry Coffee Cake
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 62
recipes.description: A spring coffee cake variation using rhubarb and strawberries.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Any-Fruit Coffee Cake, except substitute 3/4 cup fresh or frozen cut-up rhubarb and 3/4 cup frozen unsweetened whole strawberries for the fruit.
*Note: Do not simmer raspberries.

notes: Variation of Any-Fruit Coffee Cake
Do not simmer raspberries

recipes.title: Buttermilk Biscuits
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 66
recipes.description: Biscuits made with buttermilk and baking soda.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Biscuits, except stir 1/4 teaspoon baking soda into flour mixture and substitute 3/4 cup buttermilk for the milk.

notes: Variation of Biscuits

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 66)

recipes.title: Apple-Raisin Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 72
recipes.description: A warm apple sauce to serve with Puffed Oven Pancake.

instructions.text: In a skillet combine 2 large cooking apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced; 3/4 cup apple juice or water; 1/3 cup raisins; 2 tablespoons sugar; and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
Simmer, covered, till apples are just tender.
Stir together 2 tablespoons cornstarch and 2 tablespoons cold water. Add to apple mixture.
Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more.
Stir in 1 teaspoon margarine or butter. Keep warm.

recipes.title: Apricot Upside-Down Cake
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 76
recipes.description: Upside-down cake variation with apricots or peaches and coconut.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Pineapple Upside-Down Cake, except substitute one 8-1/2-ounce can apricot halves, drained and halved, or peach slices, drained, and 2 tablespoons toasted coconut for the pineapple and cherries.

notes: Variation of Pineapple Upside-Down Cake

recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 77
recipes.description: A spiced variation of Busy-Day Cake with pecans, walnuts, or peanuts.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Busy-Day Cake, except add 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg or allspice with the flour.
Stir in 1/2 cup chopped pecans, walnuts, or peanuts after beating.

recipes.title: Wheat and Raisin Busy-Day Cake
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 77

Sprinkle 1/4 cup raisins or snipped pitted whole dates atop batter in the baking pan.

notes: Variation of Busy-Day Cake

recipes.title: Citrus Yellow Cake
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 77
recipes.description: Yellow cake with orange or lemon peel, filled with Lemon Filling.

ingredients.item: finely shredded orange peel or finely shredded lemon peel

instructions.text: Prepare as for Yellow Cake, except add 2 teaspoons finely shredded orange peel or 1 teaspoon finely shredded lemon peel to the flour mixture.
Fill with Lemon Filling (see recipe, page 90) and frost with Lemon or Orange Butter Frosting (see recipe, page 89), if desired.

notes: Variation of Yellow Cake
