recipes.title: Carrot Cake
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 79
recipes.description: To match the picture on page 73, frost with Cream Cheese Frosting (see recipe, page 88) and top with walnut halves and strips of orange peel.

instructions.text: In a bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and cinnamon.
Add carrot, oil, and eggs. Beat with an electric mixer till combined.
Pour into 2 greased and floured 9x1-1/2-inch round baking pans.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or till a toothpick inserted near the centers comes out clean.
Cool on wire racks for 10 minutes. Remove cakes from pans. Cool thoroughly on racks.

notes: Frost with Cream Cheese Frosting (page 88)

recipes.title: Gingerbread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 80
recipes.description: A moist, spiced cake with molasses flavor.

instructions.text: In a bowl combine flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, ginger, baking powder, and baking soda.
Add shortening, molasses, egg, and 1/2 cup water. Beat with an electric mixer on low to medium speed till combined. Beat on high speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into a greased and floured 8x8x2-inch baking pan.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 to 40 minutes or till a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool on a rack 10 minutes. Remove from pan; serve warm.

notes: Microwave directions available

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Pound Cake
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 83
recipes.description: Pound cake originally was made with a pound each of butter, sugar, eggs, and flour. We cut the recipe but kept the rich flavor.

instructions.text: Bring butter and eggs to room temperature. In a mixing bowl stir together flour, baking powder, and, if desired, nutmeg.
In another bowl beat butter with an electric mixer on medium speed for 30 seconds.
Gradually add sugar to butter, 2 tablespoons at a time, beating on medium to high speed about 6 minutes total or till very light and fluffy. Add vanilla.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating 1 minute after each addition, scraping bowl often.
Gradually add flour mixture to butter mixture, beating on low to medium speed just till combined.
Pour batter into a greased and floured 9x5x3-inch loaf pan.
Bake in a 325° oven for 55 to 65 minutes or till a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Remove cake from pan. Cool thoroughly on a wire rack. Drizzle Powdered Sugar Icing over cake, if desired.

notes: Bring butter and eggs to room temperature before starting

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 83)

recipes.title: Pumpkin Cake Roll
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 86
recipes.description: A spiced pumpkin cake rolled with cream cheese frosting.

instructions.text: Prepare as for Jelly Roll, except add 2 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice to flour mixture and stir 1/2 cup canned pumpkin into egg yolk and sugar mixture.
Fill with Cream Cheese Frosting (see recipe, page 88). Roll up cake.
Sprinkle with sifted powdered sugar.
*Note: For another filling, try 2 cups softened ice cream. Freeze ice-cream-filled roll.

notes: Variation of Jelly Roll
Can fill with ice cream and freeze

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 86)

recipes.title: Fruitcake
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 87
recipes.description: A traditional fruitcake with candied fruits, nuts, and molasses. Store in refrigerator for 2 to 8 weeks to mellow flavors.

ingredients.item: diced mixed candied fruits and peels, or snipped mixed dried fruit
candied red or green cherries, quartered
chopped pecans, walnuts, or toasted slivered almonds

instructions.text: Grease an 8x4x2-inch loaf pan. Line bottom and sides of pan with brown paper to prevent overbrowning; grease paper.
In a bowl combine flour, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, nutmeg, allspice, and cloves. Add fruits and peels, raisins, cherries, and nuts; mix well.
Beat eggs; stir in sugar, juice, margarine, and molasses till combined. Stir into fruit mixture.

Pour batter into pan. Bake in a 300° oven for 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 hours or till a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean. (Cover pan loosely with foil after 1 hour of baking to prevent overbrowning.)
Cool in pan on rack. Remove from pan. Wrap cake in brandy- or fruit-juice-moistened cheesecloth. Overwrap with foil.
Store in the refrigerator for 2 to 8 weeks to mellow flavors. Remoisten cheesecloth about once a week, or as needed.

notes: Store in refrigerator 2-8 weeks to mellow flavors
Remoisten cheesecloth weekly

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for brandy or fruit juice

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 109

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl beat the shortening and margarine or butter with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds. Add about half of the flour, the brown sugar, sugar, eggs, vanilla, and baking soda. Beat till thoroughly combined. Beat in the remaining flour. Stir in chocolate pieces and, if desired, nuts.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoons 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake in a 375° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or till edges are lightly browned. Cool cookies on a wire rack. Makes about 60.

notes: Chocolate-Candy Cookies: Prepare as above, except substitute candy-coated milk chocolate pieces for the semisweet chocolate pieces.

Giant Chocolate Chip Cookies: Prepare as above, except drop dough from a 1/4-cup measure or scoop about 4 inches apart onto cookie sheet. Bake for 11 to 13 minutes or till edges are lightly browned. Makes about 20.

Macadamia Nut and White Chocolate Chunk Cookies: Prepare as above, except substitute chopped white baking bars (or pieces) with cocoa butter or vanilla-flavored confectioners' coating for the semisweet chocolate pieces. Stir in one 3 1/2-ounce jar macadamia nuts, chopped, with the white chocolate.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Drop Cookies
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 110
recipes.description: For a peek at the Chocolate-Peanut and Spiced Raisin drop cookies, turn to page 101.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl beat shortening and margarine or butter with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds. Add about half of the flour, the sugar, brown sugar, egg, vanilla, and baking soda. Beat till thoroughly combined. Beat in remaining flour.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoons 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake in a 375° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or till edges are golden. Cool cookies on a wire rack. Makes about 24.

notes: Chocolate-Peanut Drop Cookies: Prepare as above, except add 1/3 cup unsweetened cocoa powder and 3 tablespoons milk with the sugar. After beating in all the flour, stir in 1/2 cup chopped peanuts. Makes about 30.

Pineapple-Coconut Drop Cookies: Prepare as above, except add 1/2 cup well-drained crushed pineapple and 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger with the sugar. After beating in all the flour, stir in 1 cup coconut. Makes about 30.

Spiced Raisin Drop Cookies: Prepare as above, except add 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg with the sugar. After beating in all the flour, stir in 1 cup raisins or mixed dried fruit bits. Makes about 30.
Coconut-Pecan Drop Cookies: Prepare as above, except, after beating in all the flour, stir in 1 cup coconut and 1 cup chopped pecans. Makes about 36.
Gumdrop Drop Cookies: Prepare as above, except, after beating in all the flour, stir in 1 cup snipped gumdrops. Makes about 30.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Oatmeal Cookies
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 110

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl beat margarine or butter with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds. Add about half of the flour, the brown sugar, sugar, egg, baking powder, vanilla, and baking soda. If desired, stir in cinnamon and cloves. Beat till thoroughly combined. Beat in remaining flour. Stir in oats.
Drop by rounded teaspoons 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake in a 375° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or till edges are golden. Cool cookies on a wire rack. Makes about 48.

notes: Fruit-Topped Oatmeal Cookies: Prepare as above, except, for topping, in a medium saucepan combine 1 1/2 cups finely chopped peeled apples, pears, or peaches; 1/2 cup sugar; 1/3 cup raisins; 1/3 cup chopped pecans; and 2 tablespoons water. Bring to boiling, stirring constantly. Reduce heat. Simmer till fruit is tender and most of the liquid has evaporated, stirring occasionally. After dropping dough onto cookie sheet, press centers with your thumb. Fill each indentation with a level teaspoon of topping.
Raisin Oatmeal Cookies: Prepare as above, except, after stirring in oats, stir in 1 cup raisins or currants. Makes about 54.

Choose-a-Chip Oatmeal Cookies: Prepare as above, except, after stirring in oats, stir in 1 cup semisweet chocolate, butterscotch-flavored, or peanut-butter-flavored pieces and 1/2 cup chopped walnuts or pecans. Makes about 54.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Shortbread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 120
recipes.description: Our taste panel felt butter, not margarine, was the only choice for these rich, scrumptious cookies.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine flour and sugar. Cut in butter till mixture resembles fine crumbs and starts to cling. Form the mixture into a ball and knead till smooth.

To make wedges, on an ungreased cookie sheet pat or roll the dough into an 8-inch circle. Using your fingers, press to make a scalloped edge. With a knife, cut circle into 16 pie-shape wedges. Leave wedges in the circle shape. Bake in a 325° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or till bottom just starts to brown and center is set. Cut circle into wedges again while warm. Cool on the cookie sheet for 5 minutes. Remove from cookie sheet; cool on a wire rack. Makes 16.

notes: Spiced Shortbread: Prepare as above, except substitute brown sugar for the sugar and stir 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger, and 1/8 teaspoon ground cloves into the flour-sugar mixture.
Lemon and Poppy Seed Shortbread: Prepare as above, except stir 1 tablespoon poppy seed into flour-sugar mixture and add 1 teaspoon finely shredded lemon peel with the butter.

Butter-Pecan Shortbread: Prepare as above, except substitute brown sugar for the sugar. After cutting in butter, stir 2 tablespoons finely chopped pecans into the flour mixture. Sprinkle mixture with 1/2 teaspoon vanilla.
Oatmeal Shortbread: Prepare as above, except reduce all-purpose flour to 1 cup. After cutting in butter, stir 1/3 cup quick-cooking rolled oats into the flour mixture.

Note: For strips or rounds, on a lightly floured surface, pat or roll dough 1/2 inch thick. Using a knife, cut into twenty-four 2x1-inch strips; or, using a 1 1/2-inch-round cookie cutter, cut into 24 rounds. Place 1 inch apart on an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake in a 325° oven 20 to 25 minutes or till bottoms just start to brown. Cool cookies on a wire rack.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Applesauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 124

ingredients.item: cooking apples (9 medium), peeled, quartered, and cored

instructions.text: In a Dutch oven combine apples and water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes or till tender, adding more water, if necessary.
Remove from heat. Mash with a potato masher or process in a blender or food processor to desired texture. Serve warm or chilled. Stir before serving. Makes about 4 1/2 cups (8 servings).

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Baked Apples
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 124

ingredients.item: raisins, snipped pitted whole dates, or mixed dried fruit bits

instructions.text: Core apples; peel a strip from the top of each. Place apples in a 2-quart casserole. Combine the raisins, brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Spoon into centers of apples. Add apple juice to dish. Bake in a 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes or till apples are tender, basting occasionally with the cooking liquid. Serve warm with ice cream, light cream, or yogurt, if desired. Serves 4.

Microwave directions: Reduce apple juice or water to 2 tablespoons. Assemble as above. Micro-cook, covered, on 100% power (high) for 4 to 8 minutes or till tender, rearranging and basting apples after 3 minutes.

Pop the popcorn. Place in lightly greased sink or large bowl. Combine sugar, butter (or margarine), cream of tartar, and syrup in saucepan. Bring to boil and cook 5 minutes. Remove from heat, add soda. Pour and mix quickly over popcorn.

Place immediately the popcorn mixture into lightly greased pan(s) or onto lightly greased cookie sheet(s). Set in prewarmed oven at 200° for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes. Store in airtight container.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

instructions.text: Melt chips separately. Add 1 can of noodles to each bowl of chips. Mix carefully. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto wax paper. Refrigerate.

assumptions: Assumed 1.5 cup can for dry Chinese noodles
Estimated 6 servings based on total calories

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°. Wash and core apples - Red Delicious. Remove a 1 inch strip from around the top of each apple. Cut the bottoms of the apple so that they will stand up straight in a pan. Mix cinnamon with brown sugar. Fill each apple with 1 teaspoon butter and 1 or 2 tablespoons of sugar mixture. Place apples in baking dish and pour 1 cup of water into the dish around the base of the apples.
Bake for 45 to 60 minutes; cool before serving. Serves 6.
Cook in double boiler for 1 hour. Stir often.

assumptions: Used standard can size (1.5 cups) for Pet milk (evaporated milk)
Estimated 8 servings based on total calories

ingredients.item: garlic powder or grated garlic toes

ingredients.prep_note: use less if using soy sauce

instructions.text: Place all ingredients in a small saucepan. Stir over gentle heat until mixed. Heat only until hot, letting the sauce boil will cause the oil in the peanut butter to separate. A little more water may be added for desired consistency. Serve over Sate, grilled meats, and or rice.

assumptions: Inferred 0.25 for hot pepper paste or Tabasco (standard quantity)
Estimated 4 servings based on total calories

instructions.text: Mix sugar and milk in saucepan and boil for 2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in rest of the ingredients. Beat well with a greased, wooden spoon. Quickly pour into ungreased 9x13 inch pan.

recipes.title: Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 160
recipes.description: For homemade flavor in a hurry, try the Shortcut Macaroni and Cheese.

instructions.text: Cook macaroni according to package directions (or see chart, page 278); drain well.

Meanwhile, for cheese sauce, in a saucepan cook onion in margarine or butter till tender but not brown. Stir in flour and pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till slightly thickened and bubbly. Add shredded cheese; stir till melted.

Stir macaroni into cheese sauce. Transfer to a 1-quart casserole. Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or till bubbly. During the last 5 minutes of baking, arrange tomato slices atop macaroni, if desired. Let stand 10 minutes. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Vegetable Macaroni and Cheese: Prepare as above, except stir 2 cups frozen mixed vegetables, thawed, or one 16-ounce can mixed vegetables, drained, into cheese sauce with macaroni. Transfer to a 1 1/2-quart casserole.

Shortcut Macaroni and Cheese: Prepare as above, except immediately return the drained macaroni to the saucepan it was cooked in. Pour the cheese sauce over the macaroni; mix well. Cook over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes or till heated through, stirring frequently. Let stand for 10 minutes.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Dijon-Mustard Fillets
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 168

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish. Place fish on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from the heat till fish flakes easily with a fork. (Allow 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness. Turn once if more than 1 inch thick.)
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan stir together sour cream, milk, mustard, chives, and a dash pepper. Cook till hot (do not boil). Serve over fish. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 168)

recipes.title: Orange Swordfish Kabobs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 168

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen swordfish steaks, cut 1 inch thick
ingredients.prep_note: tuna or shark makes great kabobs because of their firm, steak-like texture

ingredients.item: large green onions, cut into 2-inch lengths
finely shredded orange or cherry tomatoes

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut fish into 1-inch cubes. Place fish, mushrooms, and onions in a plastic bag; set bag in a bowl. Combine oil, wine or orange juice, garlic, orange peel. Seal bag and marinate at room temperature for 2 hours, turning bag occasionally. Drain fish cubes, mushrooms, and onions, reserving marinade.
On eight 12-inch skewers alternately thread fish cubes, mushrooms, and onions, leaving about 1/4 inch between pieces. Place on the greased unheated rack of a broiler pan.
Broil 4 inches from the heat for 4 to 5 minutes. Turn kabobs over. Broil for 4 to 6 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork. To serve, add a tomato to each skewer. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 168)

recipes.title: Hot Tuna Sandwich Cups
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 175

ingredients.item: can tuna, drained and flaked (water pack)

instructions.text: Separate biscuits. Grease the outside of six 6-ounce custard cups. Press one biscuit over bottom and halfway down side of each custard cup, forming a biscuit cup. Place cups, biscuit side up, on a 15x10x1-inch baking pan. Bake in a 400° oven 7 minutes or till lightly browned. Remove biscuits from cups. Place upright in baking pan.

Meanwhile, in saucepan cook celery and onion in margarine till tender. Stir in mayonnaise, mustard, tuna, half of cheese, and the peas. Spoon tuna mixture immediately; remove biscuit from pan. Top with tomato slices and remaining cheese. Bake 2 to 3 minutes more or till cheese melts. Serves 6.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 175)

recipes.title: Crab Cakes
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 179

ingredients.item: crabmeat, cooked, or two 6-ounce cans crabmeat, drained, flaked, and cartilage removed

instructions.text: In a medium bowl combine egg, mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Stir in crab. Add half of the crumbs (about 3 minutes). Add half of margarine and heat about 3 minutes. Add half of the crab mixture to skillet. Press into four 3-inch patties.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes on each side or till golden. Remove; keep warm. Repeat with remaining margarine, oil, and crab mixture. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 179)

recipes.title: Crab Mornay
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 179
recipes.description: Topped with a classic cheese sauce.

ingredients.item: sliced fresh mushrooms, onion, and celery
crabmeat, cooked, or two 6-ounce cans crabmeat, drained, flaked, and cartilage removed

instructions.text: In a saucepan cook mushrooms, onion, and celery in margarine till tender. Add red pepper. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in crabmeat and wine. Cook and stir 1 minute more.

Stir in crabmeat, chopped egg, pimiento, to and mustard. Spoon into four 10-ounce casseroles or coquille shells. Top with bread crumbs with the 1 tablespoon margarine; sprinkle over casseroles. Top with almonds. Bake in a 375° oven about 20 minutes or till tops brown. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 179)

recipes.title: Deviled Crab
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 179

ingredients.item: crabmeat, cooked, or two 6 1/2-ounce cans crabmeat, drained, flaked, and cartilage removed

instructions.text: In a saucepan melt the 2 tablespoons margarine. Stir in flour. Add milk and hot pepper sauce all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in crabmeat, chopped egg, pimiento, cheese, and mustard. Spoon into four 10-ounce casseroles or coquille shells. Toss bread crumbs with the 1 tablespoon margarine; sprinkle over casseroles. Top with almonds. Bake in 375° oven about 20 minutes or till tops brown. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 179)

recipes.title: Shrimp Creole
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 180
recipes.description: This spicy New Orleans classic is the perfect match for rice.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen peeled and deveined shrimp

instructions.text: Thaw shrimp, if frozen. In a large skillet cook onion, celery, green pepper, and garlic in margarine or butter till tender. Stir in undrained tomatoes, tomato paste, bay leaf, sugar, paprika, red pepper, and salt. Bring to boiling.
Stir together water and cornstarch. Stir into tomato mixture. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly.
Add shrimp to the tomato mixture. Stir cook, covered, for 1 to 3 minutes or till shrimp turn pink. Remove bay leaf. Serve over rice. Serves 4.

notes: Fish Creole: Prepare as above, except substitute 12 ounces fresh or frozen fish fillets for shrimp. Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut fillets into 1-inch pieces. Add fish to the tomato mixture. Cook and stir till the fish is thickened and bubbly. Cook and after 3 to 5 minutes, covered, on high for 1 to 2 minutes or till shrimp turn pink. Remove bay leaf. Serve over rice.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 180)

recipes.title: Shrimp Chow Mein
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 180

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen peeled and deveined shrimp
hot cooked rice or chow mein noodles

instructions.text: Thaw shrimp, if frozen. Cut any large shrimp in half lengthwise. For sauce, combine water, soy sauce, cornstarch, bouillon granules, and ginger. Set aside.

Preheat a wok or large skillet over high heat; add cooking oil. (Add more oil as necessary during cooking.) Stir-fry mushrooms, onion, and garlic for 1 minute. Remove. Stir-fry shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes or till shrimp turn pink. Push to side of wok or skillet.

Stir sauce; add to center of wok. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Add water chestnuts, bean sprouts, pea pods, and cooked vegetables. Heat ingredients together to coat with sauce. Heat through. Serve over hot cooked rice. Serves 4.

notes: Scallop Chow Mein: Prepare as above, except substitute 12 ounces fresh or frozen scallops for the shrimp. Thaw scallops, if frozen. Cut any large scallops into bite-size pieces. Stir-fry scallops for 2 to 3 minutes or till they turn opaque.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 180)

recipes.title: Shrimp in Garlic Butter
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 181

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen peeled and deveined shrimp

instructions.text: Thaw shrimp, if frozen. In a large skillet heat margarine or butter over medium-high heat. Add shrimp and garlic. Cook, stirring, for 2 to 4 minutes or till shrimp turn pink. Sprinkle with parsley.
Above except for substitute 12 ounces fresh or frozen sea scallops for the shrimp. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Scallops in Garlic Butter: Prepare as above, except substitute 12 ounces fresh or frozen scallops for the shrimp. Cut any large scallops in half. If frozen, thaw scallops. Stir-fry scallops for 3 to 5 minutes or till they turn opaque.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 181)

recipes.title: French-Fried Shrimp
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 181
recipes.description: Putting the shrimp dry before dipping them into the batter gives a crisper coating.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen shrimp in shells
shortening or cooking oil for deep-fat frying

instructions.text: Thaw shrimp, if frozen. Peel shrimp, leaving the last few sections before the tails and the tails intact. To devein shrimp, use a sharp knife to make a shallow slit along the back of each shrimp. Remove the sandy black vein, if present.

To butterfly shrimp, make a deeper slit along the back of shrimp, cutting almost all the way through the shrimp on a flat surface so that the sides open to resemble a butterfly. Rinse; pat dry with paper towels. Set aside.
For batter, combine flour, cornmeal, sugar, and salt. Combine egg, water, and the 2 tablespoons oil. Add to flour mixture. Beat with a rotary beater till smooth.

In a large deep saucepan or deep-fat fryer, heat 2 inches shortening or oil to 375°. Meanwhile, pat shrimp dry. Dip shrimp into batter. Fry shrimp, 5 or 6 at a time, in hot fat for 2 to 3 minutes or till golden. Remove from fat. Drain on paper towels. Keep warm in a 300° oven while frying remainder. Serve with Cocktail Sauce, if desired. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 181)

recipes.title: Linguine with White Clam Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 182
recipes.description: The nutty rich taste of this alternative recipe is well worth the effort required.

instructions.text: Cook linguine according to package directions. Meanwhile, drain clams, reserving liquid from clams. Add enough of the cream or milk to make 1 cup liquid. Set aside.
In a saucepan cook onion and garlic in margarine till tender. Stir in flour, oregano, salt, and pepper. Add the 1 cup liquid. Cook and stir for 1 minute more.
Stir in clams, parsley and wine. Heat through. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Linguine with Red Clam Sauce: Prepare as above, except stir one 15-ounce can tomato sauce and 1/4 cup dry red wine into cooked onion and garlic. Heat through. Serve sauce over linguine. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 182)

recipes.title: Coquilles Saint-Jacques
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 182

instructions.text: Thaw scallops, if frozen. Halve any large scallops. In a large skillet, cook mushrooms and onion in the 1/4 cup margarine till tender. Stir in flour and pepper. Add cream. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly.
In egg yolk; stir about half of the hot mixture into yolk. Return all to skillet. Add scallops. Cook and stir for 1 to 2 minutes or till scallops turn opaque.

Spoon scallop mixture into 4 coquille shells or au gratin dishes or four 10-ounce custard cups. Place together bread crumbs, melted margarine, and parsley; sprinkle over scallops or mixture. Bake in a 400° oven for 7 to 9 minutes or till crumbs are brown. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 182)

recipes.title: Crawfish Étouffée
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 183

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen peeled crawfish tails or deveined shrimp

instructions.text: Thaw crawfish tails or shrimp, if frozen. In a large skillet cook onion, celery, green pepper, and garlic in crawfish fat, margarine, or butter for 10 minutes or till tender. Add tomato sauce, red pepper, 1 cup water, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook and stir till bubbly.
Add crawfish tails or shrimp. Return to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 4 to 5 minutes or till crawfish are tender (shrimp turn pink). Season to taste. Serve with rice. Serves 4.

recipes.title: Oysters au Gratin
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 183

instructions.text: Pat oysters dry. In a large skillet cook 4 oysters in 1 tablespoon of the margarine for 3 to 4 minutes or till edges curl. Transfer oysters to four 10-ounce casseroles. Drain.

For sauce, in the same skillet cook mushrooms and garlic in the 2 tablespoons margarine till tender. Stir in flour. Add milk and wine all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in parsley, Worcestershire sauce. Spoon over oysters.
Mix crumbs, Parmesan, and melted margarine. Sprinkle over sauce. Bake in 400° oven for 10 minutes or till crumbs are brown. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 183)

recipes.title: Creole Stuffed Roast
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 228

instructions.text: For stuffing, in a mixing bowl combine onion, green pepper, garlic, celery seed, black pepper, and red pepper. Set aside. Cut tied pork roast and separate. Trim fat. Cut slits along the flat side of one half of roast.

Fill slits with some of the stuffing. Place meat, cut side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Insert a meat thermometer. Roast in a 325° oven for 1 1/4 to 1 3/4 hours. Cover and let stand 15 minutes before carving.

recipes.title: Rice-Stuffed Rib Crown Roast
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 228
recipes.description: Sides of ribs form an impressive roast.

ingredients.item: pork rib back ribs (16 to 20 ribs)

instructions.text: To form roast, tie 2 or 3 slabs of ribs together, rib side out and double-bone end up, forming a circle about 5 inches in diameter with crown leaving the inside shallow roasting pan. Rub the inside of the crown. If desired, sprinkle meat thermometer in a 450° oven for 20 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350°. Brush roast.

Meanwhile, for stuffing, in a saucepan combine water, rice, carrot, corn syrup, salt, and the 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover; simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Spoon stuffing into crown of roast, transfer meat to a serving platter. Using a fork to steady, cut between the ribs. Make 6 to 8 servings.

notes: Fruit-Stuffed Rib Crown Roast: Prepare as above, except instead of rice stuffing, add one 6-ounce package dried fruit bits and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon with the rice.

missing_inputs: Not in database: dried Italian seasoning

recipes.title: Harvest Pot Roast
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 229

ingredients.item: medium acorn squash, peeled and sliced

instructions.text: Trim fat from meat. If desired, sprinkle meat with salt and pepper. In Dutch oven brown meat on all sides in hot oil. Drain fat. Add onion, bouillon, bay leaf, 1 1/4 cups water, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, covered, for 25 to 30 minutes.

Add squash. Cook until meat is done, about 1 hour. Cut squash in half; remove seeds. Cut each half into 4 pieces. Add squash and potatoes to Dutch oven. Simmer 25 to 30 minutes more till vegetables are done.

Transfer meat and vegetables to platter; keep warm. Discard bay leaf. Skim fat from drippings. Measure 1 1/2 cups liquid; return to pan. For gravy, stir 1/4 cup cold water into flour. Stir into pan juices. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly; cook 1 minute more. Serve with meat and vegetables. Makes 4 servings.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Roast Pork with Mushroom-Butter Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 229

ingredients.item: boneless pork roast, rolled and tied

instructions.text: For stuffing, combine mushrooms, onions, and green onions. In a skillet cook mushrooms, salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper in margarine till liquid evaporates. Remove from heat. Stir in wine, parsley, lemon juice, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.

Trim fat from roast. Make 8 pockets, about 1/4 inch deep, in meat. Spoon stuffing into pockets. Place roast, rib side down, in a shallow roasting pan. Insert meat thermometer. Roast in a 325° oven for 2 to 3 hours or till thermometer registers 170°. Cover; let stand 15 minutes before carving. Serve with Mushroom-Butter Sauce.

recipes.title: Pork with Apple-Nutmeg Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 230
recipes.description: Drizzle this tasty cider sauce over meat.

ingredients.item: boneless pork loin center rib roast

instructions.text: Trim fat from meat. If desired, sprinkle meat with salt and pepper. Place rib side down, in a shallow roasting pan. Insert a meat thermometer. Roast in a 325° oven for 1 1/4 to 1 3/4 hours or till thermometer registers 170° (well-done). Cover and let stand 15 minutes before carving.

For sauce, in a saucepan cook onion and garlic in margarine till tender. Stir in corn, apple, bouillon granules, nutmeg, and pepper. Add apple cider and stir 1 minute. Cook and stir more. Serve sauce over meat. Serves 8 to 10.

recipes.title: Citrus-Glazed Ribs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 230

instructions.text: Cut ribs into serving-size pieces. Place ribs, bone side down, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan.

Roast in a 350° oven for 1 hour. Drain. Meanwhile, for orange combine soy sauce, 2 tablespoons marmalade, lemon juice, and 3/4 teaspoon ground ginger. Roast 30 to 45 minutes more or till well-done. Brush occasionally with glaze. Brush with any remaining glaze before serving. Makes 4 servings.

recipes.title: Barbecue-Style Ribs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 230

instructions.text: Place ribs, bone side down, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Bake in a 350° oven for 1 hour. Drain.

Meanwhile, for sauce, in a small saucepan cook onion and garlic in hot oil till tender. Stir in tomato sauce, mustard, brown sugar, lemon juice, 1/4 cup water, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Simmer, uncovered, for 15 to 20 minutes or till slightly thickened. Stir in ribs. Bake ribs, covered, for 30 to 60 minutes more or till well-done, brushing occasionally with sauce. Pass remaining sauce with ribs. Serves 4.

recipes.title: Braised Steaks Italian
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 230

ingredients.item: pork shoulder blade steaks, cut 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick (2 to 2 1/2 pounds)

instructions.text: Trim fat from meat. In a large skillet brown 2 steaks on each side. Remove steaks from skillet; cook for 2 steaks and remove. Add onion to oil remaining in skillet for 2 minutes. Drain. Add pizza sauce. Return steaks to skillet.

Cover; simmer for low heat about 30 minutes or till no pink remains. Remove steaks. Skim fat from pan juices. If necessary, continue cooking juices to thicken slightly. Spoon over meat. Serve with remaining glaze. Serves 4 to 6.

missing_inputs: Not in database: can pizza sauce

recipes.title: Corn-Stuffed Pork Chops
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook, page 231
recipes.description: Savory stuffed pork chops stuffed with a buttery corn and vegetable filling.

ingredients.item: pork loin rib chops or pork loin butterfly chops, cut 1 1/4 inches thick (about 2 pounds)
corn-bread stuffing mix or herb-seasoned stuffing mix

instructions.text: Trim fat from chops. Cut a pocket in each chop by cutting from fat side almost to the bone to make a pocket for the stuffing.

For the stuffing, cook vegetables in margarine till tender but not brown, stirring occasionally. In a small saucepan cook onion and green pepper in margarine till tender. Spoon stuffing into pockets with each pork chop. Secure pockets with wooden toothpicks. Place chops on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Cover with foil.
Bake in a 375° oven for 40 to 45 minutes. Uncover; continue cooking for 10 to 15 minutes more or till pork is no pink remains. Remove picks. Makes 4 servings.

recipes.title: Penuche
recipes.description: This brown sugar fudge is pictured on page 91.

instructions.text: Line an 8x4x2- or a 9x5x3-inch loaf pan with foil; extend foil over edges. Butter foil; set aside. Butter the sides of a heavy 2-quart saucepan. Combine sugars, cream, and milk. Cook and stir over medium-high heat to boiling. Clip candy thermometer to side of pan. Cook and stir over medium-low heat to 236°, soft-ball stage (15 to 20 minutes).

Remove from heat. Add margarine and vanilla, but do not stir. Cool, without stirring, to 110°, lukewarm (about 50 minutes). Remove thermometer. Beat mixture vigorously till penuche just begins to thicken; add nuts. Continue beating till penuche becomes very thick and just starts to lose its gloss (about 10 minutes total). Spread into pan. Score into squares. Cut when firm. Makes about 1 1/4 pounds (32 servings).

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Rocky Road
recipes.description: Marshmallows and chopped nuts are the rocks in this delicious chocolate road.

instructions.text: Line an 8x8x2-inch baking pan with foil, extending foil over edges of pan. Butter foil; set aside. In a medium saucepan slowly melt chocolate over low heat, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Stir in marshmallows and nuts. Spread into prepared pan. Chill till firm (at least 1 hour). Use foil to lift candy out of pan; cut into squares. Store in the refrigerator. Makes about 36 pieces.

Microwave directions: Line pan and butter foil as above. In a medium bowl micro-cook chocolate, uncovered, on 100% power (high) for 1 1/2 to 2 1/4 minutes or till chocolate becomes smooth when stirred. Stir in marshmallows and nuts. Spread into prepared pan. Chill till firm. Lift candy from pan and cut into squares. Store in the refrigerator.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

instructions.text: Beat margarine with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds. Add 1/4 cup of the sugar. Beat till combined. Beat in the 1 cup flour till crumbly. Press into the bottom of an ungreased 8x8x2-inch baking pan. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 to 18 minutes or just till golden.
Meanwhile, combine eggs, the remaining sugar, the 2 tablespoons flour, lemon peel, lemon juice, and baking powder. Beat for 2 minutes or till thoroughly combined. Pour over hot baked layer.
Bake in a 350° oven about 20 minutes more or till lightly browned around the edges and center is set. Cool on a wire rack. If desired, sift powdered sugar over top. Cut into bars. Makes 20.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Lobster Newburg
recipes.description: The rich Madeira-flavored sauce enhances the delicate taste of lobster.

ingredients.prep_note: 5-ounce cans, drained, and broken into bite-size pieces

instructions.text: In a saucepan melt margarine or butter. Stir in flour, salt, and red pepper. Add cream all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Stir about half of the hot mixture into the beaten egg yolks; return all to saucepan.

Cook and stir over low heat about 2 minutes or till mixture just begins to thicken and bubble slightly. Stir in Madeira or dry sherry. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Add lobster; heat through. Serve in patty shells, if desired, or over toast points. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Crab Newburg: Prepare as above, except substitute 2 cups cooked crabmeat for the lobster. Garnish with parsley sprigs.
Shrimp Newburg: Prepare as above, except substitute two 6-ounce packages frozen, peeled, cooked shrimp, thawed and drained, for the lobster.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 184)

recipes.title: Boiled Lobster

instructions.text: In a 12-quart Dutch oven bring 8 quarts water and 1 1/2 to 2 teaspoons salt to boiling. Use two 1- to 1 1/2-pound live lobsters. Grasp each lobster just behind the eyes; rinse lobsters under cold running water.
Quickly plunge lobsters headfirst into the boiling water. Return to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Drain lobsters.
Remove the green tomalley (liver). Set aside and serve with the lobster meat, if desired.

notes: Using kitchen shears, halve the body lengthwise up to the tail.
Cut and Remove the black vein running through the tail and the small sac near the head. (Found only in female lobsters.)

Remove the green tomalley (liver) and, if present, the roe. Mash the tomalley and roe. Make a Clarified Butter: Melt 1/2 cup butter over very low heat without stirring; cool slightly. Pour off clear top layer. Discard milky bottom layer.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 184)

recipes.title: Catsup
recipes.description: The fresh tomato flavor comes through in this classic condiment.

instructions.text: Wash, core, and quarter tomatoes. Drain in a colander; discard liquid. Place tomatoes in an 8- or 10-quart kettle or Dutch oven. Add onions in an 8- or 10-quart kettle or Dutch oven. Bring to boiling; cook 15 minutes, stirring often.

(Measure about 7 cups.) Return puree to kettle; add sugar. Bring to boiling. Clip candy thermometer to pan. Cook and stir to 220° (about 30 minutes or to desired consistency). Strain vinegar mixture into tomatoes; discard spices. Add salt. Simmer about 30 minutes more or till of desired consistency, stirring often.
May refrigerate up to 1 month. Makes 4 half-pints.

Boiling-Water Canning Directions: Ladle hot catsup into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving a 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 15 minutes (start timing when water returns to boiling).

recipes.title: Bread Pudding
recipes.description: To dry bread cubes, bake them in a 300° oven about 15 minutes. Or, cut toasted bread slices into 1-inch cubes.

ingredients.item: raisins or other snipped dried fruit

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl beat together eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla. Place dry bread cubes in an 8x1 1/2-inch round baking dish. Sprinkle raisins or dried fruit over bread. Pour egg mixture over all.
Bake in a 325° oven for 35 to 40 minutes or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Cool slightly. Serve warm with Whiskey Sauce, if desired. Makes 6 servings.

notes: Coconut Bread Pudding: Prepare as above, except sprinkle 1/4 cup coconut over the raisins or dried fruit.

recipes.title: Vanilla Ice Cream

instructions.text: In a large saucepan combine sugar and gelatin. Stir in light cream. Cook and stir over medium heat till mixture almost boils and sugar dissolves. Stir about 1 cup of the hot mixture into beaten eggs; return all to saucepan. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Do not boil. Stir in whipping cream and vanilla. Cool. Freeze in a 4- or 5-quart ice-cream freezer according to manufacturer's directions. Makes about 3 quarts (24 servings).

notes: Chocolate Ice Cream: Prepare as above, except stir 6 squares (6 ounces) unsweetened chocolate, melted and cooled, into gelatin mixture after heating. Beat with a rotary beater till combined. Stir 1 cup chopped toasted almonds into the cooled mixture, if desired.

recipes.title: Hot Fudge Sauce

instructions.text: In a heavy small saucepan melt chocolate pieces and margarine or butter. Add the sugar; gradually stir in milk. Bring to boiling, reduce heat. Boil gently over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring frequently. Remove from heat. Serve warm over ice cream. Makes about 1 1/2 cups (8 servings).

notes: Peanut-Butter Fudge Sauce: Prepare as above, except, after cooking 8 minutes, stir in 1/4 cup peanut butter. Then remove from heat.

assumptions: Used standard can size (1.5 cups) for evaporated milk

ingredients.item: beef tenderloin steak or sirloin steak
sliced fresh mushrooms or button mushrooms

instructions.text: Partially freeze beef. Thinly slice across the grain into bite-size strips. Toss beef strips with flour and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Set aside.

In a large skillet cook mushrooms, onion, and garlic in margarine over high heat till tender. Add 1/4 cup of the broth. Stir to scrape up any drippings. Cook till thickened, stirring constantly. Remove from skillet.

Add more margarine to skillet if necessary. Add meat; cook and stir over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes or till done. Return all meat to skillet. Add remaining broth; cook and stir till thickened. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Stir in sour cream. Heat through but do not boil. Serve over hot cooked noodles. Serves 4.

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for hot cooked noodles

instructions.text: Partially freeze beef. Thinly slice across the grain into long soy sauce strips 1/4 inch thick. For marinade, combine ginger, root, garlic, sherry, molasses, mustard ginger, bine soy sauce, sherry, applesauce or molasses. Pour over meat. Marinate for 15 minutes to 1 cup water temperature. Or, 8 hours. Drain meat, reserving marinade according to style.
Place skewers on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from the heat 5 to 6 minutes or to desired doneness, turning and brushing occasionally with marinade. Makes 4 servings.
Grill directions: Cut, marinate, and skewer meat as above. Place on uncovered grill directly over hot coals 5 to 6 minutes uncovered or to desired doneness. Turn and brush with marinade often.
Thaw pea pods. Partially freeze beef. Thinly slice across the grain into thin strips. For sauce, combine sherry, soy sauce, cornstarch. Set aside.

Preheat a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add oil. Cook and stir carrots and garlic in hot oil for 2 minutes. Add broccoli, pea pods, vegetables, and bamboo shoots. Cook and stir 1 minute or till hot. Remove from center of wok. Return all beef to the wok. Stir fry for 2 to 3 minutes more. Add 1/2 cup of the beef to the center. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Pour over chops; sprinkle with cooked rice. Serves 4.

assumptions: Assumed 1.5 cup can for bamboo shoots, drained

instructions.text: For stuffing, in a small skillet cook celery and onion in margarine or butter till tender. Stir in garlic. In a medium bowl combine the spinach, rosemary; stir in the cooked onion. Add the egg. Stir in just enough of the bread crumbs to make mixture stick together.

Remove fat from meat. Starting light and flat proceed to end. Spread stuffing over meat. With boned side up, roll up and tie. Place roast, seam side down, on a rack in a 325° oven for 1 3/4 to 2 hours for medium (170°); 2 1/4 to 2 1/2 hours for well-done (180°). Let stand 15 minutes before carving. Makes 12 to 15 servings.
Cut small slits in top of lamb; insert garlic slivers. Combine lemon juice, parsley, mint or basil, onion salt, rosemary, and pepper. Rub over lamb.

Place lamb, fat side up, on rack in shallow roasting pan. Insert meat thermometer. Roast in a 325° oven till meat thermometer registers 140° for rare (1 3/4 to 2 1/4 hours), 155° for medium (2 1/4 to 2 3/4 hours), or 170° for well-done (2 3/4 to 3 1/4 hours). If desired, garnish with fresh marjoram. Makes 12 servings.

recipes.title: Currant-Glazed Rack of Lamb
recipes.description: The rib from one 1 1/2- to 2-pound lamb rib roast fits in two dry cups with currant jelly and 1/2 cup wine or apple juice and 1 teaspoon dried, crushed tarragon. Cook the glaze till thickened. Brush with glaze.

instructions.text: Place lamb rib roasts, bone side down, in a shallow roasting pan. Roast in a 325° oven, 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours for medium rare (150°) or 1 3/4 to 2 hours for medium (160°).

Meanwhile, for glaze, in a small saucepan combine currant jelly, wine or apple juice, and tarragon. Heat and stir till smooth. During last 30 minutes of roasting, brush lamb frequently with glaze. Pass remaining glaze. Makes 4 servings.

ingredients.item: medium apples, peeled, cored, and sliced

instructions.text: In a large saucepan brown half of the meat in hot oil. Remove meat. Brown remaining meat with onion, curry powder, and garlic till onion is tender. Return all meat to pan. Stir in apples, cold water into flour. Stir into saucepan. Cook and stir till thickened. Cover; simmer for 30 minutes or until meat is tender. Stir in 3/4 cup water. Return all meat to saucepan; add apples. Cover; simmer 3 to 5 minutes more. Serve over hot cooked rice.

Microwave directions: Omit cooking oil. In a 2-quart casserole micro-cook lamb, onion, curry powder (high) 5 and 1/2 minutes or till tender, stirring twice, 5 minutes, Cook, covered, on 50% power (medium) 15 minutes or till tender. Stir in apples, covered, on 100% power (high) for 3 to 5 minutes till thickened and bubbly. Cook 5 minutes. Stir in casserole every 30 seconds. Continue as above.

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for hot cooked rice

ingredients.prep_note: (4) or beef short ribs (10 to 12) into 1-rib portions

instructions.text: Cut 3 1/2 to 4 pounds lamb shanks into short ribs or ribs in 2 tablespoons hot cooking oil; drain fat.

Combine brown sugar, onion, carrot, celery, wine, tomato sauce, garlic, pepper, and bay leaf. Pour over shanks or ribs. Cover; simmer for 1 1/2 to 1 3/4 hours or till tender. Skim fat from sauce. Remove bay leaf. Skim fat sauce, boil pan juices rapidly for 6 to 8 minutes (You should have about 3 cups.) Discard bay leaf. Serve sauce over shanks and hot cooked noodles. Cook 30 seconds more. Continue as above.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

ingredients.item: frozen Italian-style green beans or frozen green beans
medium onion, sliced and separated into rings

instructions.text: Run cold water over beans to separate; set aside and trim fat from meat over high heat in large skillet. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. In a large skillet cook chops and onion in hot oil. Drain fat.

Combine beans, and bouillon granules, pepper. Pour over chops. Add water to bouillon; stir in remaining vegetables. Return meat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once or till tender. Remove meat; for sauce, skin fat from vegetables. Serves 4.

assumptions: Used standard can size (0.75 cups) for sliced pitted ripe olives

recipes.title: Dill Pickles

ingredients.item: fresh dill heads or dried dillseed

instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse cucumbers. Remove stems and cut off a thin slice from blossom end. Cut into spears or slice. Pack into hot, sterilized pint jars. In a saucepan combine water, vinegar, and salt. Bring to boiling.
Pour hot liquid over cucumbers, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 15 minutes. Makes about 8 pints.

notes: Kosher-Style Dill Pickles: Prepare as above except substitute 2 cloves garlic, halved, for 1/2 teaspoon mustard seed or 2 to 3 tablespoons.

recipes.title: Bread 'n' Butter Pickles

instructions.text: In a large bowl combine cucumbers, onions, salt, and large kettle. Stir in a thin well. Remove garlic. In a large kettle combine vinegar, sugar, and dried mixture and celery seed. Add drained mix. Bring to boiling, stirring occasionally. Pack into hot sterilized pint jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process 10 minutes. Makes 8 pints (80 servings).

notes: Horseradish Pickles: Prepare as above, except add 1/2 cup prepared horseradish to the sugar mixture.

ingredients.item: medium head cauliflower, broken into flowerets

instructions.text: Cut cucumbers into 3/4-inch chunks or 1/2-inch slices. Pack cucumbers or other vegetables into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Mix pickling salt and water and bring to a boil. Ladle hot brine over cucumbers, remaining in a boiling-water canner for 15 minutes. Makes 5 pints (50 servings).

Cut corn from cobs (do not scrape cobs). Measure 4 cups. In an 8- or 10-quart Dutch oven combine corn and 1 cup water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, covered, about 12 minutes or till nearly tender.

Add celery, red and green peppers, and onion. Stir in 2 cups vinegar, sugar, pickling salt, and celery seed. Return to boiling. Stir together remaining vinegar, flour, dry mustard, and turmeric. Add to corn mixture. Cook and stir 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir together remaining corn and all flour mixture to boiling; stir occasionally. Ladle into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 15 minutes. Makes 7 pints (224 one-tablespoon servings).

ingredients.item: medium firm ripe tomatoes, peeled, cored
large sweet red peppers, seeded, stems and seeds removed, cut up

instructions.text: Using coarse blade of a food grinder, grind tomatoes. Drain in a colander to drain in a large bowl. Place ground vegetables mixture in a clean, large bowl. Sprinkle with salt. Let stand overnight. Drain well.

Rinse well. Let stand overnight. Drain well. In an 8- or 10-quart kettle or Dutch oven combine sugar, water, thyme, and pepper. Bring to boiling, stirring to dissolve sugar. Stir in ground vegetable mixture. Return mixture to boiling. Remove from heat. Makes about 8 pints.

ingredients.item: unsweetened apple, grape, or cranberry juice cocktail, or low-calorie cranberry juice

instructions.text: Pour fruit juice into a 6- to 8-quart kettle. Bring to full rolling boil; stir in pectin. Add sugar. Return to full rolling boil, stirring constantly. Boil hard for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Quickly skim off foam with a metal spoon. Ladle into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process 5 minutes. Makes 6 half-pints.

recipes.title: Peach Jam

instructions.text: Peel, pit, and coarsely grind or mash peaches. Measure 4 cups. In an 8- or 10-quart kettle combine peaches, pectin, and lemon juice. Stir in sugar. Bring to a full rolling boil, stirring constantly. Boil hard for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Quickly skim off foam with a metal spoon. Ladle into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process 5 minutes. Makes 7 half-pints.

notes: Peach-Plum Jam: Prepare as above, except reduce peaches to 1 1/2 pounds (2 cups ground). Add 1 pound fully ripe Italian prune plums, pitted and finely chopped (2 cups), with pectin.
Peach-Berry Jam: Prepare as above, except add 2 cups strawberries, blackberries, or raspberries, crushed (1 cup), with pectin.

instructions.text: Score orange and lemon peel into 4 lengthwise sections. Remove peels; discard from fruits. Scrape off white portions of white pith from peel. Combine peel strips. Bring to boiling; Reduce heat. Cover and cook 20 minutes. Do not drain.

Remove membranes from fruits. Section fruits and chop; combine 3 cups juice and simmer for 10 minutes. Return to boiling. Measure 3 cups mixture and sugar. Bring to a full rolling boil. Quickly stir in pectin. Return to a full boil; stir, uncovered, 1 minute. Remove from heat. Skim off foam. Ladle at once into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in boiling-water canner for 15 minutes. (May take 2 weeks to set.) Makes about 6 half-pints (96 one-tablespoon servings).

recipes.title: Grape Jam
recipes.description: One gallon of grapes should make about 10 cups.

instructions.text: Wash and stem grapes. Measure 10 cups. Remove skins from half of the grapes by squeezing the skinned grapes. Combine the skinned grapes and remaining grapes. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes and stir about 10 minutes or until very soft. Sieve about 2 cups water and cooked grapes. Return to kettle.

Stir in sugar. Bring to a full rolling boil, stirring constantly. Boil and stir for 12 minutes or till jam sheets off a metal spoon. Remove from heat. Quickly skim off foam. Ladle jam at once into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving a 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 5 minutes. Makes 6 half-pints (96 one-tablespoon servings).

In a large Dutch oven combine rhubarb and raspberries. Bring to boiling. Let stand for 20 minutes or till sugar is dissolved, stirring frequently. Boil hard for 10 minutes. Let stand 20 minutes. Bring to boiling; boil, uncovered, for 5 to 6 minutes or till thick, stirring frequently. Remove from heat. Add gelatin; stir till dissolved. Ladle into hot half-pint jars or freezer containers, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Seal, label, and freeze or 1 year in the freezer. Makes about 5 half-pints.

ingredients.item: blackberries, raspberries, or strawberries, caps removed

instructions.text: Crush berries. Measure 2 cups blackberries or raspberries, 1 3/4 cups strawberries. In a bowl combine berries, sugar, and lemon peel. Let stand 10 minutes.

Combine pectin and lemon juice. Add to berry mixture; stir for 3 minutes. Ladle at once into jars or freezer containers, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace. Seal. Let stand at room temperature about 2 hours or till jam is set. Store up to 3 weeks in the refrigerator or 1 year in the freezer. Makes 4 half-pints (sixty-four 1-tablespoon servings).

In an 8- or 10-quart kettle combine apples, water, and, if desired, cinnamon. Bring to a boil, reduce heat. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Press through a food mill or sieve (you should have about 13 cups pulp).
Return pulp to kettle. Stir in sugar, cinnamon. Simmer, uncovered, about 2 hours or till very thick, stirring often. Makes about 8 half-pints (128 one-tablespoon servings).
Boiling-Water Canning: Spoon hot apple butter into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving a 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in boiling-water canner for 5 minutes.

Freezing: Spoon hot apple butter into a sink of ice water to cool apple butter. Place kettle in a sink of ice water to cool apple butter. Spoon into freezer containers, leaving the recommended headspace (see tip, page 193). Seal, label, and freeze.

recipes.title: Apple Butter
recipes.description: Freeze or can this spicy spread.

instructions.text: In an 8- or 10-quart kettle combine apples and cider. Bring to a boil; reduce heat. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Press through a food mill or sieve (you should have about 13 cups pulp).

Return pulp to kettle. Stir in sugar, cinnamon, and allspice. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or till very thick, stirring often. Spoon into hot, sterilized jars or freezer containers for quart or pint jars, leaving a 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in boiling-water canner for 5 minutes. (For pints, process for 5 minutes.) Makes 5 half-pints (see tip, page 193). Seal, label, and freeze.

recipes.title: Spaetzle
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 263
recipes.description: Serve spaetzle (SHPETS-luh) with sauces or in soups as you would noodles. Or serve it with sauerbraten, the traditional German way.

instructions.text: In a large saucepan or Dutch oven bring about 3 quarts lightly salted water to boiling.
Meanwhile, for spaetzle batter, in a bowl stir together flour and salt. In another bowl stir together egg and milk. Stir egg mixture into the flour mixture.
Set a colander with large holes (at least 3/16-inch diameter) on a large piece of waxed paper.

Pour the spaetzle batter into the colander. Immediately hold the colander over the pan of boiling water; press the batter through the colander with a wooden spoon to form the spaetzle. Cook about 5 minutes or till done, stirring occasionally. Drain well.
Melt margarine or butter; toss with bread crumbs. Sprinkle crumb mixture over the hot spaetzle.

notes: Whole Wheat Spaetzle: Prepare as above, except reduce all-purpose flour to 1/2 cup and add 1/2 cup whole wheat flour.
Pesto Spaetzle: Prepare as above, except omit margarine and crumbs. Toss hot cooked spaetzle with 1 portion (about 1/4 cup) Pesto for Pasta (see recipe, page 269).

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 263)

recipes.title: Homemade Pasta
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 266
recipes.description: In recipes that call for packaged pasta, substitute half of this recipe for each 4 ounces of the packaged product.

instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl stir together 2 cups of the flour and the salt. Make a well in the center of the mixture. In a bowl combine eggs, water, and oil. Add to flour mixture; mix well.
Sprinkle kneading surface with the remaining flour. Turn dough out onto floured surface. Knead till dough is smooth and elastic (8 to 10 minutes). Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Divide dough into fourths. On a lightly floured surface, roll each fourth into a 12x12-inch square (about 1/16 inch thick). Let stand 20 minutes. Cut as desired.
Or, if using a pasta machine, pass dough through machine according to manufacturer's directions till 1/16 inch thick. Cut as desired.
Cook pasta (see chart, page 278), allowing a few more minutes for dried or frozen pasta. Drain well.

To store: After cutting and shaping the pasta, hang it from a pasta drying rack or clothes hanger, or spread it on a wire cooling rack. Let dry overnight or till completely dry. Place in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Or, dry the pasta for at least 1 hour. Seal it in a freezer bag or freezer container. Freeze for up to 8 months.

notes: Whole Wheat Pasta: Prepare as above, except substitute whole wheat flour for the all-purpose flour.

Spinach Pasta: Prepare as above, except increase all-purpose flour to 2 3/4 cups, reduce water to 1/4 cup, and add 1/4 cup very finely chopped cooked spinach, well drained, to the egg mixture. Makes 1 1/4 pounds fresh pasta (10 servings).
Herb Pasta: Prepare as above, except add 1 teaspoon dried basil, marjoram, or sage, crushed, to flour mixture.

Egg Noodles: Prepare as above, except substitute 1 egg plus 2 egg yolks for the 2 eggs. Reduce flour to 1 3/4 cups in flour mixture and 1/4 cup for kneading. Cut dough into 1/4-inch-wide strips, then cut into 2- to 3-inch lengths.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 266)

recipes.title: Herb-Buttered Pasta
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 267
recipes.description: Simple herb-tossed pasta that makes a delicious side dish.

ingredients.item: dried basil, oregano, thyme, or marjoram, crushed; dried dillweed; or caraway seed

instructions.text: Cook pasta (see chart, page 278). Drain well.
Return to hot saucepan. Add margarine and desired herb. Toss gently till pasta is well coated.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Serves 4.

notes: Lemon-Chive Pasta: Prepare as above, except omit herb and add 1/4 cup snipped chives and 1 teaspoon finely shredded lemon peel with margarine or butter.
Nutty Cheese Pasta: Prepare as above, except omit herb and add 1/2 cup chopped walnuts, pecans, or almonds and 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan or Romano cheese with margarine.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 267)

recipes.title: Pasta Primavera
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 268
recipes.description: A colorful vegetable pasta dish with a light cream sauce.

instructions.text: Cook pasta (see chart, page 278). Drain well.

Meanwhile, in a large skillet melt 2 tablespoons of the margarine. Cook and stir broccoli, onion, and garlic in butter over medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Stir in wine. Cook and stir over medium-high heat about 2 minutes more or till broccoli is crisp-tender.
Stir in pea pods and thyme. Cook and stir 1 minute. Transfer to a serving plate. Sprinkle with cheese.

notes: Ham Pasta Primavera: Prepare as above, except stir 1 cup fully cooked cubed ham or turkey ham into vegetable mixture with the pea pods. Sprinkle with more Parmesan if desired. Makes 8 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 268)

recipes.title: Fettuccine with Marinara Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 268
recipes.description: Classic fettuccine with a rich tomato marinara sauce.

instructions.text: For marinara sauce, in a medium saucepan cook onion and garlic in oil till tender but not brown. Stir in undrained tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, sugar, and salt.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, about 30 minutes or till desired consistency.
Meanwhile, cook pasta (see chart, page 278). Drain well. Serve with marinara sauce. Serves 8.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 268)

recipes.title: Pasta with Carbonara Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 268
recipes.description: Bits of bacon highlight the cheesy, creamy sauce.

instructions.text: Let egg, cream, and margarine or butter stand at room temperature for 1 hour. Cook bacon on paper towels till crisp. Drain well. Return pasta to saucepan and place over low heat.

Meanwhile, cook pasta (see chart, page 278). Drain well. Return pasta to saucepan and place over low heat. Toss margarine with pasta. Beat together egg and cream; pour over hot pasta. Toss gently till pasta is well coated. Add bacon, cheese, and parsley; toss to mix. Season with coarsely ground pepper. Transfer to a warm serving dish. Serves 3 or 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 268)

recipes.title: Pesto for Pasta
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 269
recipes.description: Fresh basil pesto sauce perfect for tossing with hot pasta.

instructions.text: In a blender container or food processor bowl combine basil, Parmesan or Romano cheese, nuts, oil, and garlic. Cover and blend or process till the mixture is nearly smooth, stopping machine occasionally to scrape down sides.

Divide pesto into 4 portions. Serve 1 portion at a time over 4 ounces hot cooked pasta. (For remaining pesto, place each portion in an airtight container and chill for 1 to 2 days. Or, freeze for up to 1 month.)

notes: Spinach Pesto for Pasta: Prepare as above, except use 1/2 cup torn fresh spinach and 1/2 cup firmly packed fresh basil leaves instead of 1 cup basil.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 269)

recipes.title: Couscous and Tomatoes
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 269
recipes.description: Try quick-cooking rice in place of the couscous.

instructions.text: In a saucepan combine undrained stewed tomatoes, onion, pepper, garlic powder. Bring to boiling. Stir in couscous; remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes. Stir in olives and parsley. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 269)

recipes.title: Fettuccine Alfredo
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 270
recipes.description: Classic creamy Alfredo sauce tossed with fettuccine.

instructions.text: Let cream come to room temperature. Drain pasta well. Return to hot saucepan. Add cream, margarine or butter. Toss gently till pasta is well coated.
Add Parmesan cheese; toss to combine. Transfer to a warm serving dish. Sprinkle with pepper and nutmeg. Serve immediately. Makes 8 servings.

notes: Fettuccine Alfredo with Mushrooms: Prepare as above, except cook 1 1/2 cups sliced fresh mushrooms and 1 clove garlic, minced, in the margarine or butter till tender. Add to drained pasta with cream and Parmesan cheese.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 270)

recipes.title: Potluck Pasta
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 270
recipes.description: Transform this side dish into a main dish just by adding tuna, ham, or chicken or turkey.

ingredients.item: large macaroni shells, rotini, or elbow macaroni
cream of chicken or cream of mushroom soup

instructions.text: In a large saucepan cook pasta (see chart, page 278); adding frozen vegetable and onion the last 6 minutes. Drain in a colander.

In the same saucepan stir together condensed soup, sour cream, cheddar cheese, milk, carrot, oregano or basil, and pepper. Cook and stir over medium heat till bubbly and cheddar cheese is melted. Add pasta mixture; toss to coat. Transfer to a 2-quart casserole.
Bake, covered, in a 350° oven about 55 minutes or till heated through.

To make ahead: Prepare as above, except transfer mixture to a 2-quart casserole. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Cover and chill for 3 to 24 hours. To serve, bake, covered, in a 350° oven about 55 minutes or till heated through.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 270)

recipes.title: Rice Mold
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 272
recipes.description: Plain or perked up, rice shaped into a mold turns an ordinary meal into special dinner.

ingredients.item: long grain rice or brown rice

instructions.text: In a saucepan combine water or broth, rice, and salt. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes for long grain rice (35 minutes for brown rice) or till rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Press hot rice into a buttered 3-cup mold or bowl. Unmold at once. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Parsley Rice Mold: Stir 1/4 cup snipped parsley into cooked rice.
Confetti Rice Mold: Stir in 1/2 cup frozen mixed vegetables and 1/4 teaspoon dried dillweed with the uncooked rice.
Peppery Rice Mold: Stir in one 4-ounce can diced green chili peppers, drained, and 1/8 teaspoon ground red pepper with the uncooked rice.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 272)

recipes.title: Risotto
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 272
recipes.description: Parmesan flavors this creamy rice dish.

instructions.text: In a medium saucepan cook mushrooms, rice, and green pepper in margarine till green pepper is tender. Remove from heat.
Stir in broth, water, sherry, sage, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes or till tender.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 272)

recipes.title: Spanish Rice
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 272
recipes.description: Classic tomato-flavored rice with peppers and onion.

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook onion, green pepper, and garlic in oil till tender but not brown.

Stir in undrained tomatoes, rice, sugar, chili powder, 1/8 teaspoon pepper, several dashes hot pepper sauce, and 1 cup water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes or till rice is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed. Sprinkle with shredded cheddar cheese, if desired.

notes: Mexican Rice: Omit onion, green pepper, garlic, and cooking oil. Substitute stewed tomatoes for canned tomatoes. Stir in one 4-ounce can diced green chili peppers, drained, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 272)

recipes.title: Rice Pilaf
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 273
recipes.description: Add a nutty flavor to the rice by browning it lightly in margarine or butter before beginning the recipe.

ingredients.item: instant chicken or beef bouillon granules

instructions.text: In a saucepan cook onion, mushrooms, celery or green pepper, and garlic in margarine till tender but not brown.

Stir in rice, bouillon granules, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, and 1 1/2 cups water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes or till rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Stir in crumbled bacon.

notes: Curried Rice Pilaf: Omit mushrooms and add 1/4 to 1 teaspoon curry powder with onion. Stir in 1/2 cup raisins with rice.
Brown and Wild Rice Pilaf: Substitute 1/2 cup brown rice and 1/4 cup wild rice for the long grain rice. Cook rice mixture about 40 minutes.
Bulgur Pilaf: Substitute bulgur for the long grain rice.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 273)

recipes.title: Fried Rice
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 273
recipes.description: Asian-style fried rice with ham and vegetables.

instructions.text: In a large skillet heat 2 tablespoons of the oil over medium heat. Add eggs and cook without stirring till set. Loosen eggs and invert skillet over cutting board; cut into short, narrow strips.
In the skillet heat the remaining oil over medium heat. Cook ham, mushrooms, onion, and ginger in the hot oil for 3 minutes.
Stir in cooked rice, cabbage, and egg strips; sprinkle with soy sauce. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes or till heated through, tossing gently to coat with soy sauce.

notes: Vegetable Fried Rice: Omit ham and stir in 1/4 cup frozen peas, thawed, into the skillet with the rice.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 273)

recipes.title: Granola
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 274
recipes.description: Choose your favorite nuts and fruits to make this crispy snack or cereal.

instructions.text: In a bowl stir together rolled oats, coconut, almonds or peanuts, sunflower nuts, and sesame seed. In another bowl combine honey or syrup and oil; stir into oat mixture. Spread evenly into a greased 15x10x1-inch baking pan.
Bake in a 300° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or till lightly browned, stirring after 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven and immediately turn out onto a large piece of foil. Cool, then break into clumps. Store in tightly covered jars or plastic bags at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

notes: Apple-Cinnamon Granola: Reduce rolled oats to 1 1/2 cups. Stir 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon into honey-oil mixture. Just before serving, stir in 1 cup coarsely chopped dried apple.
Raisin-Date Granola: After removing granola from the oven, stir in 1/3 cup raisins and 1/2 cup snipped pitted whole dates.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 274)

recipes.title: Grits
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 274
recipes.description: Southern-style grits, perfect for breakfast or as a side dish.

instructions.text: In a saucepan bring 2 cups water or chicken broth and 1/4 teaspoon salt to boiling. Slowly add 1/2 cup quick-cooking grits, stirring constantly.
Cook and stir till boiling. Reduce heat; cook and stir for 5 to 6 minutes or till water is absorbed and mixture is thick. Serve with margarine, butter, or milk, if desired.

notes: Cheesy Grits: Omit salt. Stir 1 cup shredded American or cheddar cheese and 1 tablespoon margarine or butter into hot grits till melted. Gradually stir about 1/2 cup of the hot grits into 1 beaten egg. Return all to the saucepan and stir to combine. Pour into a greased 1-quart casserole. Bake in a 325° oven about 25 minutes or till nearly set. Let stand 5 minutes. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 274)

recipes.title: Baked Gnocchi
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 275
recipes.description: Baking makes the Parmesan-flavored gnocchi (NYAH-kee) extra crisp.

instructions.text: In a medium saucepan heat milk and margarine to boiling. Mix 1/3 cup milk, the farina, and salt. Slowly add farina mixture to boiling milk, stirring constantly. Cook and stir 3 to 4 minutes or till thick.

Remove from heat; stir about 1/3 cup of the hot mixture into egg. Return all to the saucepan; stir in the 1/3 cup Parmesan cheese. Pour into a well-buttered 10x6x2-inch baking dish. Chill about 1 hour or till firm.

Turn out of baking dish onto a cutting board. Cut into 3x1-inch rectangles. Sprinkle tops with the 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese. Place on a well-greased baking sheet. Bake in a 425° oven about 25 minutes or till golden.

notes: Spinach Gnocchi: Reduce milk to 1 1/4 cups. Cook one 10-ounce package frozen chopped spinach. Drain well. Stir spinach into hot farina mixture.
Boiled Gnocchi: Do not pour into baking dish. Cool slightly. Shape mixture into compact balls. Drop into gently boiling water. Cook about 4 minutes.
Herb-Garlic Gnocchi: Omit salt and stir in 1 teaspoon dried basil, oregano, or marjoram, crushed, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic salt with the farina.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 275)

recipes.title: Choose-a-Grain Casserole
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 275
recipes.description: Great with baked chicken or fish.

ingredients.item: chopped green or sweet red pepper
cooked rice, bulgur, wheat berries, or barley

instructions.text: In a small saucepan cook pepper, onion, celery, and garlic in margarine till tender.
Meanwhile, in a bowl combine cooked grain, cream cheese, salt, and pepper. Stir in onion mixture. Transfer to a 1-quart casserole.
Bake, covered, in a 375° oven for 25 minutes or till heated through. Sprinkle with cheese. Bake 2 to 3 minutes more or till cheese melts.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 275)

recipes.title: Pies Nutrition Analysis
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, pages 280-281
recipes.description: Comprehensive nutrition analysis table for pie recipes.

instructions.text: This reference table provides per-serving nutrition data and percent U.S. RDA for all pie recipes in this chapter.
Columns include: Servings Per Recipe, Calories, Protein (g), Carbohydrate (g), Fat (g), Cholesterol (mg), Sodium (mg), Potassium (mg), and Percent U.S. RDA for nutrients.

notes: Reference chart for meal planning and dietary needs

recipes.title: Mince-Apple Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 281
recipes.description: A delicious combination of mincemeat and fresh apples in a double-crust pie.

instructions.text: Stir together apples, mincemeat, brown sugar, and orange juice. Transfer to a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate. Cut slits in top crust. Adjust top crust. Seal and flute edge. Brush crust with milk and sprinkle with sugar, if desired. Cover edge of pie with foil.
Bake in a 375° oven for 25 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes more or till pastry is golden and apples are tender. Serve with Hard Sauce, if desired. Makes 8 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 281)

recipes.title: Double-Crust Fruit Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 282
recipes.description: Classic double-crust fruit pie that works with a variety of fruits.

instructions.text: Mix ingredients for filling, adding flavoring, if desired. Transfer to a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate. Cut slits in top crust. Adjust top crust. Seal and flute edge. Sprinkle with sugar, if desired. Cover edge with foil.
Bake in a 375° oven 25 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes more or till the top is golden and fruit is tender. (Bake cherry pie for 50 to 60 minutes total.) Serves 8.

notes: Flavoring: Add one of the following to filling with the flour: 1/2 teaspoon finely shredded lemon or peel, 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice or ginger, or 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg. Or, add 1/4 teaspoon almond extract to filling with the fruit.

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for Pastry for Double-Crust Pie

recipes.title: Crumb-Topped Fruit Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 282
