recipes.description: Use the smallest amount of sugar recommended for your fruit because the brown-sugar topping also sweetens the pie.

instructions.text: Mix ingredients for filling, adding flavoring, if desired. Transfer filling to a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate. Combine flour and brown sugar. Cut in margarine till mixture resembles coarse crumbs; sprinkle over filling. Cover edge with foil.

Bake in a 375° oven 25 minutes. Remove foil. Bake 20 to 25 minutes more or till top is golden and fruit is tender. (Bake cherry pie for 50 to 60 minutes total.) If desired, drizzle with icing. Serves 8.

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for Pastry for Single-Crust Pie
Inferred 1.0 for Powdered Sugar Icing (standard quantity)

recipes.title: Deep-Dish Apple Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 284
recipes.description: Just spoon the filling into a casserole and top it with pastry for this old-time dessert.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine sugar, flour, cinnamon, and allspice. Add apples; toss to coat fruit. Transfer to a 1 1/2-quart casserole.

Prepare Pastry for Single-Crust Pie, except roll pastry 1 inch larger than top of casserole. Cut slits in pastry. Place pastry atop apples. Seal and flute edge to rim of casserole. Cover edge of pie with foil.
Place on a baking sheet. Bake in a 375° oven for 25 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes more or till crust is golden and filling is bubbly. Serve warm or cool. Makes 8 servings.

notes: Deep-Dish Peach Pie: Prepare as above, except omit cinnamon and allspice. Substitute 6 cups sliced, peeled peaches (3 pounds) for the apples. Sprinkle peaches with 1/2 teaspoon almond extract; toss with the sugar and flour.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 284)

recipes.title: Crunchy Peach Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 284
recipes.description: Almonds in the crumb topping add the crunch.

ingredients.item: canned peach slices, or unpeeled apricot halves

instructions.text: Mix crushed wafers, almonds, and margarine; set aside. Line the bottom of a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate with a double thickness of foil. Bake in a 450° oven for 5 minutes. Remove foil. Bake 5 minutes more. Meanwhile, beat together eggs and lemon juice; stir in sugar. Fold fruit into egg mixture.

Transfer fruit mixture to the partially baked pastry shell. Sprinkle with wafer mixture. Cover edge of pie with foil. Reduce oven temperature to 375°. Bake for 20 minutes. Remove foil; bake for 15 to 20 minutes more or till set. Cool on a wire rack. Cover and chill to store. Serves 8.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 284)

recipes.title: Raisin Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 284
recipes.description: A classic raisin pie with orange and walnuts.

instructions.text: In a saucepan mix brown sugar and cornstarch. Stir in raisins, peel, orange juice, lemon juice, and 1 1/2 cups cold water. Cook and stir till bubbly; cook and stir 2 minutes more. Remove from heat; stir in nuts.

Transfer to a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate. Cut slits in top crust. Adjust top crust. Seal and flute edge. Cover edge with foil. Bake in a 375° oven 25 minutes. Remove foil; bake 20 to 25 minutes more or till crust is golden. Serves 8.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 284)

recipes.title: Berry Glacé Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 285
recipes.description: The flavor of just-picked fruit awaits you in this delicious glazed pie.

ingredients.item: medium strawberries, or 3 cups red raspberries and 3 cups sliced, peeled peaches

instructions.text: Remove stems from strawberries. Cut any large strawberries in half lengthwise. Set aside.

For glaze, in a blender container or food processor bowl combine 1 cup of the strawberries or raspberries and the water. Cover and blend or process till smooth. (If using raspberries, press through a sieve after blending to remove seeds.) Add enough additional water to equal 1 1/2 cups.

In a medium saucepan combine sugar and cornstarch. Stir in blended berry mixture. Cook and stir over medium heat till mixture is thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Stir in red food coloring, if desired. Cool for 10 minutes without stirring.

Spread about 1/4 cup of the glaze over bottom and sides of the Baked Pastry Shell. Arrange half of the remaining strawberries, stem end down, in pastry shell (or half of the remaining raspberries and half of the peaches). Carefully spoon half of the remaining glaze over fruit, thoroughly covering each piece of fruit. Arrange remaining fruit over first layer. Spoon remaining glaze over fruit, covering each piece.
Chill for 1 to 2 hours. (After 2 hours, filling may begin to water out.) Garnish with whipped cream, if desired. Makes 8 servings.

Microwave directions: Prepare strawberries as above. For glaze, blend berries as above. In a 1 1/2-quart casserole combine sugar and cornstarch. Stir in blended berry mixture. Micro-cook, uncovered, on 100% power (high) for 3 to 5 minutes or till thickened and bubbly, stirring every minute. Cook, uncovered, on high for 30 seconds more. Stir in red food coloring, if desired. Cool for 10 minutes without stirring. Assemble and chill pie as above.

notes: Peach Glacé Pie: Prepare as above, except substitute 6 cups sliced, peeled peaches for the fruit and omit food coloring.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 298)

recipes.title: Cherry Lattice Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 285
recipes.description: A ruby red filling enticingly peeks through the lattice crust.

ingredients.item: canned pitted tart red cherries (water pack)

instructions.text: Drain cherries, reserving 1 cup liquid. In a large saucepan combine 3/4 cup of the sugar and the cornstarch. Stir in reserved cherry liquid. Cook and stir over medium heat till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat. Stir in the remaining sugar, margarine or butter, almond extract, and, if desired, food coloring. Stir in cherries. Cool slightly.

Fill a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate with cherry mixture. Top with lattice crust. Cover edge of pie with foil. Bake in a 375° oven for 25 minutes. Remove foil; bake for 25 to 30 minutes more or till crust is golden. Cool on a wire rack before serving. Makes 8 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 285)

recipes.title: Custard Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 286
recipes.description: Sweet, silky, and scrumptious.

instructions.text: Bake pastry shell in a 450° oven for 5 minutes.
For filling, in a bowl beat eggs slightly with a rotary beater or fork till combined. Stir in sugar, vanilla, and salt. Gradually stir in milk. Mix well.

Place the partially baked pastry shell on oven rack. Pour the filling into the pastry shell. Sprinkle with nutmeg. Cover edge of pie with foil. Reduce oven temperature to 350° and bake for 25 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes more or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Cool pie on a wire rack. Cover and chill to store. Makes 8 servings.

notes: Coconut Custard Pie: Prepare as above, except stir in 1/2 cup toasted coconut with the milk. Mix well.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 286)

recipes.title: Lemon Chess Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 286
recipes.description: This sweet yet tart pie hails from the South.

instructions.text: Line bottom of a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate with a double thickness of foil. Bake in a 450° oven for 5 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for 5 minutes more.
For filling, in a bowl beat eggs lightly till combined. Stir in sugar, margarine, peel, lemon juice, cornmeal, and vanilla. Mix well. Place pastry shell on the oven rack. Pour filling into shell.

Cover edge of pie with foil. Reduce oven temperature to 350° and bake for 20 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes more or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Cool on a rack. Cover and chill to store. Serves 8.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 286)

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 286
recipes.description: Classic pumpkin pie perfect for Thanksgiving.

instructions.text: For filling, in a mixing bowl combine pumpkin, sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg. Add eggs. Beat lightly with a rotary beater or fork. Gradually stir in evaporated milk and milk. Mix well.
Place a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate on the oven rack; pour in filling. Cover edge with foil.

Bake in a 375° oven for 25 minutes. Remove foil; bake about 25 minutes more or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Cool on a wire rack. Serve with whipped cream, if desired. Cover and chill to store. Makes 8 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 286)

recipes.title: Pecan Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 287
recipes.description: We offer three variations of this favorite pie: Maple, Pecan, Peanut, and Coconut-Oatmeal.

instructions.text: For filling, in a mixing bowl beat eggs lightly with a rotary beater or a fork till combined. Stir in corn syrup, sugar, margarine or butter, and vanilla. Stir well. Stir in pecan halves.
Place a pastry-lined 9-inch pie plate on the oven rack; pour the filling into the pastry-lined pie plate. Cover edge of pie with foil. Bake in a 350° oven for 25 minutes.
Remove foil; bake for 20 to 25 minutes more or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Cool pie on a wire rack. Cover and chill to store. Makes 8 servings.

notes: Maple Pecan Pie: Prepare as above, except substitute maple syrup or maple-flavored syrup for the corn syrup.
Peanut Pie: Prepare as above, except substitute coarsely chopped peanuts, macadamia nuts, or cashews for the pecans.
Coconut-Oatmeal Pie: Prepare as above, except substitute 3/4 cup coconut and 1/2 cup quick-cooking rolled oats for the pecans.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 287)

recipes.title: Brown Sugar and Rhubarb Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 287
recipes.description: A delicious rhubarb pie with meringue topping.

ingredients.item: finely chopped rhubarb (1 pound) or one 16-ounce package frozen unsweetened sliced rhubarb

instructions.text: Bake pastry in a 450° oven for 5 minutes.
For filling, in a mixing bowl combine brown sugar and flour. Add rhubarb; toss to coat. Let stand for 15 minutes (30 minutes for frozen rhubarb), stirring once or twice.

Separate egg yolks from whites; set whites aside for meringue. Beat egg yolks slightly with a fork. Stir yolks into rhubarb mixture. Transfer rhubarb mixture to the partially baked pastry shell. Cover edge of pie with foil. Reduce oven temperature to 375°. Bake for 25 minutes. (If using frozen rhubarb, bake 45 minutes.) Remove foil; bake for 20 to 25 minutes more or till filling is nearly set. (Pie will appear soft in the center but will become firmer upon cooling.)
Evenly spread meringue over hot filling, sealing to edge of pastry. Reduce oven temperature to 350°. Bake for 15 minutes. Cool on rack. Cover and chill to store. Serves 8.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 287)

recipes.title: Lemon Meringue Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 288
recipes.description: A refreshingly tangy dessert with fluffy meringue topping.

instructions.text: For filling, in a medium saucepan combine sugar, flour, cornstarch, and dash salt. Gradually stir in 1 3/4 cups water. Cook and stir over medium-high heat till thickened and bubbly. Reduce heat; cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat.

Separate egg yolks from whites; set whites aside for meringue. Beat egg yolks slightly. Gradually stir about 1 cup of the hot filling into yolks. Return all to saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Remove from heat. Stir in margarine and lemon peel. Gradually stir in lemon juice, gently mixing well. Pour hot filling into Baked Pastry Shell.
Evenly spread meringue over hot filling, sealing to edge. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes. Cool on a wire rack. Cover and chill to store. Makes 8 servings.

notes: Orange Meringue Pie: Prepare as above, except substitute 1 tablespoon finely shredded orange peel for the lemon peel and orange juice for the lemon juice. If desired, add 2 drops red food coloring and 1 drop yellow food coloring with the orange juice.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 288)

recipes.title: Key Lime Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 288
recipes.description: Although named for a variety of lime grown on the Florida Keys, our version tastes great with any type of lime.

instructions.text: Separate egg yolks from whites; set whites aside for meringue. In a bowl beat yolks till thick and lemon colored. Stir in condensed milk and lime peel. Gradually add lime juice, beating at low speed just till combined. Do not overbeat. Stir in green food coloring, if desired.

Spoon lime mixture into pastry shell. Evenly spread meringue over filling; seal to edge. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes. Cool. Cover and chill about 4 hours or till firm. Serve with whipped cream, if desired.

notes: Creamy Key Lime Pie: Prepare as above, except substitute 2 whole eggs for the yolks and omit meringue. Beat eggs till slightly thickened. Stir in condensed milk, peel, and juice. Spoon into pastry shell. Cover and chill about 4 hours or till firm. Serve with whipped cream, if desired.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 288)

recipes.title: Meringue for Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 288
recipes.description: Light and fluffy meringue topping for pies.

instructions.text: Bring egg whites to room temperature. In a mixing bowl combine egg whites, vanilla, and cream of tartar. Beat with an electric mixer on medium speed about 1 minute or till soft peaks form (tips curl).

Gradually add sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating on high speed about 4 minutes more or till mixture forms stiff, glossy peaks and sugar dissolves. Immediately spread meringue over pie, carefully sealing to edge of pastry to prevent shrinkage. Bake as directed in pie recipe.

notes: Four-Egg-White Meringue: Prepare as above, except use 4 egg whites, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 1/2 teaspoon cream of tartar, and 1/2 cup sugar. Beat about 5 minutes till stiff, glossy peaks form.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 290)

recipes.title: Vanilla Cream Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 289
recipes.description: If you like, skip the meringue and top the filling with whipped cream.

instructions.text: For filling, in a medium saucepan combine sugar and cornstarch or flour. Gradually stir in milk. Cook and stir over medium-high heat till mixture is thickened and bubbly. Reduce heat; cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat.

Separate egg yolks from whites; set whites aside for meringue. Beat egg yolks lightly with a fork. Gradually stir about 1 cup of the hot filling into yolks. Return all to saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil. Cook and stir 2 minutes more.

Remove from heat. Stir in margarine or butter and vanilla. Pour the hot filling into Baked Pastry Shell. Evenly spread meringue over hot filling, seal to edge. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes. Cool on a wire rack. Cover and chill to store. Makes 8 servings.

notes: Coconut Cream Pie: Prepare as above, except stir in 1 cup flaked coconut with margarine or butter and vanilla. Sprinkle another 1/2 cup flaked coconut over meringue before baking.
Banana Cream Pie: Prepare as above, except before adding filling, spread 3 medium bananas, sliced (about 2 1/4 cups), into the bottom of the Baked Pastry Shell.
Dark-Chocolate Cream Pie: Prepare as above, except increase the sugar to 1 cup. Stir in 3 squares (3 ounces) unsweetened chocolate, chopped, with the milk.
Milk-Chocolate Cream Pie: Prepare as above, except stir in 3 squares (3 ounces) semisweet chocolate, chopped, with the milk.

Sour Cream and Raisin Cream Pie: Prepare as above, except increase cornstarch to 1/3 cup (or increase flour to 2/3 cup). Fold in 1 cup raisins and 1/2 cup dairy sour cream with the margarine or butter and vanilla.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 286)

recipes.title: Fruity Cream Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 289
recipes.description: A light and creamy fruit-topped pie.

ingredients.item: canned unpeeled apricot halves or peach slices, or drain one 8 1/2-ounce can crushed pineapple

instructions.text: In a medium saucepan cook one 4-serving-size package regular vanilla pudding mix according to package directions, except use only 1 1/2 cups milk. Remove from heat. Drain and chop one 8 1/2-ounce can unpeeled apricot halves or peach slices, or drain one 8 1/2-ounce can crushed pineapple. Stir drained fruit and 2 tablespoons light rum or brandy into pudding. Cover surface with clear plastic wrap; cool to room temperature without stirring.

Fold one 4-ounce container frozen whipped dessert topping, thawed, into pudding mixture. Pour into a Baked Pastry Shell (see recipe, page 293). Cover and chill several hours. If desired, garnish with toasted coconut. Serves 8.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 289)

recipes.title: Black-Bottom Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 290
recipes.description: A rich chocolate layer topped with rum-flavored custard.

instructions.text: For filling, in a heavy medium saucepan combine 1/2 cup sugar and the cornstarch. Stir in milk. Cook and stir over medium heat till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Beat egg yolks slightly. Gradually stir about 1 cup of the hot mixture into egg yolks. Return all to saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Pour half of the filling (about 1 1/2 cups) into a bowl; add chocolate pieces. Stir till chocolate is melted. Spread chocolate filling into Baked Pastry Shell. Chill.
For rum layer, soften gelatin in 1/4 cup cold water. Stir softened gelatin and rum into remaining filling. Chill till mixture mounds when spooned, stirring occasionally.

For meringue, beat egg whites and cream of tartar with an electric mixer on medium speed till soft peaks form. Gradually add 1/4 cup sugar, beating on high speed till stiff peaks form. Fold rum mixture into meringue. Spread over chocolate layer. Chill about 4 hours or till set. Garnish with whipped cream and grated chocolate, if desired.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 290)

recipes.title: Lemon Chiffon Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 290
recipes.description: Light and fluffy lemon chiffon pie.

instructions.text: In a small saucepan combine gelatin and 1/2 cup of the sugar. Beat together egg yolks, lemon peel, lemon juice, and 1/2 cup water; add to gelatin mixture. Cook and stir over medium heat till gelatin is dissolved and mixture slightly thickens (do not boil). Remove from heat.
Transfer to a bowl. Chill about 2 hours or till mixture mounds when spooned, stirring occasionally.

Beat egg whites with electric mixer on medium speed till soft peaks form (tips curl). Gradually add remaining sugar, beating on high speed till stiff peaks form. Fold lemon mixture into egg whites. Spoon into Baked Pastry Shell. Chill about 4 hours or till set. Garnish with whipped cream, if desired.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 290)

recipes.title: Chocolate Chiffon Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 290
recipes.description: Rich chocolate chiffon in a flaky pastry shell.

instructions.text: In a medium saucepan combine gelatin and 1/2 cup of the sugar. Stir in 1 1/4 cups water. Add chocolate. Cook and stir over medium heat till chocolate is melted and gelatin is dissolved.

Beat egg yolks slightly. Gradually stir about half of the hot mixture into egg yolks. Return all to saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla.
Transfer to a bowl. Chill about 2 hours or till mixture mounds when spooned, stirring occasionally.

Beat egg whites with electric mixer on medium speed till soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining sugar, beating on high speed till stiff peaks form. Fold chocolate mixture into egg whites. Spoon into Baked Pastry Shell. Chill about 4 hours or till set. Garnish with whipped cream, if desired.

notes: Mocha Chiffon Pie: Prepare as above, except add 2 tablespoons instant coffee crystals to saucepan with the gelatin and sugar.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 290)

recipes.title: Parfait Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 290
recipes.description: An easy ice cream pie using frozen whipped topping.

ingredients.item: strawberry, raspberry, or cherry ice cream topping
Baked Pastry Shell or Graham Cracker Crust

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl fold together thawed dessert topping and ice cream topping. Spoon into pastry shell or crumb crust. Cover and freeze for 8 hours or overnight. Let stand at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes before serving.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 290)

recipes.title: Strawberry Chiffon Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 291
recipes.description: Fresh strawberry flavor in a light chiffon filling.

ingredients.item: fresh strawberries, or one 10-ounce package frozen sliced strawberries, thawed

instructions.text: Place fresh strawberries in a blender container or food processor bowl. Cover and blend or process till nearly smooth (should have about 1 3/4 cups). Or, if using frozen strawberries, do not thaw; blend till smooth.
In a medium saucepan combine gelatin and 1/3 cup of the sugar. Stir in pureed strawberries and lemon juice. Cook and stir over medium heat till gelatin is dissolved.
Transfer to a bowl. Chill till mixture mounds when spooned, stirring occasionally.

Beat egg whites with electric mixer on medium speed till soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining sugar, beating on high speed till stiff peaks form. Fold strawberry mixture into egg whites. Spoon into Baked Pastry Shell. Chill about 4 hours or till set. Garnish with whipped cream, if desired.

notes: Raspberry Chiffon Pie: Prepare as above, except substitute 3 cups fresh or frozen red raspberries for the strawberries. After blending, sieve to remove seeds.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 291)

recipes.title: Fudge Ribbon Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 292
recipes.description: Layers of peppermint ice cream and fudge sauce.

instructions.text: For fudge sauce, in a small saucepan combine sugar, milk, and chocolate. Cook and stir over medium heat till bubbly. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat. Stir in margarine or butter and vanilla. (If necessary, beat smooth with a rotary beater.) Set aside to cool.

Stir ice cream just to soften; spread half in Graham Cracker Crust. Cover; freeze till firm. Drizzle with half of the fudge sauce. Freeze till firm. Repeat ice cream and sauce layers; freeze till firm. (Cover and chill any remaining sauce to serve later.) To serve, let stand at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 292)

recipes.title: French Silk Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 292
recipes.description: Silky smooth chocolate filling in a flaky pastry.

instructions.text: In a medium mixing bowl beat butter with an electric mixer on medium speed for 30 seconds. Gradually add sugar, beating about 4 minutes or till fluffy. Stir in cooled chocolate and vanilla. Gradually add egg product, beating on high speed and scraping bowl constantly till light and fluffy.
Spread filling into Baked Pastry Shell. Cover and chill for 5 to 24 hours. Garnish with whipped cream and chocolate curls, if desired.

notes: For food safety, this recipe uses pasteurized egg product instead of raw eggs.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 292)

recipes.title: Grasshopper Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 292
recipes.description: Minty green pie in a chocolate crumb crust.

instructions.text: In a medium saucepan heat marshmallows and milk over low heat till marshmallows are melted, stirring frequently. Remove from heat; stir in crème de menthe and crème de cacao. Cool, stirring occasionally.

In a chilled bowl beat whipping cream with chilled beaters of an electric mixer on medium speed till soft peaks form. Fold marshmallow mixture into whipped cream. Spoon into Chocolate-Wafer Crust. Cover and chill about 4 hours or till set.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 292)

recipes.title: Pastry for Single-Crust Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 293
recipes.description: Basic flaky pie crust for single-crust pies.

instructions.text: In a bowl stir together flour and salt. Cut in shortening till pieces are the size of small peas.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the water over part of the mixture; gently toss with a fork. Push to side of bowl. Repeat till all is moistened. Form into a ball.

On a lightly floured surface, flatten dough with hands. Roll dough from center to edges, forming a 12-inch circle. Wrap pastry around rolling pin. Unroll into a 9-inch pie plate. Ease pastry into pie plate, being careful not to stretch. Trim to 1/2 inch beyond edge of pie plate; fold under extra pastry. Make a fluted edge. Do not prick pastry. Bake as directed in individual recipes.

notes: Baked Pastry Shell: Prepare as above, except prick bottom and sides of pastry generously with the tines of a fork. Prick where bottom and sides meet all around the pie shell. Bake in a 450° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or till golden. Cool on a wire rack.
Pecan Pastry: Prepare as above, except add 1/4 cup ground toasted pecans to flour mixture. Bake as for Baked Pastry Shell.
Cocoa Pastry: Prepare as above, except reduce flour to 1 cup. Sift 3 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder and 2 tablespoons sugar with the flour.
Cinnamon Pastry: Prepare as above, except add 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon to flour mixture. Bake as for Baked Pastry Shell.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 293)

recipes.title: Pastry for Double-Crust Pie
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 294
recipes.description: Basic flaky pie crust for double-crust pies.

instructions.text: In a bowl stir together flour and salt. Cut in shortening till pieces are the size of small peas.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon water over part of the mixture; gently toss with a fork. Push to side of bowl. Repeat till all is moistened. Divide dough in half. Form each half into a ball.

On a lightly floured surface, flatten one ball of dough with hands. Roll dough from center to edges, forming a 12-inch circle. Wrap pastry around rolling pin; unroll into a 9-inch pie plate. Ease pastry into pie plate. Trim to edge of pie plate. Fill as directed in individual recipes.
Roll remaining dough into a 12-inch circle. Cut slits for steam to escape. Place on filling. Trim to 1/2 inch beyond edge. Fold top pastry under bottom pastry; flute edge. Bake as directed.

notes: Electric-Mixer Pastry: Prepare as above, except use 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 1/4 cups shortening, and 1/3 cup cold water. Combine flour and salt in mixing bowl. Add shortening. Beat with electric mixer on low speed till pieces are the size of small peas. Add water; mix on low speed just till dough clings together. Makes enough for 2 double-crust pies or 4 single-crust pies.

Pastry for Lattice-Top Pie: Prepare as above. Fill pastry-lined pie plate. Cut remaining pastry into 1/2-inch-wide strips. Weave strips atop filling to make a lattice. Press ends into rim of crust. Fold bottom pastry over strips; seal and flute.
Cheese Pastry: Prepare as above, except reduce shortening to 1/2 cup and add 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese to flour mixture.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 294)

recipes.title: Oil Pastry
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 294
recipes.description: Easy pie crust made with oil instead of shortening.

instructions.text: In a bowl stir together flour and salt. In a measuring cup combine oil and milk. Pour oil mixture all at once into flour mixture.
Stir with a fork till dough forms a ball. (If dough seems dry, add 1 to 2 tablespoons additional milk.)

On waxed paper or between 2 sheets of waxed paper, roll dough from center to edges, forming a 12-inch circle. Peel off top paper. Invert pastry into a 9-inch pie plate; peel off paper. Press pastry into pie plate. Trim; flute edge. Do not prick pastry. Fill and bake as directed in individual recipes. (Or, for a baked pastry shell, prick crust and bake in a 450° oven for 10 to 12 minutes.)

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 294)

recipes.title: Graham Cracker Crust
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 294
recipes.description: Classic crumb crust for cream pies.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine crushed crackers and sugar. Stir in melted margarine or butter. Mix well.
Spread mixture evenly into a 9-inch pie plate. Press onto bottom and sides to form a firm, even crust.
Bake in a 375° oven for 6 to 8 minutes or till edges are brown. Cool on a wire rack before filling. (Or, chill about 1 hour or till firm.)

notes: Chocolate-Wafer Crust: Prepare as above, except substitute 1 1/4 cups finely crushed chocolate wafers (about 20 cookies) for the graham crackers and omit sugar.
Gingersnap Crust: Prepare as above, except substitute 1 1/4 cups finely crushed gingersnaps (about 20 cookies) for the graham crackers and omit sugar.
Vanilla-Wafer Crust: Prepare as above, except substitute 1 1/4 cups finely crushed vanilla wafers (about 30 cookies) for the graham crackers and omit sugar.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 294)

recipes.title: Coconut Crust
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 294
recipes.description: Toasted coconut crust for cream pies.

instructions.text: Combine coconut and melted margarine or butter. Press evenly onto the bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate.
Bake in a 325° oven for 20 minutes or till edge is golden. Cool on a wire rack before filling.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 294)

recipes.title: Poultry Nutrition Analysis
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, pages 296-297
recipes.description: Comprehensive nutrition analysis table for poultry recipes.

instructions.text: This reference table provides per-serving nutrition data and percent U.S. RDA for all poultry recipes in this chapter.
Columns include: Servings Per Recipe, Calories, Protein (g), Carbohydrate (g), Fat (g), Cholesterol (mg), Sodium (mg), Potassium (mg), and Percent U.S. RDA for nutrients.

notes: Reference chart for meal planning and dietary needs

recipes.title: Four-Way Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 299
recipes.description: Basic roasted chicken with four different sauce options.

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Skewer neck skin to back. Tie legs to tail; twist wing tips under back. Place, breast side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Brush with oil; sprinkle with salt and pepper.

Roast, uncovered, in a 375° oven for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours or till drumstick moves easily in socket. When bird is two-thirds done, cut string between legs. Brush with desired sauce during the last 15 minutes of roasting. Makes 6 servings.

notes: Barbecue Sauce: Combine 1/2 cup catsup, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.

Cumberland Sauce: In a saucepan combine 1/2 cup currant jelly, 2 tablespoons orange juice, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger, and dash ground red pepper. Cook and stir till jelly melts.
Ginger-Honey Glaze: Combine 2 tablespoons honey, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, and 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger.

recipes.title: Pepper-Lime Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 300
recipes.description: Grilled chicken with a zesty pepper-lime marinade.

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Place in a plastic bag set in a shallow dish. For marinade, combine lime juice, oil, pepper, paprika, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Pour over chicken. Close bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 2 to 24 hours, turning bag occasionally.

Drain chicken, reserving marinade. Place chicken, bone side up, on an uncovered grill directly over medium coals. Grill for 20 minutes. Turn chicken; brush with reserved marinade. Grill for 15 to 25 minutes more or till tender, brushing often with marinade. Makes 6 servings.

notes: Lemon-Mustard Chicken: Prepare as above, except substitute 3 tablespoons lemon juice for lime juice and 1 tablespoon Dijon-style mustard for the pepper.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 300)

recipes.title: Herb-Marinated Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 300
recipes.description: Grilled chicken with herb vinaigrette marinade.

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Place in a plastic bag set in a shallow dish. For marinade, combine vinegar, oil, garlic, basil, thyme, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Pour over chicken; close bag.
Marinate in the refrigerator for 2 to 24 hours, turning bag occasionally. Grill as for Pepper-Lime Chicken. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 300)

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Glazed Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 301
recipes.description: Grilled chicken with a tangy sweet-and-sour glaze.

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. For glaze, combine undrained pineapple, brown sugar, lemon juice, and soy sauce.

Place chicken, bone side up, on an uncovered grill directly over medium coals. Grill for 20 minutes. Turn; grill 15 to 25 minutes more or till tender, brushing with glaze the last 10 minutes. Heat any remaining glaze; pass with chicken.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 301)

recipes.title: Chicken Kabobs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 301
recipes.description: Grilled chicken and vegetable kabobs with honey-lime glaze.

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Cut into 1-inch pieces. For glaze, combine honey, lime juice, and mustard.

On six long skewers, alternately thread chicken, zucchini, and tomatoes. Place on an uncovered grill directly over medium coals. Grill for 12 to 14 minutes or till chicken is tender and no longer pink, turning and brushing often with glaze. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 301)

recipes.title: Cranberry-Sauced Turkey Steaks
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 302
recipes.description: Broiled turkey steaks with tangy cranberry sauce.

ingredients.item: cranberry-orange relish or whole cranberry sauce

instructions.text: Rinse turkey; pat dry. Place on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 4 to 5 inches from the heat for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, for sauce, combine relish or cranberry sauce, orange juice, mustard, and ginger. Turn turkey; brush with sauce. Broil for 5 to 7 minutes more or till no longer pink, brushing once more with sauce. Heat remaining sauce; serve with turkey. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 302)

recipes.title: Oven-Fried Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 303
recipes.description: Crispy oven-baked chicken with a variety of coating options.

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse; pat dry. Brush chicken with melted margarine or butter.
In a plastic bag combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, thyme or sage, paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add 2 or 3 pieces of chicken at a time; shake to coat.

In a greased 15x10x1-inch baking pan arrange chicken, bone side down, so pieces don't touch. Drizzle with remaining margarine. Bake, uncovered, in a 375° oven for 45 to 55 minutes or till tender and no longer pink. Do not turn. Makes 6 servings.

notes: Potato-Chip Chicken: Prepare as above, except substitute 1 1/4 cups finely crushed potato chips for the bread crumbs. Omit thyme and paprika.
Parmesan Chicken: Prepare as above, except increase Parmesan cheese to 1/2 cup and omit thyme.
Curry-and-Parsley Chicken: Prepare as above, except add 1/2 to 3/4 teaspoon curry powder to crumb mixture.

Crispy Barbecue-Style Chicken: Prepare as above, except substitute 1/2 cup bottled barbecue sauce for the melted margarine or butter. Reduce crumbs to 1/2 cup; omit Parmesan cheese, herb, and paprika.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 303)

recipes.title: Chicken Nuggets
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 303
recipes.description: Crispy bite-size chicken pieces.

ingredients.item: dried basil, oregano, or thyme, crushed

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Cut into 1-inch pieces.
In a plastic bag combine crumbs, Parmesan cheese, herb, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Dip chicken pieces in margarine; shake, a few at a time, in crumb mixture.
Arrange in a single layer in a shallow baking pan. Bake in a 400° oven for 6 to 8 minutes or till no longer pink.

notes: Chili Chicken Nuggets: Prepare as above, except add 1 1/2 teaspoons chili powder to crumb mixture.
Sesame-Soy Chicken Nuggets: Prepare as above, except substitute 2 tablespoons sesame seed for the Parmesan cheese and 1/4 cup soy sauce for the margarine or butter.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 303)

recipes.title: Chicken Dijon
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 304
recipes.description: Creamy Dijon mustard sauce over tender chicken breasts.

ingredients.item: long grain rice or herb-flavored rice mix

instructions.text: Cook rice according to package directions. Meanwhile, rinse chicken; pat dry. Sprinkle both sides of chicken with lemon-pepper seasoning and onion powder.
In a skillet cook chicken in margarine over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes or till tender and no longer pink, turning to brown evenly. Transfer to a platter; keep warm.

For sauce, measure pan juices; add light cream or milk to make 1/2 cup liquid. Return to the skillet. Stir 1/4 cup light cream or milk into flour; add to juices mixture. Stir in mustard. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 1 to 2 minutes more. Spoon some sauce over chicken; pass remaining sauce. Serve with rice. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 304)

recipes.title: Chicken Kiev
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 304
recipes.description: Classic stuffed chicken breasts with herb butter.

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Place each breast half, boned side up, between 2 pieces of clear plastic wrap. Working from the center to the edges, pound lightly with the flat side of a meat mallet to 1/4-inch thickness. Remove plastic wrap. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Combine onion, parsley, and garlic; sprinkle on chicken.

Cut chilled butter into four 2 1/2x1/2-inch sticks. Place one piece in the center of each chicken piece. Fold in sides; roll up jelly-roll style, pressing edges to seal. Stir together egg and 1 tablespoon water. Coat rolls with flour, dip into egg mixture, then coat with crumbs. Cover; chill 1 to 24 hours.

In a large skillet melt the 1 tablespoon butter; add oil. Add chilled chicken rolls; cook over medium-high heat about 5 minutes or till golden brown, turning to brown all sides. Transfer to a 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. Bake in a 400° oven for 15 to 18 minutes or till no longer pink. Spoon drippings over rolls. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Cheesy Chicken Kiev: Prepare as above, except, for the butter in chicken rolls, substitute four 2x1/2-inch sticks of caraway cheese, Gruyère cheese, blue cheese, Camembert (rind removed), Brie (rind removed), or cheddar cheese.

Pick-a-Butter Chicken Kiev: Prepare as above, except, for the butter in the chicken rolls, substitute 1/4 cup (1/2 recipe) parsley butter or lemon-tarragon butter (see tip, page 368), shaped into four 2 1/2x1/2-inch sticks and chilled.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 304)

recipes.title: Chicken Saltimbocca
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 305
recipes.description: Italian-style chicken rolls with prosciutto and cheese.

ingredients.prep_note: (1 1/2 pounds total), skinned, boned, and halved lengthwise

ingredients.item: thin slices prosciutto or fully cooked ham
dairy sour cream or plain yogurt

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Place each breast half, boned side up, between 2 pieces of clear plastic wrap. Working from the center to the edges, pound lightly with the flat side of a mallet to form 1/8-inch-thick rectangles. Remove plastic wrap.

For each roll, place 1 slice of prosciutto or ham on a chicken piece, folding if necessary to fit. Place 1 slice of cheese atop prosciutto or ham near one edge. Top with some of the tomato. Fold in long sides of chicken and roll up jelly-roll style, starting from the edge with the cheese. Secure with wooden toothpicks.
In a large skillet cook chicken rolls in 2 tablespoons of the margarine over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes or till no longer pink, turning to brown evenly. Remove toothpicks.

For sauce, in a medium saucepan melt remaining margarine. Add mushrooms and garlic. Cook till tender. Remove from heat. Stir together milk, sour cream, flour, paprika, nutmeg, 1/8 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Add to sauce. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Arrange noodles and chicken on a platter. Pour sauce over all. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 305)

recipes.title: Chicken Marsala
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 306
recipes.description: Tender chicken in a rich Marsala wine sauce with mushrooms.

ingredients.prep_note: (1 1/2 pounds total), skinned, boned, and halved lengthwise

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Place each breast half, boned side up, between 2 pieces of clear plastic wrap. Working from the center to edges, pound lightly with the flat side of a mallet till 1/8 inch thick. Remove the plastic wrap. Stir together flour, marjoram, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Lightly press chicken pieces into flour mixture on both sides; shake off excess.

In a large skillet cook mushrooms and green onion in 1 tablespoon of the margarine till tender; remove from skillet. In the same skillet cook chicken pieces in remaining margarine over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, turning to brown evenly. Remove skillet from heat. Return mushrooms and onion to skillet. Carefully add broth and marsala. Cook, uncovered, 2 to 3 minutes or till mushroom mixture thickens slightly, stirring occasionally. Transfer chicken to a serving platter. Spoon mushroom mixture over. Sprinkle with snipped parsley, if desired. Serves 4.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 306)

recipes.title: Skillet-Fried Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 307
recipes.description: Classic pan-fried chicken with crispy coating.

ingredients.item: all-purpose flour or 1/2 cup fine dry bread crumbs
paprika, curry powder, chili powder, or dried basil or marjoram, crushed; or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder or onion powder

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. In a plastic bag combine flour, paprika or other seasoning, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add chicken pieces, a few at a time, shaking to coat.

In a 12-inch skillet heat oil. Add chicken, placing meaty pieces toward the center of the skillet. Cook, uncovered, over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning to brown evenly. Reduce heat; cover tightly. Cook for 25 minutes. Uncover; cook for 5 to 10 minutes more or till tender and no longer pink. Drain on paper towels. Makes 6 servings.

Oven directions: Rinse chicken; pat dry. Coat chicken as above. Brown chicken in a 12-inch ovenproof skillet. (Or, brown chicken in a regular skillet, then transfer, skin side up, to a 15x10x1-inch baking pan.) Place in a 375° oven. Bake, uncovered, for 35 to 40 minutes or till no longer pink. Do not turn.
Crisp-Fried Chicken: Prepare as above, except, after browning for 15 minutes, cook, uncovered, over medium-low heat for 35 to 40 minutes more or till no longer pink, turning often.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 307)

recipes.title: Garlic Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 308
recipes.description: Stir-fried chicken with lots of garlic.

ingredients.item: dry sherry or dry white wine

ingredients.prep_note: (1 pound total), skinned, boned, and cut into 3/4-inch pieces
minced (3 tablespoons), or 2 to 3 tablespoons bottled minced garlic

instructions.text: For marinade, in a bowl stir together water, sherry, and soy sauce. Add chicken to marinade. Cut chicken into 3/4-inch pieces. Rinse chicken; dry. Cut chicken into 3/4-inch pieces. Add chicken to marinade, stirring to coat. Let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes. Drain chicken.

Preheat a wok or large skillet over high heat; add oil. (Add more oil as necessary during cooking.) Stir-fry green onions or leeks, garlic, and water chestnuts for 1 to 2 minutes or till crisp-tender. Remove from wok or skillet.

Add half of the chicken to hot wok or skillet. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till no longer pink. Remove. Stir-fry remaining chicken for 2 to 3 minutes. Return all chicken and garlic mixture to wok. Stir in reserved marinade. Heat through. Serve over rice sticks. Serves 4.

notes: Garlic Chicken with Zucchini: Prepare as above, except stir-fry 1 1/2 cups (about 1 1/4 cups) halved lengthwise and cut into 1/4-inch-thick slices zucchini for 3 minutes. Remove from wok or skillet. Return zucchini to wok with cooked chicken.

Chicken with Cashews: Prepare as above, except stir 1/4 teaspoon crushed red pepper into marinade. Reduce garlic to 2 cloves (or 1 1/2 teaspoons bottled minced garlic). Stir-fry 1 cup unsalted cashews or peanuts with the garlic and green onions.

Orange Chicken with Walnuts: Prepare as above, except substitute finely shredded orange peel for the sherry and add 1/2 teaspoon finely shredded orange peel to the sauce. Stir in two oranges, peeled and sectioned, just before serving.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 308)

recipes.title: Chicken with Walnuts
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 308
recipes.description: Stir-fried chicken with walnuts and vegetables.

instructions.text: For sauce, in a small bowl stir together soy sauce, sherry, sugar, and cornstarch, and red pepper. Set aside. Rinse chicken; pat dry. Cut into 1-inch pieces, set aside.
Preheat a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add walnuts; stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till lightly toasted. Remove from wok or skillet; set aside.
Add oil to wok. Stir-fry green peppers and ginger for 1 to 2 minutes or till crisp-tender. Remove from wok.
Add half of the chicken to the wok or skillet. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till no longer pink. Remove. Stir-fry remaining chicken 2 to 3 minutes; remove.

Stir sauce; add to the center of the wok or skillet. Cook and stir till bubbly. Return all chicken, green peppers, and walnuts to wok. Stir all ingredients to coat with sauce. Stir-fry about 1 minute or till heated through. Stir in kumquats, if desired. Serve with hot rice. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 308)

recipes.title: Ginger Chicken
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 309
recipes.description: Stir-fried chicken with ginger and vegetables.

ingredients.item: fresh pea pods, tips and strings removed, or one 6-ounce package frozen pea pods, thawed
bias-sliced bok choy or chopped cabbage

instructions.text: Stir together sherry, soy sauce, hoisin or bean sauce, water, and cornstarch. Set aside. Rinse chicken; pat dry. Cut into thin bite-size strips.

Preheat a wok or large skillet over high heat; add 1 tablespoon of the oil. (Add remaining oil as necessary during cooking.) Add bok choy or cabbage, carrots, and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till crisp. Add pea pods, bok choy, carrots, and onions; stir-fry about 3 seconds. Add soy sauce mixture to wok or skillet. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir about 1 minute more. Serve with hot rice. Makes 4 servings.
Stir the soy sauce mixture to remix the ingredients, then add it to the center of the wok or skillet.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 309)

recipes.title: Chicken Fricassee
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 312
recipes.description: This braised chicken, with its rich, creamy sauce, represents country cooking at its best.

ingredients.item: chopped green or sweet red pepper or celery
dried basil, marjoram, oregano, or thyme, crushed

instructions.text: In a plastic or paper bag combine the 1/4 cup flour, paprika, salt, and pepper. Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse chicken; pat dry. Add chicken, two or three pieces at a time, to the bag, shaking to coat well.
In a 12-inch skillet cook chicken in hot oil about 15 minutes or till lightly browned, turning to brown evenly. Remove chicken; set aside.

Drain fat, reserving 2 tablespoons of the drippings in the skillet (add more oil, if necessary). Add mushrooms, green or red pepper or celery, and green onion to skillet. Cook and stir for 2 minutes. Stir in chicken broth and basil, marjoram, oregano, or thyme.

Bring to boiling, scraping up browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Return chicken to the skillet. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes or till chicken is tender and no longer pink.

Transfer chicken and vegetables to a platter; keep warm. Skim fat from pan juices; measure 3/4 cup of the pan juices and return to the skillet. Stir cream or milk into the 1 tablespoon flour. Stir into pan juices. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 1 minute more.
Spoon some of the sauce over chicken; pass remaining sauce. Serve with hot noodles or spaetzle. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 312)

recipes.title: Chicken Paprikash
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 312
recipes.description: Hungarian-style chicken in a rich paprika sour cream sauce.

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse and pat dry. In a 12-inch skillet cook chicken in hot oil about 15 minutes or till lightly browned, turning to brown evenly. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Remove chicken; set aside.

Add onion and paprika to skillet; cook till onion is tender. Add chicken, turning pieces to coat with paprika mixture. Add broth and wine. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover; simmer 40 minutes or till chicken is tender and no longer pink.
Transfer chicken to a platter. Cover and keep warm.

For sauce, skim fat from pan juices. Measure 1 1/2 cups juices, adding water, if necessary. In a bowl stir together sour cream and flour; gradually stir in juices mixture. Pour into skillet. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly; cook and stir for 1 minute more. Spoon some sauce over chicken; pass remainder. Serve with hot cooked noodles or rice. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 312)

recipes.title: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 313
recipes.description: Italian hunter-style chicken braised with tomatoes and mushrooms.

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse and pat dry. In a large skillet cook chicken, onion, and garlic in hot oil about 15 minutes or till chicken is lightly browned, turning to brown evenly. Drain off fat.

Stir together mushrooms, tomato sauce, undrained tomatoes, wine, broth, basil, bay leaf, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Pour over chicken in the skillet. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes or till chicken is tender and no longer pink.

Transfer chicken to a platter. Cover; keep warm. Discard bay leaf. Skim fat from tomato mixture. Stir together cornstarch and 2 tablespoons cold water; stir into tomato mixture. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 2 minutes more. Serve over chicken and noodles. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 313)

recipes.title: Coq au Vin
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 313
recipes.description: Classic French chicken braised in burgundy wine sauce.

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse and pat dry. In a 12-inch skillet cook chicken pieces in hot oil about 15 minutes or till lightly browned, turning to brown evenly. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Add onions or shallots, burgundy, mushrooms, carrot, the 1 tablespoon parsley, garlic, marjoram, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes or till chicken is tender and no longer pink.
Transfer chicken and vegetables to a serving platter. Cover and keep warm. Discard bay leaf.

In a bowl stir together flour and softened margarine or butter to make a smooth paste. Stir into burgundy mixture in the skillet. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Pour burgundy mixture over chicken and vegetables. Sprinkle with bacon and, if desired, additional parsley. Serve with hot noodles. Makes 6 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 313)

recipes.title: Chicken Enchiladas
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 317
recipes.description: Cheese-topped chicken enchiladas with sour cream sauce.

ingredients.item: canned jalapeño chili peppers, rinsed, seeded, and chopped; or one 4-ounce can diced green chili peppers, drained

instructions.text: Wrap tortillas in foil. Heat in a 350° oven for 10 to 15 minutes or till softened.

For sauce, in a saucepan cook onion, garlic, coriander, and pepper in margarine or butter till onion is tender. Stir flour into sour cream; add to onion mixture. Stir in broth and chili peppers. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Remove from heat; stir in 1/2 cup of the cheese.

For filling, stir 1/2 cup of the sauce into chicken. Place about 1/4 cup filling atop each tortilla; roll up. Arrange rolls, seam side down, in a lightly greased 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. Top with remaining sauce. Bake, covered, in a 350° oven about 35 minutes or till heated through.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese. Bake, uncovered, about 5 minutes more or till cheese melts. If desired, sprinkle with olives, tomatoes, and green onions. Let stand 10 minutes. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: From Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis (p. 317)

recipes.title: Pecan Crunch
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.source_note: Cookbook page - Cakes, Cookies, Candies section
recipes.description: A chocolate-topped shortbread bar with toasted pecans.

instructions.text: Into large bowl, measure first 5 ingredients. With hand, knead dough until well blended and it holds together.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Pat dough evenly into 15½" by 10½" jelly-roll pan. Bake 25 minutes.
In small saucepan over low heat, melt chocolate, stirring frequently; set aside.
Remove pan from oven; pour chocolate over baked layer; with spatula, evenly spread over; sprinkle with pecans. Cool on wire rack.
When cool, cut lengthwise into 6 strips, cut each strip crosswise into 12 pieces. Store in tightly-covered container; use up within 1 week.

notes: 75 calories per bar

assumptions: Per bar as stated in cookbook

recipes.title: Chicken Jambalaya
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: A quick Cajun-style one-pot meal with chicken, rice, tomatoes, and vegetables.

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook celery, onion, and green pepper in margarine or butter till vegetables are tender.
Stir in the undrained tomatoes, chicken broth, rice, basil or thyme, garlic salt, pepper, hot pepper sauce, and bay leaf.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 20 minutes or till rice is tender.
Stir in chicken; cook till heated through. Discard bay leaf. Makes 4 servings.

notes: FAST recipe tag in cookbook

recipes.title: Chicken-Cheese Crepes
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant crepes filled with chicken, peas, carrots, and a creamy cheese sauce.

ingredients.item: shredded process Swiss, Gruyere, or American cheese

instructions.text: Prepare Crepes. Cook frozen peas and carrots according to package directions. Drain and season to taste with salt and pepper; set aside.

For sauce, in a medium saucepan cook onion and green pepper in margarine till tender. Stir in flour. Add milk and broth all at once. Cook and stir till bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Stir in cheese; sherry, if desired; parsley; and hot pepper sauce. Remove 1 cup of the sauce; set aside.

Drain mushrooms; stir into remaining sauce. For filling, combine cooked peas and carrots, the 1 cup sauce, and chicken or turkey. Spread 1/4 cup filling over the unbrowned side of each crepe, leaving a 1/4-inch rim around edge. Roll up crepes.

Place, seam side down, in a 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. Cover; bake in a 375° oven for 15 to 18 minutes or till heated through. Reheat remaining sauce; drizzle some over crepes. Pass remaining sauce. Makes 6 servings.

notes: Microwave directions available in original

assumptions: Inferred 0.25 for bottled hot pepper sauce (standard quantity)

recipes.title: Chicken Divan
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic casserole with chicken and broccoli in a creamy cheese sauce, topped with Parmesan.

instructions.text: Cook broccoli according to package directions; drain. Arrange in a 10x6x2-inch baking dish.

Meanwhile, for sauce, in a medium saucepan melt margarine or butter. Stir in flour, pepper, and nutmeg. Add cream or milk and chicken broth all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Add Swiss cheese and wine, stirring till cheese melts.
Pour half of the sauce over broccoli. Top with chicken or turkey, then the remaining sauce. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and paprika.
Bake in a 350° oven about 20 minutes or till heated through. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Microwave directions available in original

recipes.title: Chicken-Asparagus Stacks
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: English muffins topped with asparagus, chicken, and a creamy yogurt sauce.

instructions.text: Cook asparagus or broccoli according to package directions. Drain; keep warm.

In a saucepan cook onion in margarine till onion is tender. Stir in condensed soup and yogurt till smooth. Stir in chicken. Heat through. If desired, stir in almonds. Top rusks or muffin halves with the asparagus or broccoli, chicken mixture, and egg slices. Makes 4 servings.

notes: FAST recipe tag in cookbook
Microwave directions available

recipes.title: Chicken Submarines
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Hearty submarine sandwiches filled with chicken, avocado, and a creamy yogurt dressing.

ingredients.item: dairy sour cream, plain yogurt, mayonnaise, or salad dressing

ingredients.prep_note: small, halved, seed removed, peeled, and thinly sliced
American, Swiss, cheddar, or Monterey Jack

instructions.text: In a bowl mix 1/2 cup dairy sour cream, plain yogurt, mayonnaise, or salad dressing; 2 teaspoons prepared mustard; 1/2 teaspoon dried basil, crushed; and 1/8 teaspoon garlic powder.
Halve, seed, peel, and thinly slice 1 small avocado. If desired, brush avocado with lemon juice.
Split 4 individual French rolls and scoop out some of the center of each half. Spread both halves of rolls with some of the yogurt mixture.

On the bottom half of each roll, layer 1 leaf lettuce; 2 slices cooked chicken or turkey; 1 slice American, Swiss, cheddar, or Monterey Jack cheese; 3 thin slices tomato or 6 thin slices cucumber; and the avocado slices. If desired, top with alfalfa sprouts. Replace roll tops. Serves 4.

recipes.title: Glazed Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Roasted chicken with potatoes, carrots, and apples in a honey-mustard glaze.

ingredients.prep_note: peeled and quartered, or 6 new potatoes

instructions.text: Rinse chicken and pat dry. Skewer neck skin to back. Tie legs to tail. Twist wing tips under back. Place, breast side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Brush with oil. Roast chicken, uncovered, in a 375° oven for 1 hour.
Cook potatoes and carrots in boiling water for 20 to 25 minutes or till nearly tender. Drain.
For glaze, in a saucepan combine honey, mustard, margarine, onion, curry powder, garlic salt, red pepper, and ginger. Bring to boiling, stirring constantly. Remove from heat; set aside.

Discard fat in roasting pan. Cut apples into wedges. Arrange potatoes, carrots, and apples around chicken in the pan. Spoon glaze over poultry, vegetables, and apples. Roast for 15 to 20 minutes more or till chicken is no longer pink, the drumsticks move easily in their sockets, and the vegetables are tender. Makes 6 servings.

notes: Microwave directions available in original

recipes.title: Roast Herb Chicken
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Roasted chicken brushed with a tangy herb-lemon mixture.

ingredients.item: dried tarragon, oregano, basil, thyme, savory, or sage

instructions.text: Rinse chicken and pat dry. Skewer neck skin to back; tie legs to tail. Twist wings under back.
Place, breast side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Melt margarine or butter; stir in lemon juice and a herb or garlic. Brush over chicken.

Roast, uncovered, in a 375° oven for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours or till no longer pink and the drumsticks move easily in their sockets, brushing occasionally with drippings. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Makes 6 servings.

recipes.title: Honey and Spice Duckling
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Roasted duck with a sweet and spicy Szechwan pepper glaze.

ingredients.prep_note: coarsely ground, or 1 teaspoon whole pepper, coarsely ground

instructions.text: Rinse duck; pat dry. In a bowl combine pepper, salt, ginger, and five-spice powder. Sprinkle body cavity of duck with some of the salt mixture; rub remaining mixture on skin of duck. Skewer neck skin to back; tie legs to tail. Twist wing tips under back. Prick skin all over with a fork.

Place duckling, breast side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Roast in a 375° oven for 1 3/4 to 2 1/4 hours or till the drumsticks move easily in their sockets and duck is no longer pink, spooning off fat occasionally. Meanwhile, mix honey and soy sauce; baste duck with honey mixture once or twice during the last 10 minutes of roasting. Makes 3 or 4 servings.

recipes.title: Stuffed Cornish Game Hens
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant individual game hens stuffed with a savory bread stuffing and glazed with orange sauce.

instructions.text: Cook bacon till crisp. Remove bacon; drain and crumble. Cook carrot in drippings over medium heat till tender; remove from heat. Stir in bacon, parsley, savory, and pepper. Stir in bread cubes.
Dissolve the 1/4 teaspoon bouillon granules in 2 tablespoons hot water. Drizzle over bread mixture, tossing lightly.

Rinse hens; pat dry. Season cavities with salt. Lightly stuff hens with bread mixture. Pull neck skin, if present, to back of each hen. Twist wing tips under back, holding skin in place. Tie legs to tail.
Place hens, breast side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Brush with oil; cover loosely with foil. Roast in a 375° oven for 30 minutes.

Stir together wine, melted margarine or butter, and the 2 tablespoons orange juice; brush on hens. Roast hens, uncovered, about 1 hour more or till tender and no longer pink, brushing with wine mixture twice.

For sauce, add additional orange juice to remaining wine mixture to make 3/4 cup. In a small saucepan combine cornstarch, brown sugar, and the 1/2 teaspoon bouillon granules. Stir in wine mixture. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Serve sauce with hens. Makes 4 servings.

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Bread Stuffing
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic sage-seasoned bread stuffing for poultry.

ingredients.item: poultry seasoning or dried sage leaves

instructions.text: In a small saucepan cook celery and onion in margarine or butter till tender but not brown.
Stir in poultry seasoning or sage, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Place dry bread cubes in a bowl. Add onion mixture. Drizzle with enough broth or water to moisten, tossing lightly. Use to stuff one 8- to 10-pound turkey. Makes 8 to 10 servings.

notes: Microwave directions available in original
Variations: Mushroom Stuffing, Giblet Stuffing, Oyster Stuffing, Chestnut Stuffing, Peanut or Raisin Stuffing, Herb and Onion Stuffing

recipes.title: Harvest Stuffing
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Apple and walnut bread stuffing with wheat germ.

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook carrots, celery, and onion in margarine or butter till tender. Stir in nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.

In a bowl combine bread cubes, apple, walnuts, and wheat germ. Add carrot mixture. Drizzle with enough broth to moisten, tossing lightly. Use to stuff one 8- to 10-pound turkey. Makes 8 to 10 servings.

recipes.title: Corn Bread and Bacon Stuffing
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Southern-style stuffing with corn bread and bacon.

instructions.text: In a skillet cook chopped bacon, celery, and onion over medium heat till bacon is crisp and vegetables are tender. Do not drain.

Meanwhile, in a bowl combine eggs, parsley, poultry seasoning, and pepper. Add Corn Bread and bread cubes; toss lightly till mixed. Add bacon mixture. Drizzle with enough of the broth to moisten, tossing lightly till mixed. Use to stuff one 8- to 10-pound turkey or domestic goose. Makes 8 to 10 servings.

recipes.title: Wild Rice Stuffing
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Delicious nutty stuffing with wild rice, mushrooms, and almonds.

ingredients.item: toasted slivered almonds or pine nuts

instructions.text: Rinse wild rice in a strainer under cold water about 1 minute. In a medium saucepan combine wild rice, brown rice, bouillon granules, sage or nutmeg, and 1 cup water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat.

Cover and simmer for 45 minutes. Add mushrooms, celery, and green onions. Cook, covered, over medium-low heat for 10 to 20 minutes more or till vegetables are just tender, stirring frequently. Stir in nuts, if desired. Use to stuff one 2 1/2- to 3-pound broiler-fryer chicken. (Or, add 1/4 cup water and transfer to a 1-quart casserole. Bake in a 375° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.) Makes 6 servings.

notes: Apricot-Wild-Rice Stuffing variation available

recipes.title: Bulgur Pilaf Stuffing
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Hearty stuffing with bulgur wheat and turkey sausage.

ingredients.item: pork sausage or ground turkey sausage

instructions.text: In a small saucepan bring broth and Worcestershire sauce to boiling. Add bulgur. Remove from heat. Cover and let stand for 15 minutes.
In a medium skillet crumble sausage; add onion, celery, and carrot. Cook about 6 minutes or till sausage is no longer pink and vegetables are tender, stirring often to break up large pieces.
Drain. Stir in bulgur mixture. Use to stuff one 2 1/2- to 3-pound broiler-fryer chicken. Serves 6.

notes: Microwave directions available

recipes.title: Cream Gravy
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The perfect crowning touch for fried poultry.

instructions.text: After frying poultry, transfer poultry to a platter; keep warm. Reserve 2 tablespoons of the drippings in the skillet (discard remaining drippings).

Stir in flour, bouillon granules, and pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir over medium heat till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 1 minute more. If necessary, thin with a little additional milk. Makes 1 3/4 cups (6 or 7 servings).

missing_inputs: Not in database: fried poultry drippings

recipes.title: Pan Gravy
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic pan gravy made from roast poultry drippings.

instructions.text: After transferring roast poultry to a serving platter, pour pan drippings into a large measuring cup. Also scrape the browned bits into the cup.

Skim and reserve fat from drippings. Place 1/4 cup of the fat in a medium saucepan (discard remaining fat). Stir in flour. Add enough broth or water to remaining drippings in the measuring cup to equal 2 cups. Add all at once to flour mixture.
Cook and stir over medium heat till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Makes 2 cups (8 to 10 servings).

missing_inputs: Not in database: pan drippings from roast poultry
assumptions: Inferred 1.0 for chicken broth or water (standard quantity)

recipes.title: Giblet Gravy
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Rich gravy with chopped giblets for extra flavor.

ingredients.item: turkey or chicken giblets and neck
pan drippings from roast turkey or chicken

instructions.text: Rinse giblets and neck. Refrigerate liver till needed. In a medium saucepan combine remaining giblets, neck, celery, onion, and lightly salted water to cover. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 1 hour or till tender. Add liver; simmer 20 to 30 minutes more for turkey (5 to 10 minutes more for chicken) or till tender.
Remove and finely chop giblets. Discard neck bones. Strain broth. Discard vegetables. Chill chopped giblets and broth till needed.
After transferring roast turkey or chicken to a platter, pour pan drippings into a large measuring cup. Skim and reserve fat from pan drippings.

Pour 1/4 cup of the fat into the saucepan (discard remaining fat). Stir in flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Add reserved broth to the drippings to measure 1 1/2 cups. Add broth mixture all at once to flour mixture. Cook and stir till bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Stir in giblets. If desired, chop egg and stir in. Heat through. Makes 2 cups (8 to 10 servings).

assumptions: Inferred 1.0 for pan drippings from roast turkey or chicken (standard quantity)

recipes.title: Nut-Flavored Oil
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Homemade nut-infused oil to add zest to salads and dressings.

ingredients.item: unblanched shelled whole hazelnuts, almonds, or walnuts

instructions.text: To make flavored oil, place 1 1/2 cups unblanched shelled whole hazelnuts, almonds, or walnuts in a blender container or food processor. Cover; blend or process till chopped. With blender on slow speed, gradually add 1/2 cup salad oil through opening in lid. Blend till the nuts are finely chopped.

Transfer mixture to a small saucepan. Place a candy thermometer in the pan. Cook over low heat, stirring often, till thermometer registers 160°. Remove from heat; cool slightly. Combine mixture with 2 cups salad oil. Cover tightly; let stand in a cool place for 1 to 2 weeks.

Line a colander with several layers of cheesecloth. Pour mixture through colander; let drain in a bowl. Discard nut paste. Pour strained oil into a clean 1-pint jar; cover tightly. Store in the refrigerator up to 3 months. Makes 2 1/2 cups (forty 1-tablespoon servings).

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Chef's Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic main-dish salad with meat, cheese, and fresh vegetables.

ingredients.item: fully cooked ham, chicken, turkey, beef, pork, or lamb
cubed Swiss, cheddar, American, provolone, or Gruyère cheese or crumbled blue cheese

ingredients.prep_note: cut into wedges, or 8 cherry tomatoes, halved

ingredients.item: small green or sweet red pepper
Creamy French Dressing, Buttermilk Dressing, Creamy Italian Dressing, or other salad dressing

instructions.text: In a large salad bowl toss together lettuce and romaine or spinach. Arrange meat or poultry, cheese, hard-cooked eggs, tomatoes, pepper rings, and green onions over the greens.
Sprinkle with Croutons, if desired. Pour Creamy French Dressing or other salad dressing over all. Toss to coat. Makes 4 main-dish servings.

Note: To serve Chef's Salad as individual salads, toss together lettuce and romaine or spinach and divide among four individual salad bowls. Top each serving with one-fourth of the meat or poultry, cheese, hard-cooked eggs, tomatoes, pepper rings, and green onions. Sprinkle each with Croutons, if desired. Pass Creamy French Dressing or other salad dressing.

recipes.title: Taco Salads
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Tex-Mex salad served in crispy tortilla cups with seasoned meat and all the fixings.

ingredients.item: ground beef, ground raw turkey, or bulk pork sausage

instructions.text: For meat mixture, in a large skillet cook meat and garlic till meat is no longer pink. Drain off fat. Stir in undrained kidney beans, taco sauce, and chili powder. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover; simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, for salads, combine lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, green pepper, olives, and green onions. Add hot meat mixture. Toss to mix. Divide among Tortilla Cups or individual salad plates.
Garnish with avocado, if desired. Serve with sour cream and additional taco sauce or salsa, if desired. Makes 6 main-dish servings.

Tortilla Cups: In a heavy 3-quart saucepan heat 2 inches cooking oil or melted shortening for deep-fat frying to 375°. Place one 7-inch flour tortilla on top of hot oil. Using a metal ladle, press tortilla into fat, forming the tortilla into a cup. Fry for 40 to 60 seconds or till golden. Remove with tongs. Drain on paper towels. Repeat with five more tortillas.

notes: Microwave directions available for meat mixture

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Caesar Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The classic anchovy and Parmesan salad with homemade croutons.

ingredients.prep_note: one can, drained, rinsed, and patted dry

instructions.text: Allow egg to come to room temperature. To coddle egg, add egg in shell to a small saucepan of boiling water. Remove from heat; let stand 1 minute. Remove egg from water and cool slightly.

Cut garlic clove in half lengthwise. Rub a large wooden salad bowl with cut sides of the garlic clove. Discard garlic. Add oil, lemon or lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, and hot pepper sauce to bowl. Break the coddled egg into the bowl. Using a fork or a wire whisk, beat till creamy. Add romaine. Toss to coat. Sprinkle with croutons, Parmesan cheese, and pepper; toss to mix. Top with anchovy fillets. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

assumptions: Inferred 0.25 for bottled hot pepper sauce (standard quantity)

recipes.title: Three-Bean Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic marinated bean salad that keeps well in the refrigerator.

ingredients.item: cut wax beans or 8 1/2-ounce can lima beans

instructions.text: Combine wax beans, green beans, red kidney beans, onion, and green pepper. For dressing, in a screw-top jar combine vinegar, oil, sugar, celery seed, and garlic. Cover and shake well. Add to vegetables; stir lightly.
Cover; chill for 4 to 24 hours, stirring often. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

Creamy Three-Bean Salad: Prepare as above, except omit salad oil and sugar. For dressing, combine 1/2 cup mayonnaise or salad dressing, 1 tablespoon vinegar, celery seed, 1 teaspoon prepared mustard, and garlic.

notes: EASY recipe tag in cookbook
Store any leftovers in the refrigerator for up to three days

recipes.title: Coleslaw
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic creamy coleslaw with cabbage and carrots.

ingredients.item: small green or sweet red pepper

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine cabbage, carrot, green or sweet red pepper, and green onions. For dressing, stir together mayonnaise or salad dressing, vinegar, sugar, and celery seed. Pour the dressing over the cabbage mixture; toss to coat.
Cover and chill for 1 to 24 hours. Makes 4 side-dish servings.

Vinaigrette Coleslaw: Prepare as above, except substitute vinaigrette for dressing. For vinaigrette, in a screw-top jar combine 1/4 cup vinegar, 3 tablespoons salad oil, 2 to 3 tablespoons sugar, and, if desired, several dashes bottled hot pepper sauce. Cover and shake well.

Nutty Citrus Coleslaw: Prepare as above, except omit green onions. Add 1 small orange, peeled, sliced, and chopped; 1/4 cup chopped walnuts; and 2 tablespoons raisins to the cabbage mixture. Makes 5 side-dish servings.

notes: Variations: Vinaigrette Coleslaw, Nutty Citrus Coleslaw

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Tabbouleh
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: A classic Middle Eastern salad with bulgur (precooked cracked wheat).

instructions.text: Rinse bulgur in a colander with cold water. Drain. Combine bulgur, cucumber, parsley, and onions.
