recipes.title: Swedish Meatballs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 241
recipes.description: Classic Swedish meatballs in a creamy sauce, served over noodles.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine egg, 3/4 cup of the milk, the bread crumbs, onion, and the allspice or nutmeg. Add the ground beef or veal, pork, and parsley; mix well. Shape into 30 meatballs.
Place meatballs in a 15x10x1-inch baking pan. Bake in a 375° oven for 15 to 20 minutes or till no pink remains. Drain.

Meanwhile, in a medium saucepan combine remaining milk and bouillon granules. Stir in flour. Cook and stir over medium heat till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 1 minute more. Stir in sour cream; heat through (do not boil).
Pour sauce over meatballs. Serve over noodles. Makes 4 to 6 servings.

notes: Microwave directions: In a mixing bowl combine egg, 1/4 cup of the milk, the bread crumbs, onion, parsley, the 1/4 teaspoon allspice or nutmeg. Add meat; mix well. Shape into 30 meatballs. Place in a 2-quart casserole. Micro-cook, covered, on 100% power (high) for 6 to 8 minutes or till no pink remains, turning meatballs and rearranging once. Drain meatballs on paper towels. Rearrange meatballs in dish. For sauce, in a 1 1/2-quart casserole stir remaining milk, bouillon granules, flour, and 1/4 teaspoon allspice. Micro-cook on high for 3 1/2 to 5 1/2 minutes or till thickened, stirring every minute. Add sour cream; micro-cook 40 to 50 seconds or till heated through, stirring once. Drain meatballs. Pour sauce over meatballs.

recipes.title: Spaghetti Sauce
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 242
recipes.description: Classic Italian-American meat sauce for spaghetti.

instructions.text: In Dutch oven cook meat, onion, green pepper, and celery till meat is brown. Drain. Stir in undrained tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, sugar, oregano, basil, bay leaf, and garlic. Bring to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer about 30 minutes or till desired consistency. Discard bay leaf. Serve over hot pasta. Serves 6.

Microwave directions: In a 3-quart casserole combine meat, onion, green pepper, and garlic on 100% power (high) for 6 to 8 minutes or till no pink remains, stirring twice. Drain. Stir in remaining ingredients except pasta. Micro-cook, covered, on high 6 to 8 minutes or till mixture bubbles, stirring once. Discard bay leaf. Serve over pasta. Makes 6 servings.

recipes.title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 242
recipes.description: Classic spaghetti with homemade meatballs in tomato sauce.

instructions.text: Combine egg, bread crumbs, 2 tablespoons water, and pepper. Add ground beef and Italian sausage; mix well. Shape into 48 meatballs.

In a skillet heat oil. Add half the meatballs at a time; cook until brown. Drain. Meanwhile, combine onion, green pepper, and mushrooms, cooking until mushrooms are soft, and oregano, basil, and fennel, bay leaf. Stir in tomatoes, tomato paste, water, sugar.
Simmer, uncovered, about 20 minutes or till of desired consistency. Discard bay leaf. Serve over spaghetti. Makes 8 servings.

recipes.title: Porcupine Meatballs
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 242
recipes.description: Meatballs with rice that stick out like porcupine quills when cooked, in tomato sauce.

instructions.text: Combine egg, 1/4 cup of the soup, uncooked rice, onion, Worcestershire, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Add beef; mix well. Shape meat mixture into 20 meatballs. Place in a large skillet.

Mix the remaining soup and water; pour over meatballs. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes or till rice is tender. Stir sauce; spoon over meatballs to serve. Makes 4 servings.

Microwave directions: Combine egg, 1/4 cup of the soup, rice, onion, Worcestershire, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Add beef; mix well. Shape into 20 meatballs. Place in an 8x8x2-inch baking dish, covering with 1/2 cup soup and water; pour over. Micro-cook on 100% power (high) for 6 minutes. Rearrange meatballs. Add remaining soup mixture. Micro-cook, covered, on high 10 minutes more. Let stand, covered, 5 minutes. Stir sauce; spoon over meatballs. Serve.

recipes.title: Hamburgers
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 243
recipes.description: Classic homemade hamburgers with multiple flavor variations.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine egg, bread crumbs, onion, milk, mustard or horseradish, salt, and pepper. Add meat; mix well. Shape meat mixture into four 3/4-inch-thick patties.

Place patties on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from the heat for 6 minutes. Turn; broil 6 to 8 minutes more for medium. (Or, place patties in an unheated skillet. Cook, uncovered, over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes for medium. Turn patties after half the cooking time.)
Serve patties on buns with remaining catsup, mayonnaise or salad dressing, lettuce. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Cheeseburgers: Prepare as above, except add 1/4 cup shredded cheddar, Swiss, or Monterey Jack cheese or 1/4 cup crumbled blue cheese to egg mixture.
Italian-Style Burgers: Prepare as above, except substitute 1 tablespoon tomato paste for mustard. Stir in 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano.
Mexican-Style Burgers: Prepare as above, except substitute salsa or taco sauce for the milk. Serve with lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and shredded cheese.
Greek-Style Burgers: Prepare as above, except substitute plain yogurt for the milk and 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano, crushed, or 1/4 teaspoon cracked wheat for bread crumbs.
Indian-Style Burgers: Prepare as above, except add additional plain yogurt and 1 teaspoon curry powder with the bread crumbs.

recipes.title: German-Style Burgers
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 243
recipes.description: Hamburgers seasoned German-style with caraway.

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine egg, rye bread crumbs, onion, mustard, and caraway seed. Add meat; mix well. Shape mixture into four 3/4-inch-thick patties.
Place patties on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from the heat for 6 minutes. Turn; broil 6 to 8 minutes more. Serve on buns.

recipes.title: Stuffed Burgers
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 244
recipes.description: Hamburger patties stuffed with a savory filling.

ingredients.item: ground beef, veal, or ground lamb
shredded zucchini, carrots, or 1/4 cup shredded cheese

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine bread crumbs, basil, onion salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add meat; mix well. Shape mixture into eight thin patties.

For filling, combine olives and zucchini, carrots, or cheese. Place about 1 tablespoon filling atop each of 4 patties. Spread to within 1/4 inch of edges. Top with remaining patties; seal edges. Place patties on the unheated rack of a broiler pan.
Broil 4 inches from the heat for 6 minutes. Turn patties; broil 6 to 8 minutes more or till no pink remains. Serve on buns. Makes 4 servings.

recipes.title: Garden Burgers
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 244
recipes.description: Hamburgers with vegetables mixed in and topped with fresh garden toppings.

ingredients.item: parsley or pepper, shredded hash brown potatoes or shredded zucchini

instructions.text: Combine egg, the 3 tablespoons catsup, the basil, onion salt, and pepper. Stir in hash browns or zucchini and bread crumbs. Add meat; mix well. Shape into four 3/4-inch-thick patties.
Place patties on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from the heat for 15 to 18 minutes or till no pink remains, turning once. Brush with barbecue sauce or catsup before serving.
Serve patties on buns with additional catsup, mayonnaise, lettuce. Makes 4 servings.

assumptions: Inferred 1.0 for ground pork or ground lamb (standard quantity)
Assumed 1 unit for barbecue sauce or catsup

recipes.title: Glazed Ham Patties
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 244
recipes.description: Sweet-glazed ham patties with raisins and apricots.

instructions.text: Combine egg, bread crumbs, raisins, if desired, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add meat and the 1/4 cup onion; mix well. Shape mixture into four 1/2-inch-thick patties.
In a greased 8x8x2-inch baking dish layer 8 bread-slice halves, the cheese slices, then the remaining bread-slice halves. Beat eggs; stir in milk. Stir in orange juice or water. Spoon over patties.
Bake in a 375° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or till juices run clear. Stir glaze; spoon over patties. Makes 4 servings.

recipes.title: Tacos
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 245
recipes.description: Classic ground beef tacos with traditional toppings.

instructions.text: Heat taco shells according to package directions. In a large skillet cook meat and onion till meat is brown. Drain fat.
Stir in undrained tomatoes. Add chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 5 to 10 minutes or till of desired consistency.
Spoon meat mixture into taco shells. Top with lettuce, cheese, tomato, and, if desired, sour cream and/or guacamole. Makes 12 tacos (6 servings).

recipes.title: Burritos
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 245
recipes.description: Flour tortillas filled with seasoned beef, beans, and cheese.

ingredients.item: shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook meat, onion, and garlic till meat is brown. Drain fat. Stir in refried beans, salsa or taco sauce, and chili powder.

Wrap tortillas tightly in foil and heat in a 350° oven about 10 minutes to soften. (Or, wrap tortillas in microwave-safe paper towels. Micro-cook on 100% power (high) for 30 to 45 seconds or till softened.)
Spoon about 1/2 cup of the meat mixture onto each tortilla just below center. Top with cheese. Fold bottom edge of each tortilla up and over filling. Fold in opposite sides; roll up from the bottom.
Arrange burritos, seam side down, on a baking sheet. Bake in a 350° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or till heated through. If desired, serve with sour cream, salsa, and/or guacamole. Serves 6.

notes: Chimichangas: Prepare as above, except wrap tortillas tightly in foil and heat in a 350° oven for about 10 minutes to soften. Fold up the tortilla. In a skillet fry filled tortillas, two or three at a time, in 1 inch of hot oil, starting from the bottom. Secure heat 1 inch of cooking oil for deep-fat frying to 375°. Fry filled tortillas, two or three at a time, about 1 minute on each side or till crisp and golden brown. Drain on paper towels. Keep warm while frying others. Remove wooden picks. Serve chimichangas warm on lettuce and top with tomatoes and cheese. If desired, pass sour cream and guacamole. Do not use microwave directions.

recipes.title: Sloppy Joes
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 245
recipes.description: Classic loose-meat sandwich with a tangy tomato-based sauce.

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook meat, onion, and green pepper till meat is brown. Drain fat. Stir in catsup, water, Worcestershire sauce, and chili powder. Bring to boiling; reduce heat.
Simmer, uncovered, for 5 to 10 minutes or till of desired consistency, stirring occasionally.
Spoon meat mixture onto buns. Makes 6 servings.

notes: Microwave directions: In a 1 1/2-quart casserole combine meat, onion, and green pepper. Micro-cook on 100% power (high) for 4 to 6 minutes or till no pink remains, stirring once. Drain. Stir in catsup, water, Worcestershire sauce, and chili powder. Micro-cook, covered, on high for 2 to 3 minutes or till bubbly. Serve on buns.

recipes.title: Lasagna
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 246
recipes.description: Classic layered pasta with meat sauce and cheese, for a cheesy, vegetarian version see page 159.

ingredients.item: ground beef, pork, or bulk Italian sausage
ricotta cheese or cream-style cottage cheese

instructions.text: For meat sauce, in a large saucepan cook meat, onion, and garlic till meat is brown and onion is tender. Drain fat. Stir in undrained tomatoes, tomato sauce, oregano, basil, fennel, if desired, salt, and pepper. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 15 to 20 minutes or till slightly thickened, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, cook lasagna noodles according to package directions. Drain noodles; rinse with cold water. Drain again.
For filling, combine eggs, ricotta or cottage cheese, Parmesan or Romano cheese, and parsley.
Layer half of the cooked noodles in a 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. Spread with half of the filling. Top with half of the meat sauce and half of the mozzarella cheese. Repeat layers.
Bake in a 375° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or till heated through. Let stand 10 minutes before serving. Makes 8 servings.
To make ahead: Prepare as above, except after assembling, cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours. Uncover and bake in a 375° oven about 35 minutes more or till heated through.

recipes.title: Pizza
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 247
recipes.description: Homemade pizza with yeast crust and your choice of toppings.

instructions.text: In a large bowl combine 1 1/4 cups of the flour, the yeast, and salt. Add warm water and oil.
Beat with an electric mixer on low speed for 30 seconds, scraping the bowl constantly. Beat on high speed for 3 minutes. Using a wooden spoon, stir in as much of the remaining flour as you can.

Turn out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead in enough of the remaining flour to make a moderately stiff dough that is smooth and elastic (6 to 8 minutes total). Divide dough in half. Cover; let rest 10 minutes.

Grease two 12-inch pizza pans or baking sheets. On a lightly floured surface, roll each half of dough into a 13-inch circle. Transfer to pans. Build up edges slightly. Do not let rise. Bake in a 425° oven about 12 minutes or till lightly browned.
Spread Pizza Sauce over hot crusts. Top with desired meat, vegetables, and cheese. Bake in a 425° oven for 10 to 15 minutes more or till bubbly. Makes 2 pizzas (8 servings).

notes: Thin Pizzas: Make pizza dough as above. Grease two baking sheets. On a lightly floured surface, roll each half of dough into a 13-inch circle. Transfer to pans or baking sheets. If desired, sprinkle each crust with cornmeal. On a lightly floured surface, roll each half of dough edges slightly. Do not let rise. Bake in a 425° oven about 10 minutes or till lightly browned. Spread Pizza Sauce over hot crusts. Top as desired. Bake about 8 minutes more or till bubbly. Makes 2 thin pizzas.

Pan Pizzas: Grease two 11x7x1 1/2-inch or 9x9x2-inch baking pans or two 12-inch pizza pans. If desired, sprinkle with cornmeal. With greased hands, pat dough into bottoms and halfway up sides of prepared pans. Cover; let rise halfway (30 to 45 minutes). Bake in a 375° oven 20 to 25 minutes or till lightly browned. Meanwhile, prepare Pizza Sauce. Spread Pizza Sauce over hot crusts. Top as desired. Bake 15 to 20 minutes more or till bubbly. Serves 8.

Pizza Sauce: In a medium saucepan combine one undrained 7 1/2-ounce can tomatoes, cut up, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 tablespoon dried crushed oregano, 1 teaspoon crushed dried basil, 1/4 teaspoon crushed fennel seed (optional), 1/4 teaspoon crushed hot red pepper (optional), and 1 clove garlic, minced. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, about 30 minutes or till thick enough to spread on pizza. Makes about 1 cup.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Calzones
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 247
recipes.description: Folded pizza pockets stuffed with meat, vegetables, and cheese.

instructions.text: Prepare pizza dough. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Add meat, mushrooms, green pepper, and olives to sauce.
Divide dough into 4 portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll each portion into a 7-inch circle.

Spread about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture onto half of each circle to within 1/2 inch of the edge. Sprinkle mozzarella and Parmesan over meat mixture. Fold dough in half over filling. Fold edges to seal; cut slits in top of dough to allow steam to escape.
Bake in a 375° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or till golden. Makes 4 servings.

recipes.title: Kitchen Tip: How to Knead Bread
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook
recipes.description: Learn the proper technique for kneading bread dough.

instructions.text: Kneading should be done on a lightly floured surface, a board or counter top; add a little more flour if the dough remains sticky. Knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic; it should have tiny air bubbles under the surface.
Turn the dough on to a lightly floured board or counter top. With lightly floured hands, shape the dough into a ball and fold it toward you.
With the heels of hands, using a rolling motion, push it away. Give dough a quarter of a turn.
Knead 8 to 10 minutes; dough should no longer stick and will be ready for second rising or shaping, as recipe directs.

recipes.title: Kitchen Tip: Judging Ground Meat Doneness
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 244
recipes.description: Safety guidelines for cooking ground meat to proper doneness.

instructions.text: For safety's sake, we recommend cooking all meat loaves and meatloaf-type ground-meat patties to 170° or till no pink remains.
Ground-meat patties, with no other ingredients added, however, may be cooked till their centers are brownish pink (medium doneness).

recipes.title: Kitchen Tip: Candy Temperature Stages
recipes.source_note: Better Homes and Gardens New Cookbook, page 93
recipes.description: Guide to the different temperature stages when making candy.

instructions.text: Thread stage (230° to 233°): When a teaspoon is dipped into the hot mixture, then removed, the candy falls off the spoon in a fine, thin thread.
Soft-ball stage (234° to 240°): When the ball of candy is removed from the cold water, the candy instantly flattens and runs between your fingers.
Firm-ball stage (244° to 248°): When the ball of candy is removed from the water, it is firm enough to hold its shape, but quickly flattens at room temperature.
Hard-ball stage (250° to 266°): When the ball of candy is removed from the water, it doesn't flatten until pressed.
Soft-crack stage (270° to 290°): When dropped into water, the candy separates into hard, but pliable and elastic, threads.
Hard-crack stage (295° to 310°): When dropped into water, the candy separates into hard, brittle threads that snap easily.

notes: Always use a candy thermometer for best results
The water test is a backup method if you don't own a candy thermometer

recipes.title: Catsup
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The tomato flavor comes through in this homemade ketchup

instructions.text: In a saucepan combine vinegar, stick cinnamon, cloves, and celery seed; bring to boiling. Remove from heat.
Wash, core, and quarter tomatoes. Drain in a colander; discard liquid. Place tomatoes in an 8- or 10-quart kettle or Dutch oven. Add onion. Bring to boiling. Cook 15 minutes, stirring often.
Rinse through a food mill or sieve; discard seeds. Return puree to kettle; add sugar, salt, and ground red pepper. Bring to boiling.
Strain vinegar mixture into tomato mixture; stir. Simmer for 1-1/2 to 2 hours or till reduced by half, stirring occasionally.
Ladle catsup into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 10 minutes.
May refrigerate up to 1 month. Makes 4 half-pints.

recipes.title: Dill Pickles

Cut off a slice from stem end of cucumbers. Pack cucumbers into hot, sterilized jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace.
Combine water, vinegar, and pickling salt. Bring to boiling.
Pour hot liquid over cucumbers, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Add dill and mustard seed. Adjust lids.
Process in a boiling-water canner.

Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Corn Relish
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Fresh corn relish for canning

instructions.text: Cut corn from cobs (do not scrape cobs). Measure 6 cups corn.
In an 8- or 10-quart kettle or Dutch oven combine corn and 2 cups water.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, covered, about 12 minutes or till nearly tender.
Add celery, red pepper, and green pepper, and onion. Stir in 2 cups vinegar, sugar, pickling salt, and celery seed. Return to boiling.
Boil, uncovered, 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir together remaining vinegar, flour, dry mustard, and turmeric.
Add to corn mixture. Cook and stir till bubbly; cook 1 minute more.
Ladle into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Vegetable Relish

Place ground vegetable mixture in a colander. Let stand overnight. Drain well with plastic wrap. Place in a container.
Add salt. Bring to boiling, stirring often. Reduce heat. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat. Return mixture to ground vegetable mixture to boiling, stirring often. Stir in sugar, vinegar, water, thyme, and pepper. Bring to boiling.
Boiling-Water Canning: Ladle hot vegetables into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in a boiling-water canner for 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Jellies and Jams Tips
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Guide to making jellies and jams including terms and techniques
notes: Jelly making is one canning project you can do year-round. By using either fresh produce or frozen jams, jellies, and products, your family can enjoy your delicious creations for gift giving.
EQUIPMENT: You'll need a large kettle or pot to prevent the mixture from boiling over. To allow for vigorous boiling, the pan should have more than three-fourths of its capacity.

Canning is often done in a boiling-water canner. If you don't have a metal produce basket, before starting, be sure to sterilize the length of the jars by dipping each one in boiling water for at least 15 minutes.
TERMS TO KNOW:
Full Rolling Boil: A boil that is so rapid you can't stir it down with a spoon.

Sheets Off the Spoon: A test for the jelled point. Dip a metal spoon into the boiling mixture, then hold it over the kettle. When two drops come together and fall off together as one sheet, the jelly is ready.

Pectin: A substance in some fruits, especially underripe fruits, that makes the jelly gel or set. Powdered liquid, or sugar mixture that can be used or purchased. Some commercial pectins are added for a recipe if the fruit doesn't have enough natural pectin to gel. Be sure to use the type of pectin called for.

recipes.title: Fruit-Juice Jelly

recipes.description: Easy jelly made from unsweetened fruit juice

instructions.text: Pour fruit juice into a large kettle. (If using fresh apple juice, strain it through cheesecloth first.) Add 1/4 cup lemon juice and powdered pectin.
Bring to full rolling boil, stirring constantly. Stir in sugar. Return to full rolling boil; boil hard 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat; quickly skim off foam with metal spoon.
Ladle into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in boiling-water canner for 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Peach Jam
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic homemade peach jam

instructions.text: Peel, pit, and coarsely grind or mash peaches. Measure 4 cups.
In an 8- or 10-quart kettle combine peaches, pectin, and lemon juice. Stir in sugar.
Bring to full rolling boil, stirring constantly. Stir in sugar.
Return to full rolling boil; boil hard 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat; quickly skim off foam with a metal spoon. Ladle into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace.
Adjust lids. Process in boiling-water canner for 5 minutes.

Peach-Berry Jam: Prepare as above except reduce peaches to 2 pounds (3 cups ground).

recipes.title: Grape Jam
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Homemade Concord grape jam

instructions.text: Wash and stem grapes. Measure 10 cups. Remove skins from half of the grapes by squeezing each grape between fingers.
In a large kettle cook skinned grapes, covered, about 10 minutes or till very soft. Strain into a bowl, pressing to extract juice. Discard seeds.
Add unskinned grapes and their skins to cooked pulp. Cook and stir over low heat about 10 minutes or till skins are tender.
Stir in sugar. Bring to full rolling boil, stirring often. Boil hard, uncovered, for 10 to 12 minutes or till mixture sheets off a metal spoon or jam reaches 220°F.
Remove from heat; quickly skim off foam. Ladle hot jam at once into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace.
Process in a boiling-water canner for 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Orange Marmalade
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic citrus marmalade

instructions.text: Score orange and lemon peels into 4 lengthwise sections. Remove peels. Scrape off white portions from peels; discard.
Cut peels into very thin strips. Bring to boiling. Combine peels, water, and baking soda. Bring to boiling.
Cover; simmer for 20 minutes. Do not drain. Section fruits. Add fruit and juices to peel mixture. Return to boiling.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes. Measure 3 cups fruit mixture. Return to kettle or combine 3 cups fruit and sugar in an 8- or 10-quart kettle.
Bring to full rolling boil, stirring constantly. Add pectin. Return to full rolling boil; boil hard 1 minute. Remove from heat; skim off foam.
Ladle into hot, sterilized half-pint jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. (May take 2 weeks to set.)
Process in boiling-water canner for 15 minutes. Adjust lids.

recipes.title: Rhubarb-Raspberry Jam
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Tangy-sweet rhubarb and raspberry combination

ingredients.item: frozen loose-pack raspberries or one 12-ounce package frozen raspberries

instructions.text: In a large Dutch oven combine rhubarb and sugar. Let stand 20 minutes.
Bring to boiling, stirring frequently. Boil hard for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add raspberries. Return to full rolling boil; boil 5 to 6 minutes or till thick, stirring frequently.
Remove from heat. Add gelatin; stir till dissolved.
Ladle into hot, sterilized half-pint jars or freezer containers, leaving a 1/4-inch headspace. Seal, label. Let stand at room temperature about 2 hours or till jam is set.
Store up to 3 weeks in the refrigerator or 1 year in the freezer.

recipes.title: Berry Freezer Jam

recipes.description: Quick no-cook freezer jam with fresh berries

Combine pectin and lemon juice. Add to berry mixture, stirring for 3 minutes.
Ladle at once into jars or freezer containers, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace. Let stand at room temperature about 2 hours or till jam is set.
Store up to 3 weeks in the refrigerator or 1 year in the freezer.

recipes.title: Harvest Applesauce
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Homemade applesauce with cinnamon

instructions.text: In a large kettle combine apples, water, and, if desired, stick cinnamon.

Return pulp to kettle. Stir in sugar. (If desired, add 1/2 cup butter, stirring till melted.) Bring to boiling.

recipes.title: Apple Butter
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Spiced apple butter spread

instructions.text: In an 8- or 10-quart kettle or Dutch oven combine apples and cider or juice.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, covered, about 30 minutes or till very tender, stirring occasionally.
Press through a food mill or sieve. Return pulp to kettle (you should have about 15 cups).
Stir in sugar, cinnamon, and allspice. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for about 2 hours or till very thick, stirring often.
Boiling-Water Canning: Spoon hot apple butter into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving a 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust lids. Process in boiling-water canner for 5 minutes.
Freezing: Cool apple butter. Place kettle in a sink of ice water to cool apple butter quickly, leaving the recommended headspace. Seal, label, and freeze.

recipes.title: Meat Chapter Introduction & Tips
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Introduction to cooking meat with tips on recognizing cuts, handling, and storing
notes: Whether for grilling, braising, roasting, or micro-cooking, the recipes on the following pages bring out the best in beef, veal, pork, and lamb.

RECOGNIZING MEAT CUTS: Our recipes list the most common names for meat cuts. Your butcher, however, may use different names. To be sure you're buying the right cut of meat, refer to the identification pictures in this chapter. Also on these pages, we list the best ways to cook each cut of meat.
HANDLING AND STORING MEAT: Be sure to follow these rules for meat safety:
- Freeze raw meats you don't plan to use in one to two days. Wrap meats in freezer paper or bags.
- Thaw meat overnight in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
- Thoroughly wash your hands and utensils after handling raw meat.
- Never leave raw or cooked meat at room temperature for more than two hours.

USE THE HOT LINE: Do you have questions about storing and preparing meat? Call the toll-free Meat and Poultry Hotline (800) 535-4555. Home economists from the U.S. Department of Agriculture answer calls from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. eastern time.

recipes.title: How Much Meat to Buy Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Guide for calculating meat portions per person
notes: When buying meat, remember that cuts with the smallest amount of bone and fat yield more servings per pound. The servings per pound listed on this chart will help you get what you need from meat with different amounts of bone.
Type of Meat / Servings Per Pound:
Boneless meat (ground meats, boneless roasts and steaks, boneless cubes) - 4 or 5 servings
Cuts with little bone (beef and lamb rib roasts, veal or lamb) - 3 or 4 servings
Cuts with much bone (round or bone-in chuck roasts, ham, lamb or beef ribs, rib or loin chops) - 2 or 3 servings

recipes.title: How to Use a Meat Thermometer
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Guide to using a meat thermometer for perfect results
notes: You'll be guaranteed perfect roasts every time if you use a meat thermometer. It's the only accurate way to check doneness.
To be sure you get accurate readings, be sure the thermometer is inserted into the thickest part of the meat without touching fat or bone.
Steps to use a meat thermometer:
1. Push the thermometer into the thickest part of the roast, avoiding fat and bone.
2. The thermometer should register the internal temperature.
3. Continue cooking if the temperature hasn't reached the desired doneness.
4. When the roast reaches 5 to 10 degrees below the desired final temperature, remove it from the oven. The internal temperature will continue to rise as the roast stands.
5. Let roast stand for 15 minutes before carving.

recipes.title: Beef Wellington
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant beef tenderloin wrapped in puff pastry with liver pâté

ingredients.item: liver pâté or canned liver pâté

instructions.text: If roast is long and narrow, fold narrow ends under and tie. If roast is flat and wide, tie crosswise in 2 or 3 places to form a round, thick roast. (Final meat should be about 7x3x3 inches.) Remove from oven.
Wrap in foil in a shallow pan. Roast in a 425° oven about 25 minutes or till rare (120°). Remove from oven.

Meanwhile, for pastry, combine flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cut in shortening till pieces are the size of small peas. Combine egg yolks and water. Add to flour mixture, tossing with a fork till all is moistened. Form into a ball.

On floured surface, roll pastry into a 14x12-inch rectangle. Spread pâté to within 1-1/2 inches of edges. Center meat atop pastry. Wrap pastry around meat. Trim excess pastry from ends; fold up and seal. Brush with beaten egg white.
Place seam side down. Bake in a golden brown, Serve with Bordelaise Sauce.

Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. Remove bay leaf. Stir together 3 tablespoons softened margarine and 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour; stir into broth. Cook and stir for 1 minute more. Stir in 1 tablespoon snipped parsley.

recipes.title: Vegetable-Stuffed Rolled Roast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Beef eye round roast stuffed with vegetables

instructions.text: To butterfly the roast, make a single lengthwise cut down the center of the meat, cutting to within 1/2 inch of the other side. Spread the meat open.

recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic braised beef steak with tomatoes

instructions.text: Cut meat into 4 serving-size pieces.
Combine flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. With a meat mallet, pound flour mixture into meat.

In a large skillet brown meat on both sides in hot oil. Drain fat. Add undrained tomatoes, onion, celery, carrot, and thyme. Cover; cook over low heat about 1-1/4 hours or till meat is tender. Skim fat. Serve with hot rice or noodles.

Crockery-cooker directions: Cut meat into 4 pieces. Brown meat in hot oil in a 3-1/2- or 4-quart electric slow cooker. Sprinkle with thyme, 2 tablespoons quick-cooking tapioca, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Add tomatoes over vegetables. Pour undrained tomatoes over all. Cover; cook on low-heat setting for 10 to 12 hours. Oven directions: Cut meat into 4 pieces. Transfer meat to an 8x8x2-inch baking dish. In the same skillet combine undrained tomatoes, onion, celery, carrot, and thyme. Bring to boiling; scraping up any browned bits in the pan. Pour over meat. Cover and bake in a 350° oven about 1 hour or till tender. Continue as above.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Steak and Spinach Pinwheels
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant beef pinwheels stuffed with spinach and bacon

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook bacon till just done but not crisp. Drain on paper towels. Score steak by making shallow diagonal cuts at 1-inch intervals in a diamond pattern. Repeat on second side. With a meat mallet, pound steak into a 12x8-inch rectangle, working from center.
To edges: Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Arrange bacon lengthwise on steak. Spread spinach on bacon. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Roll up from a short side. Secure with wooden picks at 1-inch intervals, starting 1/2 inch from one end. Cut between picks into eight 1-inch slices.

Place cut side down on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from the heat for 6 minutes. Turn; broil for 6 to 8 minutes more for medium doneness. Remove picks. If desired, serve with Mock Hollandaise Sauce.
Grill directions: Prepare meat as above. Grill slices on an uncovered grill directly over medium coals for 6 minutes, allowing 6 to 8 minutes per side for medium. Serve as above.

notes: Score the steak by making shallow diagonal cuts about 1 inch apart in a diamond pattern
Using a sharp knife, cut the meat roll between the picks into eight 1-inch slices

missing_inputs: Not in database: Mock Hollandaise Sauce

recipes.title: London Broil
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic flank steak broiled and sliced thin

instructions.text: Score meat by making shallow diagonal cuts at 1-inch intervals in a diamond pattern on both sides.
Place meat in a plastic bag. For marinade, combine oil, vinegar, and garlic; pour over meat. Marinate at room temperature for 1 hour or in refrigerator for 4 to 24 hours.
Remove meat from marinade. Pat dry. Place on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 to 4 inches from heat for 6 minutes. Turn; broil 5 to 6 minutes more for medium doneness.
To serve, thinly slice diagonally across the grain.

recipes.title: Pepper-Rubbed Steaks
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Steaks with cracked pepper crust and brandy cream sauce

ingredients.item: beef top loin or tenderloin steaks

instructions.text: Slash fat on edges of steaks at 1-inch intervals. Sprinkle pepper onto surface of steaks. In a 12-inch skillet melt margarine. Cook steaks over medium-high heat for 7 to 9 minutes for medium-rare, turning once. Remove meat. Gradually reduce heat.

Stir in brandy, stirring to scrape up crusty browned bits. Stir cream into skillet. Cook for 1 minute on low heat. Bring to boiling. Reduce heat. Simmer for 1-1/2 to 2-1/2 minutes or till slightly thickened. Pour over steaks. Serves 4.

recipes.title: French Onion Sandwiches
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Open-faced steak sandwiches with melted Swiss cheese

instructions.text: In a large skillet melt margarine. Add steaks and garlic. Cook over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Place steak slices on French bread. Sprinkle with Swiss cheese. Broil 3 inches from heat till cheese melts. Serves 4.

assumptions: Inferred 2 for London Broil steak slices (standard quantity)
Estimated 4 servings based on total calories

recipes.title: Veal Cordon Bleu
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic veal cutlets stuffed with ham and Swiss cheese

instructions.text: Cut ham into strips. Cut veal into 4 pieces. With a meat mallet, pound each piece to 1/4-inch thickness. Place some ham in center of each veal piece, then overlap each piece with wooden picks.

Combine bread crumbs, parsley, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Roll meat bundles in flour, egg, then crumb mixture. In a large skillet melt margarine. Cook meat bundles over medium heat for 14 to 17 minutes or till golden brown, turning occasionally.

Oven directions: Prepare meat bundles as above. In a large skillet brown meat bundles in melted margarine for 5 minutes. Transfer to a 12x7-1/2x2-inch baking dish. Bake in a 400° oven for 18 to 20 minutes or till done.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Veal Marsala
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic Italian veal cutlets with Marsala wine sauce

ingredients.item: boneless veal leg top round steak

instructions.text: Cut veal into 4 pieces. With a meat mallet, pound each piece to 1/4-inch thickness. If desired, sprinkle with salt and pepper.

In a large skillet cook mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of the margarine till tender; keep warm on each side of the veal over medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon of the veal over medium heat for 2 minutes on each side. Remove veal; keep warm.
Add remaining margarine, sherry, and bouillon granules to skillet. Bring to boiling. Cook, stirring rapidly, for 3 minutes. Stir in parsley.
Pour over veal. If desired, serve with hot cooked noodles.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Beef Fajitas
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Serve the most sizzling hot for a typical South Texas flair

ingredients.item: boneless beef plate skirt steak, beef flank steak, or beef round steak

ingredients.prep_note: (see recipe, page 13) or dairy sour cream (optional)

ingredients.item: Shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese

instructions.text: Partially freeze beef. Thinly slice across the grain into bite-size strips. Place strips in a plastic bag set into a deep bowl. For marinade, in a mixing bowl combine the 1/2 cup Salsa, the lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce. Pour mixture over beef. Seal bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 6 to 24 hours, stirring occasionally.

Wrap tortillas in foil. Meanwhile, in a 350° oven for 10 minutes to soften. Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add oil. Cook and stir onion and sweet pepper strips in hot oil for 1-1/2 minutes. Add beef, cook and stir about 1-1/2 minutes or till crisp-tender. Remove vegetables from skillet.
Add half of the beef to the hot skillet. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till done. Remove beef. Repeat with remaining beef and vegetables to the hot skillet. Add 1/2 cup Salsa; heat through.
To serve, immediately fill warm tortillas with beef-vegetable mixture. If desired, add Guacamole or avocado dip, sour cream, cheese, and additional Salsa. Roll up fajitas. Makes 4 servings.

notes: Marinating the Easy Way: Marinating is a cinch if you use a plastic bag. The meat stays in the marinade and it's easy to turn and rearrange. Cleanup is easy, too. Just toss the bag.

assumptions: Inferred 1.0 for Shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese (standard quantity)

recipes.title: Beef Stroganoff
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic Russian-inspired beef in sour cream sauce

ingredients.item: beef tenderloin steak or sirloin steak

instructions.text: Partially freeze beef. Thinly slice across the grain into bite-size strips. Combine flour and sour cream; set aside.

In a large skillet cook mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of the margarine till tender. Remove mushrooms. Add remaining margarine. Add half of the beef to hot skillet. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till done. Remove beef. Repeat with remaining beef.
Add 3/4 cup water and bouillon granules to skillet. Stir in sour cream mixture. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more.
Return beef and mushrooms to skillet. Heat through. Serve over hot cooked noodles. Serves 4.

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for hot cooked noodles

recipes.title: Beef Teriyaki Kabobs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Grilled beef kabobs with teriyaki marinade

instructions.text: Partially freeze beef. Thinly slice across the grain into long strips. For marinade, combine soy sauce, sherry, molasses, applesauce, gingerroot, and garlic. Pour over meat.
Marinate for 15 minutes at room temperature. Or, 8 hours in refrigerator, reserving marinade.
Drain meat, reserving marinade. Thread accordion-style on skewers.
Place skewers on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from the heat for 5 to 6 minutes or to desired doneness, turning and brushing occasionally with marinade.
Grill directions: Cut, marinate, and skewer meat as above. Place on uncovered grill directly over hot coals 5 to 6 minutes, turning and brush with marinade often.

recipes.title: Ginger-Beef Stir-Fry
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Quick Asian-style beef stir-fry with ginger

ingredients.item: beef top round steak or sirloin steak

instructions.text: Thaw pea pods. Partially freeze beef. Thinly slice across the grain into bite-size strips. For sauce, combine sherry, soy sauce, cornstarch, and gingerroot.
In a wok or large skillet stir-fry carrots and garlic in hot oil for 2 minutes. Add broccoli; stir-fry 2 minutes more.
Add pea pods and bamboo shoots; stir-fry about 1 minute or till vegetables are crisp-tender. Remove vegetables from wok.
Add half of the beef to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till done. Remove beef. Repeat with remaining beef.

Add 1/2 cup water or beef broth to center of wok. Stir sauce; add to center of wok. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Return beef and vegetables to wok; stir to coat. Heat through.
If desired, serve with hot cooked rice. Serves 4.

notes: Stir-Frying Hints: There's no mystery to stir-frying if you follow these hints:
- Use a spatula or a long-handled spoon to gently lift and turn the food with a folding motion so it won't burn.
- Use high heat, but keep the food moving so it won't burn.
- If you need to add more oil during cooking, bring it to frying temperature before adding more food.

recipes.title: Lamb Cuts Identification Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Visual guide to identifying lamb cuts with cooking methods

recipes.title: Spinach-Stuffed Lamb Roast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Boneless leg of lamb stuffed with spinach and feta cheese

instructions.text: For stuffing, in a small saucepan cook onion and celery in margarine till tender. Cool. Stir in spinach, feta cheese, and oregano.
Remove fell (paper-thin, pinkish red layer) from lamb, if present. Cut pockets in lamb and fill with garlic slivers.
Spread stuffed surface of meat with spinach mixture. Roll up from a long side. Tie securely. Add 1/4 cup water. Place, seam side down, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan.
Roast in a 325° oven for 1-1/2 to 3 hours or till meat thermometer registers 150°. Let stand 15 minutes before carving. Makes 12 to 15 servings.

notes: To carve a leg of lamb, cut 3 slices from the thin side parallel to the bone. Rest the leg on its base.

recipes.title: Herb-Rubbed Leg of Lamb
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic roasted leg of lamb with herbs

instructions.text: Remove fell from lamb. Cut small slits in lamb; insert garlic slivers.
Combine lemon juice, parsley, mint, onion salt, rosemary, and pepper. Rub over lamb.
Place lamb, fat side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Insert a meat thermometer. Roast in a 325° oven for 1-3/4 to 2-1/4 hours or till thermometer registers 150°.
Let stand 15 minutes before carving. If desired, garnish with fresh mint. Serve with mint jelly. Makes 12 to 16 servings.

notes: Beginning at the wide end, cut 1/4-inch slices down to leg bone. Cut along bone to free slices.

recipes.title: Currant-Glazed Rack of Lamb
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant rack of lamb with currant glaze

ingredients.item: tarragon or wine or apple juice

instructions.text: Trim fat from meat. Place roast, rib side down, in a shallow roasting pan. Roast in a 325° oven. With a small saucepan combine jelly, wine, and tarragon. Heat till smooth. Brush roast with glaze.
Roast for 1 to 1-1/4 hours for medium (160°), brushing occasionally with glaze.
Mini-Glazed Rack of Lamb: Prepare as above, except use mint jelly for currant jelly.

recipes.title: Curried Lamb
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Lamb stew with curry and apples

instructions.text: In a large saucepan brown half of the meat in hot oil. Remove meat. Brown remaining meat with onion, curry powder, and garlic till onion is tender. Return all meat to pan.
Stir in flour. Add 3/4 cup water. Stir in bouillon granules and apples. Cook for 30 minutes or till thickened. Stir in raisins. Cook 5 more minutes.

Microwave directions: Omit cooking oil. In a 2-quart casserole micro-cook lamb, onion, curry, and garlic, covered, on 100% power (high) 5 minutes, stirring once. Drain. Stir in flour. Add 3/4 cup water and bouillon. Cook, covered, on 50% power (medium) for 9 to 11 minutes or till tender, stirring every 5 minutes. Stir in apples, covered, on high 3 to 5 minutes more. Stir into casserole. Cook, covered, on 50% power (medium) 5 minutes; stir every minute. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes or till thickened and bubbly, stirring every minute.
Serve over hot cooked rice.

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for hot cooked rice

recipes.title: Vegetable-Lamb Skillet
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Italian-style lamb with vegetables and beans

ingredients.item: frozen Italian-style green beans or frozen green beans

instructions.text: Run cold water over beans to separate; set aside.
Trim fat from meat. In a large skillet brown chops and onion in hot oil. Drain fat.
Combine 3/4 cup water, bouillon granules, pepper, oregano, and basil. Pour over chops. Add beans and potatoes.
Cover; cook for 20 to 25 minutes or till tender. Remove meat and vegetables. Skim fat from juices. Cook juices, uncovered, for 3 to 4 minutes.

assumptions: Assumed 1 unit for pitted ripe olives

recipes.title: Saucy Lamb Shanks
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Braised lamb shanks with vegetables

instructions.text: Cut 3-1/2 to 4 pounds lamb shanks (4) into 1-rib portions. In a 12-inch skillet brown shanks or ribs in 1 tablespoon hot cooking oil. Drain fat.
Combine 1 cup finely chopped carrot, 1 cup finely chopped celery, 1/4 cup dry red wine, and 2 cloves garlic, minced.
Add to skillet. Cover; simmer for 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 hours or till tender. Remove shanks or ribs. Cover; keep warm.
For sauce, skim fat from pan juices. Add water to equal 1 cup. Return to skillet. Add 1 can (8 oz) tomato sauce, 1 bay leaf.
For sauce, boil pan juices rapidly for 6 to 8 minutes. (You should have about 3 cups.) Discard bay leaf. Serve sauce over shanks and hot cooked noodles. Makes 4 servings.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Lamb Chops with Herb Sauce
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Quick lamb chops with sour cream herb sauce

ingredients.item: lamb shoulder chops or sirloin chops

instructions.text: Trim fat from meat. In a large skillet brown chops with salt and pepper in hot cooking oil.
Add 3/4 cup water, celery, bouillon granules, and thyme. Cover; simmer for 10 to 15 minutes or till tender. Remove meat; set aside.
For sauce, combine sour cream or yogurt and flour; stir into pan juices. Cook and stir over medium-high heat till thickened and bubbly, stirring every minute.

For sauce, reserve 1/2 cup juices; set aside. Skim fat from reserved juices. Cook cream or yogurt, flour, thyme or diluted mushrooms. Cook on high for 3 to 4 minutes or till thickened and bubbly, stirring every minute. Pass sauce with lamb chops.

notes: Microwave directions: Trim fat from meat. In a 12x7-1/2x2-inch baking dish, micro-cook lamb chops, covered with vented clear plastic wrap, on 100% power (high), for 3 minutes. Turn chops. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Cover and micro-cook, on high for 4 to 6 minutes more or till chops are done. Reserve 1/2 cup juices. Skim fat.

recipes.title: Lamb Chops with Honey-Mustard Glaze
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Broiled lamb chops with sweet and tangy glaze

instructions.text: Trim fat from lamb chops. Place chops on unheated rack of broiler pan.
Broil 3 inches from heat for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine honey, mustard, and lemon juice. Turn chops; brush with honey mixture. Broil for 5 to 7 minutes more or till desired doneness, brushing once with remaining honey mixture.
Grill directions: Prepare meat and honey mixture as above. Grill chops on uncovered grill directly over medium coals for 10 to 14 minutes, turning once. Continue as above.

recipes.title: Lamb Shish Kabobs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic Middle Eastern lamb kabobs

instructions.text: Partially freeze lamb. Cut into 3-inch-long strips about 1/4 inch thick. For marinade, in a bowl combine 1/4 cup lemon juice, oil, garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add lamb; stir to coat.
Marinate in refrigerator for 4 to 24 hours.
Drain meat, reserving marinade. On four long skewers, alternately thread meat accordion-style, zucchini, and mushrooms. Add cherry tomatoes to each skewer.
Place on unheated rack of broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from heat for 6 to 8 minutes for medium, turning and brushing skewers often. Add 2 cherry tomatoes or cherry tomatoes to each skewer.

Grill directions: Prepare meat and marinade as above. In covered grill, arrange medium-hot coals around a drip pan. Test for medium heat. Place kabobs on grill rack over pan. Cover; grill for 6 to 8 minutes for medium, turning and brushing with marinade.

recipes.title: Creole Stuffed Roast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Boneless pork roast with flavorful Creole stuffing.

instructions.text: For stuffing, in saucepan cook celery, onion, and garlic in butter until tender but not brown.
Add bread cubes, parsley, thyme, and hot pepper sauce. Toss to mix, adding enough broth to moisten.
Cut a lengthwise slit in the roast, cutting to but not through opposite side. Spread open.
Spoon stuffing into opening. Tie roast securely with string at 1-inch intervals.
Place roast on rack in shallow roasting pan. Insert meat thermometer.
Roast uncovered at 325°F for 1¾ to 2¼ hours or until thermometer registers 160°F.
Let stand 15 minutes before carving.

notes: Internal temperature should reach 160°F

recipes.title: Rib Crown Roast of Pork
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant crown roast of pork formed from the rib section, perfect for special occasions.

instructions.text: Season roast with salt and pepper. Place bone ends up in shallow roasting pan.
Wrap tips of bones with foil to prevent burning.
Insert meat thermometer into thickest portion, not touching bone.
Roast uncovered at 325°F for 2½ to 3 hours or until thermometer registers 160°F.
Transfer to warm platter. Remove foil from bone tips. If desired, place paper frills on bones.
Fill center with hot cooked vegetables or stuffing if desired.

notes: Allow 1 to 1¼ ribs per serving
Ask butcher to tie roast into crown shape
Can fill center with your favorite stuffing or vegetables

recipes.title: Harvest Pot Roast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Tender pork roast braised with vegetables for a hearty one-pot meal.

instructions.text: In Dutch oven brown roast on all sides in hot oil. Drain off fat.
Add cider, onion, celery, salt, caraway seed, and pepper.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer 1¼ hours.
Add potatoes and carrots. Cover and cook 30 minutes more.
Add cabbage wedges. Cook 15 to 20 minutes more or until meat and vegetables are tender.
Transfer meat and vegetables to platter. Skim fat from juices; pass with meat.

notes: Apple cider adds subtle sweetness to the braising liquid

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Roast Pork with Mushroom-Butter Sauce
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic pork roast served with a rich mushroom butter sauce.

ingredients.item: dry white wine or chicken broth

instructions.text: Season roast with salt and pepper. Place on rack in shallow roasting pan.
Insert meat thermometer. Roast uncovered at 325°F for 1¾ to 2¼ hours or until thermometer registers 160°F.
For sauce, in skillet cook mushrooms and green onions in butter until tender.
Add wine. Bring to boiling; reduce slightly.
Slice roast and serve with mushroom sauce.

notes: Sauce can be made while roast rests after cooking

recipes.title: Checking Pork Doneness Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Guide to determining when pork is properly cooked.
notes: Use a meat thermometer for accurate results
Insert thermometer into thickest part of meat, not touching bone
Fresh pork should be cooked to 160°F internal temperature
Let roasts stand 15 minutes before carving - temperature will rise 5-10 degrees
Well-done pork (170°F) is no longer required; 160°F produces juicier meat

recipes.title: Pork with Apple-Nutmeg Sauce
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Pork tenderloin served with a sweet apple and nutmeg sauce.

instructions.text: In large skillet cook pork slices in butter over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side or until no longer pink. Remove and keep warm.
Add apple juice to skillet, scraping up browned bits.
Stir in applesauce, brown sugar, and nutmeg.
Cook and stir until slightly thickened. Serve sauce over pork.

notes: The sauce can be made thicker by cooking longer

recipes.title: Citrus-Glazed Pork Ribs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Tender pork ribs with a tangy citrus glaze.

ingredients.item: pork loin back ribs or spareribs

instructions.text: Cut ribs into serving-size pieces. Place ribs, bone side down, in shallow roasting pan.
Roast uncovered at 350°F for 1 hour. Drain off fat.
Meanwhile, combine marmalade, lemon juice, soy sauce, and ginger.
Brush ribs generously with glaze. Roast 30 minutes more, brushing occasionally with glaze.

notes: Ribs can also be finished on the grill for a smoky flavor

recipes.title: Barbecue-Style Ribs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic oven-baked ribs with homemade barbecue sauce.

ingredients.item: pork loin back ribs or spareribs

instructions.text: Cut ribs into serving-size pieces. Place ribs, bone side down, in large shallow roasting pan.
Roast uncovered at 350°F for 1 hour. Drain off fat.
Meanwhile, in saucepan combine remaining ingredients. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Brush ribs with sauce. Roast 45 minutes to 1 hour more, brushing with sauce every 15 minutes.

notes: Reserve some sauce for serving at the table

recipes.title: Braised Steaks Italian
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Pork steaks braised in a savory Italian tomato sauce.

instructions.text: In large skillet brown steaks on both sides in hot oil. Drain off fat.
Combine tomato sauce, water, onion, green pepper, Italian seasoning, salt, and garlic.
Pour over steaks in skillet.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer 45 to 60 minutes or until meat is tender.
Serve steaks with sauce.

notes: Serve over hot cooked pasta or rice

recipes.description: Tips and guidelines for planning beverage service at parties.
notes: Generally expect to use 1½ ounces of liquor for each bar drink - get about 16 drinks from a 750-milliliter bottle (fifth)
Chill beer to about 45° to 50°F. For quick chilling, place beer bottles or cans in a deep tub of ice cubes
Generally expect to use 3 ounces of wine for each drink, getting about 8 drinks from one 750-milliliter bottle. For bigger parties, consider buying wines available in larger 1.5-liter bottles
Remember to make a variety of nonalcoholic beverages available to your guests. Nonalcoholic Eggnog, Nonalcoholic Punch, or Homemade Soda Pop are a few choices

Keep punches cold by floating easy-to-make ice rings in the serving bowls. To make an ice ring, fill a ring mold with water and freeze till firm. Or, for a fruit-filled ice ring, line the bottom of the ring mold with citrus slices, berries, or melon balls. Add enough water to just cover the fruit. Freeze till firm. Then fill the mold with water and freeze till firm

Don't buy unnecessary types of bar glasses. Ten- or 12-ounce all-purpose glasses and 9- or 10-ounce stemmed wineglasses are suitable for nearly every drink and occasion. Disposable plastic glasses, available in various sizes, are convenient to use, especially at large parties

recipes.title: Cooking Fish Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Comprehensive guide to cooking fish using various methods.
notes: Fish in most of its forms makes a quick-cooking main dish. Follow the times and directions below, cooking the fish till it flakes easily when tested with a fork.

BAKE: Fresh Fillets or Steaks - Place in single layer in greased shallow baking pan. For fillets, tuck under any thin edges. Brush with melted margarine or butter. Bake uncovered in a 450°F oven for 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness. Frozen - Bake uncovered in a 450°F oven for 9 to 11 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness. Dressed - Bake uncovered in a 350°F oven for 6 to 9 minutes per 1/2 pound.

BROIL: Fresh - Broil 4 inches from the heat for 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness. If fish is 1 inch or more thick, turn it over halfway through broiling. Frozen - Broil 4 inches from the heat for 5 to 9 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness. If fish is 1 inch or more thick, turn it over halfway through broiling. Dressed - Not recommended.

POACH: Add 1½ cups water, broth or wine to a large skillet. Bring to boiling. Add fish. Return to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, covered for 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness. For frozen steaks, simmer covered for 6 to 9 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness.

GRILL: Place fillets or dressed fish in a well-greased grill basket. Place steaks on a greased grill rack. Grill on an uncovered grill directly over medium-hot coals for 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness, turning once. Brush with melted margarine or butter, if necessary.

MICRO-COOK: For fresh fillets, arrange fish in a single layer in a shallow baking dish. For fillets, tuck under any thin edges. Cover with vented clear plastic wrap. Micro-cook on 100% power (high). For 1/2 pound of 1/2-inch-thick fillets, allow 3 to 4 minutes; for 1 pound of 1/2-inch-thick fillets, allow 4 to 7 minutes. For 1-inch-thick steaks, to 1-inch-thick steaks, allow 7 to 9 minutes.

recipes.title: Preparing and Cooking Shellfish Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Comprehensive guide for preparing and cooking various types of shellfish.
notes: CLAMS: Scrub live clams under cold running water. Combine 4 quarts cold water and 1/3 cup salt. Soak for 15 minutes; rinse. Drain and rinse. Discard water. For 24 clams in shells, add water to an 8-quart Dutch oven to 1/2-inch depth. Bring to boiling; add clams. Steam, covered, for 5 to 8 minutes or till shells open. Discard any that do not open. Serve with melted butter or margarine.

CRAWFISH: Rinse live crawfish under cold running water. For 4 pounds live crawfish, combine 8 quarts cold water and 1/2 cup salt in a 12- to 16-quart kettle. Add crawfish and soak for 15 minutes; rinse, drain. Return 5 quarts water to the kettle; bring to boiling. Reduce heat. Add crawfish. Return to boiling, stirring occasionally. Drain. 5 minutes or till shells turn bright red. Drain. Serve at once with a butter sauce or melted butter or margarine.

LOBSTER TAILS: Thaw frozen tails. For 4 tails in a 3-quart saucepan bring 6 cups water and 1½ teaspoons salt to boiling. Add tails; return to boiling. Reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 8 to 12 minutes for 5-oz tails, 8 to 12 minutes for 6- to 8-oz tails. Drain. Remove meat. Serve with melted butter or margarine.

MUSSELS: Scrub live mussels under cold running water. Using your fingers, pull out the beards that are visible between the shells. Soak (see clams, above). For 24 mussels, add water to an 8-quart Dutch oven to 1/2-inch depth; bring to boiling. Add mussels. Steam, covered, for 3 to 5 minutes or till shells open. Discard any that do not open. Serve with melted butter or margarine.

OYSTERS: Scrub live oysters under cold running water. For easier shucking, chill them before opening. Shuck, reserving bottom shells, if desired. For 24 shucked oysters, simmer uncovered in 2 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt for 1 to 2 minutes or till oysters begin to curl around edges. Drain and chill. Serve on the half shell with a sauce.

SCALLOPS: Thaw shelled scallops, if frozen. Rinse scallops and cut large ones in half. For 1 pound, simmer, uncovered, in 4 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt for 1 to 2 minutes or till opaque. Drain. Use as cooked scallops in a recipe or chill and serve with a sauce.

SHRIMP (in shells or peeled and deveined): Rinse shrimp in shells or peeled shrimp under cold running water and drain. Store in the refrigerator for up to 2 days if not to be used immediately. For 1 pound, simmer, uncovered, in 4 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt for 1 to 3 minutes or till shrimp turn pink, stirring occasionally. Rinse under cold running water. Drain. Use as cooked shrimp in a recipe or chill and serve with a sauce.

recipes.title: General Freezing Steps Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Step-by-step instructions for properly freezing foods.
notes: 1. Wash fruits and vegetables with fresh cold water. Prepare as directed on pages 194-195. Follow directions for blanching and cooling.

2. Selecting Containers: Be sure to select varieties of fruits and vegetables recommended for freezing (check seed catalogs), and to freeze the food when it's young, tender, and at its peak of flavor and texture.
3. Put the food in the labeled container (see tip, page 193). For fruit, add sugar or syrup as indicated in the chart on pages 194-195.
4. For fruits, add one of the following packs: Water pack, Sugar pack, or Dry pack. Add no sugar as specified in the chart. Unsweetened pack: Use this for fruit with ascorbic acid color keeper.

5. Wipe any spills from the rims of the containers and jars. Seal containers according to manufacturer's directions, pressing out as much air as possible. If necessary, use freezer tape around the edges of the lids to ensure a tight seal.

Using Frozen Foods: Don't thaw vegetables until ready to cook. These fruits, vegetables, and meats can be cooked or partially thawed (within 8 to 10 months) before using. Leave space between the packages so air can circulate around them.
Wrap solid blocks of food in freezer paper or foil. Fold the edges down in a series of locked folds. Fold in the ends of the package, pressing out air and fitting snugly. Secure with freezer tape.

recipes.title: Freezing Prepared Food Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Guide to freezing various prepared foods with storage times and reheating instructions.
notes: BREADS, ROLLS: Bake and cool. Seal in a freezer bag or container. Storage: 3 months. To serve: Thaw in foil in a 300°F oven about 20 minutes.
CAKES, CUPCAKES: Bake, remove from pans, and cool. Freeze on a tray, then wrap. Storage: 6 months. To serve: Thaw, covered, at room temperature 1 to 2 hours.

CASSEROLES: Use less seasoning (some intensify during freezing) and undercook slightly. Cool quickly. Pour into a freezer container. Storage: 2 to 4 weeks. To serve: Bake in a 400°F oven for 1½ hours per quart, baking for first half of time covered.

COOKIES: Unbaked: Drop dough and freeze on a tray. Lift into freezer bags. Baked: Stack with waxed paper, wrap individually. Storage: 6 months. To serve: Bake dropped dough without thawing. Thaw baked cookies at room temperature.
LEFTOVERS (meat with gravy, stews): Cool. Package in rigid freezer containers. Storage: 1 to 3 months. To serve: Thaw, covered, in the refrigerator. Reheat.

PIES: Unbaked: Do not freeze pecan pie. Treat light-colored fruit with ascorbic acid color keeper. Prepare pie as usual but do not cut slits in top crust. Use a metal or freeze-to-oven pie plate. Cover with inverted paper plate to protect crust. Place in a freezer bag. Baked: Do not freeze cream or custard pies. Bake pie and cool. Package as for unbaked pies. Storage: 2 to 4 months. To serve: Unwrap; cut slits in top. Cover edge with foil. Bake frozen pie in a 450°F oven for 15 minutes, then in a 375°F oven for 15 minutes. Uncover; bake about 30 minutes more or till done.

SANDWICHES: Spread bread with margarine. Use cheese, meat, poultry, tuna, salmon, or peanut butter filling. Not recommended: Lettuce, tomatoes, celery, jelly, cooked egg whites, mayonnaise or salad dressing. Storage: 2 months. To serve: Thaw in wrap in the refrigerator for 1 to 2 hours. Thaw other sandwiches at room temperature.

STEWS, SOUPS: Use vegetables that freeze well (not potatoes). Omit salt and thickening. If to be kept longer than 2 months, undercook vegetables. Cool quickly. Pour into freezer containers or bags, leaving some headspace. Storage: 1 to 3 months. To serve: Place frozen food in a heavy saucepan. Cook over low heat, separating often with a fork till hot. Season and thicken.

recipes.title: General Canning Steps Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Comprehensive guide to safe home canning procedures.
notes: CANNING: For year-round enjoyment, follow a canning process suitable food in standard canning jars, topped with lids and screw bands for an airtight seal. Select the freshest, top-quality produce. Sort out any bruised or underripe items.

EQUIPMENT: A water-bath canner is used for processing high-acid foods such as fruits, tomatoes (with added acid), pickles, and relishes. The 212°F temperature produced in the boiling water is sufficient for these foods. A pressure canner is used for processing low-acid foods and vegetables. It reaches temperatures of 240°F to 250°F, the safe level for these foods. This canning method must be followed for safe canning of low-acid foods. A 16-quart pressure canner is ideal.

JARS: Use only standard canning jars, and their mouths are specially designed to seal properly for canning. Run your finger over the mouth of the jars to check for any chips or cracks. Discard any jars with chips or cracks. Use them for dry storage only.

LIDS: Use self-sealing compound bands and flat metal lids with built-in sealing compound. Carefully follow the manufacturer's directions when preparing them. Lids are designed for one-time use, but you can reuse screw bands if they are not bent or rusty.
Foods are packed into canning jars by either raw-pack (cold-pack) or the hot-pack method. In raw packing, the uncooked food is packed into jars.
Other useful pieces of equipment are: a large kettle or Dutch oven, wide-mouth funnel, jar lifter and food mill, colander, or sieve.

STEPS: 1. After the jars are completely cooled, press the center of each lid to check the seal. If it dips up and down, the jar is sealed. If the lid bounces and reprocesses the contents using a clean jar and new lid, processing for the full length of time specified. Or, freeze the food (allowing 1/2-inch headspace). If you plan to use the food within a day or two, you also can refrigerate it.
2. Wipe the jars and lids. Label jars with contents and date. Remove the screw bands. Store in a cool (50° to 70°F), dry, dark place. Use the food within one year.

recipes.title: How Much Meat to Buy Guide
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Guide for determining how much meat to purchase per serving.
notes: When buying meat, remember that cuts with the most bone-in meat will give fewer servings per pound of meat per serving. The servings per pound will vary, and you'll need to consider what else you'll be serving and of course, the appetites of those eating.
Boneless meat (ground meats, boneless roasts and steaks, boneless stew cubes, variety meats): 4 or 5 servings per pound
Cuts with little bone (rib roasts, bone-in ham, center cut pork and lamb loin, rib or loin chops): 2 or 3 servings per pound
Cuts with much bone (short ribs, beef round bone or veal cuts, shanks, spareribs, brisket, ham, lamb and chops): 1 or 2 servings per pound

recipes.title: Citrus-Ginger Pot Roast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Asian-inspired pot roast with orange and ginger flavors.

instructions.text: Trim fat from roast. In a Dutch oven brown roast on all sides in hot oil. Drain fat.
Combine orange juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic. Pour over roast.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 1½ to 2 hours or till meat is tender.
Transfer meat to serving platter. Skim fat from pan juices. Serve juices with meat.

notes: Orange and ginger create an Asian-inspired flavor profile

recipes.title: Horseradish-Rubbed Beef Roast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Rib eye roast with a tangy horseradish and sour cream topping.

ingredients.item: dairy sour cream or whipping cream

instructions.text: Cut 1-inch-wide pockets into roast at 3-inch intervals. In a mixing bowl combine horseradish, lemon peel, and lemon juice. Reserve 2 tablespoons of the horseradish mixture. Stir margarine into remaining horseradish mixture. Rub margarine mixture onto roast and into pockets.
Place meat, fat side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Insert a meat thermometer.

Roast in a 325°F oven for 1¾ to 2½ hours for medium-rare (140°F), or 1½ to 2 hours for medium (160°F), or 1½ to 2½ hours for well-done (170°F). Cover with foil and let stand for 15 minutes before carving.
Meanwhile, stir together reserved horseradish mixture, sour cream or whipped cream, and parsley. Pass with meat.

notes: Horseradish intensifies the beef flavor
Let roast rest before carving for juicier results

recipes.title: Beef Pot Roast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic braised beef pot roast with vegetables.

ingredients.item: water, dry wine, or tomato juice

instructions.text: Trim fat from roast. In a Dutch oven brown roast on all sides in hot oil. Drain fat.
Combine water, Worcestershire sauce, bouillon granules, and basil. Pour over roast.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add onions, carrots, potatoes, and celery. Cover and simmer 45 to 60 minutes more or till meat and vegetables are tender.

Remove meat and vegetables; keep warm. For gravy, skim fat from pan juices. Measure 1½ cups pan juices. Combine ¼ cup cold water and flour. Stir into pan juices. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly.

notes: Crockery-cooker directions included in original recipe

recipes.title: Pan Gravy for Roasted Meat
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic pan gravy made from roast meat drippings.

instructions.text: After removing roasted meat from pan, pour drippings into a large measuring cup, scraping out the crusty browned bits. Skim fat, reserving ¼ cup fat. (To skim fat: The oily liquid that rises to the top.)
Reserve all the oily liquid and ¼ cup of reserved fat.
In a medium saucepan combine reserved fat and ¼ cup all-purpose flour. Cook and stir for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add enough beef broth or water to equal 2 cups liquid. Add all at once to flour mixture. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 1 to 2 minutes more. Season to taste.

notes: The browned bits from the pan add tremendous flavor

instructions.text: Trim fat from meat. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. In a Dutch oven brown meat on all sides in hot oil. Drain fat.

recipes.title: Steak and Spinach Pinwheels
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Flank steak rolled with spinach and bacon, sliced into attractive pinwheels.

ingredients.item: beef top round or flank steak

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook bacon till just done but not crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Score steak by making shallow diagonal cuts at 1-inch intervals in a diamond pattern. Repeat on second side. With a meat mallet, pound steak into a 12x8-inch rectangle, working from center to edges.

Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Arrange bacon lengthwise on steak. Sprinkle with spinach. Roll up from a short side. Secure with wooden picks at 1-inch intervals, starting ½ inch from one end. Cut between picks into eight 1-inch slices.

Place cut side down, on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 3 inches from the heat for 6 minutes. Turn; broil for 6 to 8 minutes more for medium doneness. Remove picks. Serve with Mock Hollandaise Sauce if desired.

notes: Grill directions: Grill slices on an uncovered grill directly over medium coals for 6 minutes, allowing 6 to 8 minutes per side for medium.

recipes.title: Rib Crown Roast of Pork with Rice Stuffing
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant crown roast of pork filled with savory rice stuffing.

instructions.text: For stuffing, in a saucepan combine rice, carrot, onion, celery, salt, and pepper, Italian seasoning and 1¼ teaspoons ground pepper. Add the 2 cups broth; bring to boiling. Reduce heat. Cover; simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat; let stand for 15 minutes.
Cut off stuffing with the rice.
Cover; stand the Brush roast. Using a fork to steady the crown; Using roast. Spoon stuffing into crown, cut between the ribs to serve.
Remove strings; transfer meat to a serving platter. Cover and let stand 15 minutes before carving.
Meanwhile, for fruit stuffing, combine rice mixture and add one 6-ounce package (1½ cups) mixed dried fruit bits and ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon with the rice.
