recipes.title: Soft-Cooked Eggs and Hard-Cooked Eggs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

instructions.text: Place eggs in saucepan. Add enough cold water to cover eggs. Bring to boiling over high heat. Reduce heat so water is just below simmering; cover. For soft-cooked eggs, cook 4 to 6 minutes. For hard-cooked eggs, cook 15 minutes. Drain.
For soft-cooked eggs, add cold water to the pan just till eggs are cool enough to handle. Cut off tops and serve in egg cups. Or, cut eggs in half and use a spoon to scoop the eggs into dishes.

For hard-cooked eggs, fill the saucepan with cold water and let stand 2 minutes. To quickly cool, add a few ice cubes. Drain. Gently tap each egg on the countertop. Roll egg between palms of hands. Peel off eggshell, starting at the large end.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Deviled Eggs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Four different flavors to choose from.

instructions.text: Halve hard-cooked eggs lengthwise and remove yolks. Place yolks in a bowl; mash with a fork. Add mayonnaise, mustard, and vinegar; mix well. Season with salt and pepper, if desired. Stuff egg white halves with yolk mixture. Garnish with paprika or parsley, if desired.

notes: Italian-Style Deviled Eggs: Prepare as above, except omit mayonnaise, mustard, and vinegar. Add 1/4 cup creamy Italian salad dressing and 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese to mashed yolks; mix well.
Indian-Style Deviled Eggs: Prepare as above, except omit mustard and vinegar. Add 1/4 cup finely chopped peanuts and 1/2 teaspoon curry powder to yolk mixture; mix well.

Mexican-Style Deviled Eggs: Prepare as above, except omit mustard and vinegar. Add 2 tablespoons canned diced green chili peppers, 1 tablespoon chopped pitted ripe olives, 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, and 1/8 teaspoon ground red pepper to yolk mixture; mix well. Stuff egg whites with yolk mixture. Garnish with sliced pitted ripe olives or cilantro and serve with salsa, if desired.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Fried Eggs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: No need to turn the eggs with this simple method.

ingredients.item: margarine or butter, or nonstick spray coating

instructions.text: In a large skillet melt margarine or butter over medium heat. (Or, spray a cold skillet with nonstick coating, then heat.) Add eggs. When whites are set, add 1 tablespoon water. Cover skillet; cook eggs to desired doneness (about 2 minutes for soft or 4 minutes for firm).

notes: Note: For 1 or 2 eggs, use a small skillet and 1 teaspoon margarine or butter.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Baked Eggs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Same great poached-egg taste, but less work.

ingredients.item: shredded cheddar, Swiss, or Monterey Jack cheese (optional)

instructions.text: Generously grease three 10-ounce casseroles with margarine. Carefully break 2 eggs into each casserole; sprinkle with salt, pepper, and chives or herb. Set casseroles into a 13x9x2-inch baking pan; place on an oven rack. Pour hot water around casseroles in pan to a depth of 1 inch.

Bake in a 325° oven about 25 minutes or till eggs are firm and whites are opaque. If desired, after 20 minutes of cooking, sprinkle cheese atop eggs. Cook for 5 to 10 minutes more or till eggs are cooked and cheese melts.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Egg-Salad Sandwiches
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: slices bread, or 2 small pita bread rounds or 2 bagels, split

instructions.text: In a bowl combine chopped eggs, green onion, and pimiento; stir in mayonnaise and mustard. Add salt and pepper to taste. Spread egg mixture on 2 slices of bread, in pita rounds, or on bagel bottoms. Top with lettuce and, if not using pitas, remaining bread slices or bagel tops.

notes: Greek-Style Egg-Salad Sandwiches: Prepare as above, except omit the pimiento and mustard. Stir 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese, 1/4 cup finely chopped tomato, and 2 tablespoons chopped pitted ripe olives into egg mixture.

California-Style Egg-Salad Sandwiches: Prepare as above, except omit pimiento. Stir 1/4 cup chopped avocado and 1/4 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese into egg mixture. Substitute alfalfa sprouts for lettuce.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Asparagus-Egg Casserole
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Next time, try frozen chopped broccoli in place of the asparagus.

ingredients.item: crushed rich round or whole wheat crackers (about 6 crackers)

instructions.text: Cook asparagus according to package directions; drain. For sauce, in a medium saucepan cook onion and green pepper in the 2 tablespoons margarine till tender. Stir in flour, dry mustard, salt, and pepper. Add milk. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Add cheese; stir till melted.

Reserve 1/4 cup asparagus. Stir remaining asparagus and chopped eggs into sauce. Pour into a 1-quart casserole. Bake, covered, in a 375° oven for 10 minutes. Arrange reserved asparagus on top. Combine crushed crackers with the melted margarine. Sprinkle atop casserole. Bake, uncovered, for 10 minutes more.

recipes.title: Scrambled Eggs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

instructions.text: In a bowl beat together eggs, milk or light cream, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and dash pepper. In a large skillet melt margarine over medium heat; pour in egg mixture. Cook, without stirring, till mixture begins to set on the bottom and around edge.

Using a large spoon or spatula, lift and fold partially cooked eggs so uncooked portion flows underneath. Continue cooking over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes or till eggs are cooked throughout but are still glossy and moist. Remove from the heat immediately.

notes: Herbed Scrambled Eggs: Prepare as above, except add 1 tablespoon snipped parsley and 1/8 teaspoon dried thyme, crushed, to the beaten egg mixture.
Cream-Cheese Scrambled Eggs: Prepare as above, except add one 3-ounce package cream cheese with chives, cut into small cubes, to the beaten egg mixture.

Cheese-Onion Scrambled Eggs: Prepare as above, except cook 1 green onion, sliced, in margarine 30 seconds. Then add egg mixture. Add 1/2 cup shredded American cheese after eggs begin to set. Do not use microwave directions.

Mushroom Scrambled Eggs: Prepare as above, except increase margarine to 2 tablespoons. Cook 1/2 cup sliced fresh mushrooms and 1 tablespoon chopped onion in margarine. Add 1 tablespoon snipped parsley, 1/2 teaspoon dry mustard, and 1/4 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce to beaten egg mixture. Do not use the microwave directions.

Denver Scrambled Eggs: Prepare as above, except omit salt and increase margarine to 2 tablespoons. In the skillet cook 1/3 cup diced fully cooked ham; 1/4 cup chopped onion; one 2-ounce can mushroom stems and pieces, drained; and 2 tablespoons finely chopped green pepper in margarine. Then add egg mixture. Do not use the microwave directions.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Farmer's Breakfast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: For a quicker breakfast, substitute frozen hash brown potatoes for the fresh potatoes.

ingredients.item: medium potatoes, peeled and finely chopped (2 cups)

instructions.text: In a large nonstick or well-seasoned skillet cook potatoes and onion in margarine over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes or till tender; stir often.

Beat together eggs, milk, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper; stir in ham. Pour over potato mixture. Cook, without stirring, till mixture begins to set on the bottom and around edge. Using a large spoon, lift and fold partially cooked egg mixture so uncooked portion flows underneath. Continue cooking about 4 minutes or till eggs are cooked throughout but still glossy and moist.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Scrambled-Egg Casserole
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Use the make-ahead directions when you know your morning is going to be busy.

ingredients.item: chopped green pepper or sliced green onion
shredded American or process Swiss cheese (3 ounces)
plain or seasoned fine dry bread crumbs

instructions.text: In a large skillet cook green pepper or onion in 1 tablespoon of the margarine till tender. Add eggs; cook over medium heat without stirring till mixture begins to set on bottom and around edge. Lift and fold partially cooked eggs so uncooked portion flows underneath. Continue cooking till just set. Transfer to a 1-quart casserole.

In a small saucepan melt 1 tablespoon of the margarine. Stir in flour and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in cheese till melted. Stir in pimiento. Fold cheese mixture into cooked eggs.
Melt remaining margarine; toss with crumbs. Sprinkle over egg mixture. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 to 20 minutes or till hot.

notes: To make ahead: Prepare as above, except do not bake. Cover and refrigerate casserole for 3 to 24 hours. Bake, covered, 25 minutes. Uncover; bake 10 to 15 minutes more or till hot.

recipes.title: Eggs in a Puff
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Cheesy eggs served in a cream puff shell.

ingredients.item: chopped green or sweet red pepper
shredded cheddar or Swiss cheese (4 ounces)

instructions.text: For cream-puff shell, combine the 1/2 cup margarine and 1 cup water. Bring to boiling. Add flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt all at once, stirring vigorously. Cook and stir till mixture forms a ball that doesn't separate. Remove from heat. Cool 5 minutes. Add 4 eggs, one at a time, beating with a wooden spoon after each addition till smooth. Spread over bottom and up the sides of a greased 9-inch pie plate. Bake in a 400° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or till golden brown and puffy.

Meanwhile, beat together the remaining eggs, milk, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and dash pepper. Stir in pea pods and green or red pepper. In a large skillet melt the 1 tablespoon margarine. Pour in egg mixture. Cook, without stirring, till mixture begins to set on bottom and around edge, sprinkle with cheese. Lift and fold egg mixture till eggs are cooked but still glossy and moist, and cheese melts. Spoon into baked puff shell.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Egg-Pita Sandwiches
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: sliced green onion or chopped green pepper

instructions.text: In a medium skillet cook mushrooms and green onion or chopped green pepper in margarine or butter till tender. In a bowl beat together 3 eggs; 3 tablespoons milk; 1/8 teaspoon dried basil, crushed; dash salt; and dash pepper. Pour over mushroom mixture. Cook, without stirring, till eggs begin to set on bottom and around edge. Lift and fold partially cooked eggs so uncooked portion flows underneath. Continue cooking till thoroughly cooked but still glossy and moist.
Sprinkle 1/4 cup shredded cheddar cheese over eggs. Remove from heat. Let stand 1 minute or till cheese melts slightly. Halve 1 pita bread round; spoon egg mixture into halves.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: French Omelet
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The Vegetable French Omelet with zucchini and cheddar cheese is pictured below right.

instructions.text: In a bowl combine eggs, water, salt, and dash pepper. Using a fork, beat till combined but not frothy. In an 8- or 10-inch skillet with flared sides, heat margarine or butter till a drop of water sizzles. Lift and tilt the pan to coat the sides.

Add egg mixture to skillet; cook over medium heat. As eggs set, run a spatula around the edge of the skillet, lifting eggs and letting uncooked portion flow underneath. When eggs are set but still shiny, remove from the heat. Fold omelet in half. Transfer onto a warm plate.

notes: Mushroom French Omelet: Prepare as above, except for filling, cook 1/2 cup sliced fresh mushrooms in 1 tablespoon margarine till tender. Spoon across center of omelet. Fold sides over.

Cheese French Omelet: Prepare as above, except omit salt. For filling, sprinkle 1/4 cup shredded cheddar, Swiss, Monterey Jack, or American cheese across center of omelet. Fold sides over. Top with shredded cheese and snipped parsley.

Fruited French Omelet: Prepare as above, except for filling, spread 2 tablespoons dairy sour cream or yogurt across center of omelet. Fold sides over. Top omelet with 1/4 cup halved strawberries; sliced, peeled peaches; or blueberries. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon brown sugar.

Vegetable French Omelet: Prepare as above, except for filling, cook 1/3 cup vegetables (combination of sliced asparagus, sliced zucchini, sliced green onion, sliced celery, or chopped green pepper) and 1/8 teaspoon dried basil, crushed, in 1 tablespoon margarine. Spoon filling across center of omelet. Sprinkle grated Parmesan, shredded cheddar, or crumbled feta cheese atop filling before folding omelet.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Denver Omelet
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Chock-full of bright garden vegetables and ham.

ingredients.item: fully cooked ham, cut into 1-inch-long strips (1/2 cup)

instructions.text: Prepare Puffy Omelet (see recipe, opposite). Prepare filling while omelet is baking.

For filling, in a skillet melt 2 tablespoons margarine or butter. Add 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms; 1 medium green pepper, chopped; 4 green onions, bias sliced; and 1/2 teaspoon dried basil, crushed. Cook till tender but not brown. Stir in 3 ounces fully cooked ham, cut into 1-inch-long strips (1/2 cup), and 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, halved. Heat through. Remove omelet from the oven. Fill omelet with ham mixture before folding.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Puffy Omelet
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

instructions.text: In a bowl beat egg whites till frothy. Add 2 tablespoons water; continue beating about 1 1/2 minutes or till stiff peaks form (tips stand straight). Fold egg yolks into egg whites.

In a large ovenproof skillet heat margarine till a drop of water sizzles. Pour in egg mixture, mounding it slightly higher at the sides. Cook over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes or till puffed, set, and golden brown on the bottom. Then bake in a 325° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Loosen sides of omelet with a metal spatula. Make a shallow cut slightly off center across the omelet. Fold smaller side over the larger side.

notes: Cheese-Herb Puffy Omelet: Prepare as above, except while omelet is baking, melt 1 tablespoon margarine or butter in a saucepan. Stir in 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon snipped chives, and 1/4 teaspoon dried fines herbes, crushed. Add 1/3 cup milk. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Stir in 1/3 cup shredded cheddar or Swiss cheese till melted. Pour over folded omelet.

Ham-and-Cheese Puffy Omelet: Prepare as above, except while omelet is baking, melt 1 tablespoon margarine or butter in a saucepan. Stir in 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour. Add 2/3 cup milk. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Stir in 1/3 cup shredded cheddar or Swiss cheese till melted. Stir in 1/4 cup diced fully cooked ham and one 2-ounce jar sliced mushrooms, drained. Heat through. Pour over folded omelet.

Bacon-Asparagus Puffy Omelet: Prepare as above, except place one 10-ounce package frozen cut asparagus in a colander. Run hot water over asparagus till thawed; drain. Stir together 1/4 cup cold water, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, and 2 teaspoons cornstarch; set aside. In a skillet cook 2 slices bacon till crisp; drain, reserving drippings. Crumble bacon; set aside. Cook 1/4 cup chopped onion in drippings over medium heat till tender. Add asparagus; cook and stir for 3 minutes. Stir soy sauce mixture; add to skillet. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Add bacon; spoon atop omelet before folding.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Frittata
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: An open-face omelet that's easy to whip up for a quick supper or breakfast.

instructions.text: In a bowl beat eggs and 1/8 teaspoon pepper; set aside. In a 10-inch broilerproof or regular skillet cook onion and garlic in margarine or butter till tender. Stir in chopped vegetables or meat.

Pour egg mixture into skillet over vegetables or meat. Cook over medium heat. As mixture sets, run a spatula around edge of skillet, lifting egg mixture to allow uncooked portions to flow underneath. Continue cooking and lifting edges till egg mixture is almost set (surface will be moist).

Place broilerproof skillet under the broiler 4 to 5 inches from the heat. Broil for 1 to 2 minutes or till top is just set. (Or, if using a regular skillet, remove skillet from the heat; cover and let stand 3 to 4 minutes or till top is set.) Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Cut into wedges.

notes: Greek Frittata: Prepare as above, except substitute 4 cups torn fresh spinach for the chopped cooked vegetables or meat. After adding spinach to onion and garlic in the skillet, cook for 2 to 3 minutes more or till spinach is limp. Substitute 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese for Parmesan cheese. Do not use microwave directions.

Oven Frittata: Prepare as above, except use an ovenproof skillet. After pouring egg mixture into the skillet, bake in a 350° oven about 15 minutes or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Cheese Soufflé
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Choose from four cheeses to make this melt-in-your-mouth dish.

ingredients.item: shredded cheddar, process Swiss, Colby, or Havarti cheese (12 ounces)

instructions.text: Measure enough foil to wrap around a 2-quart soufflé dish with 6 inches to spare. Fold foil into thirds lengthwise. Lightly butter one side. With buttered side in, position foil around dish, letting it extend 2 inches above the top. Fasten the foil.

For cheese sauce, in a saucepan melt margarine or butter; stir in flour and red pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Remove from the heat. Add cheese, 1 cup at a time, stirring till melted. In a bowl beat yolks with a fork till combined. Slowly add cheese sauce to yolks, stirring constantly. Cool slightly.

In a bowl beat egg whites till stiff peaks form (tips stand straight). Gently fold about 2 cups of the stiffly beaten whites into cheese sauce. Gradually pour cheese sauce over remaining stiffly beaten whites, folding to combine. Pour into the ungreased soufflé dish. Bake in a 350° oven about 50 minutes or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Gently peel off foil; serve soufflé immediately.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Vegetable Soufflé
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Puffs nicely in either a 10x6x2-inch dish or a soufflé dish.

ingredients.item: fresh marjoram, basil, dill, or tarragon, snipped; or 1/4 teaspoon dried herb, crushed
shredded cheddar or Swiss cheese (4 ounces)
finely chopped cooked broccoli, cauliflower, asparagus, carrot, or spinach

instructions.text: In a medium saucepan cook onion and garlic in margarine or butter till tender. Stir in flour, desired herb, salt, and pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Remove from heat. Add shredded cheese and stir till melted. Stir in broccoli, cauliflower, asparagus, carrot, or spinach.
In a bowl beat egg yolks with a fork till combined. Gradually add vegetable mixture, stirring constantly. Set aside.

In a bowl beat egg whites till stiff peaks form (tips stand straight). Gently fold about 1 cup of the beaten egg whites into vegetable mixture to lighten it. Gradually pour vegetable mixture over remaining beaten egg whites, folding to combine. Pour into an ungreased 1 1/2-quart soufflé dish or a 10x6x2-inch baking dish.
Bake in a 350° oven about 40 minutes for the soufflé dish (25 to 30 minutes for the 10x6x2-inch baking dish) or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Serve soufflé immediately.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Spinach Puff
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Serve this soufflé-like dish as an entrée, or as a side dish with fish or roast beef.

ingredients.item: shredded Swiss or cheddar cheese (6 ounces)

instructions.text: Drain spinach well in a colander, pressing out liquid with a spoon. Grease a 1-quart soufflé dish or casserole; sprinkle with crumbs. Set aside.

In a bowl, blender container, or food processor bowl, combine cottage cheese and eggs. Add shredded cheese, flour, margarine, onion salt, and peel. Beat with an electric mixer, or cover and blend or process till smooth. Stir in spinach.
Transfer mixture to the prepared dish. Bake in a 350° oven about 1 hour or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.

recipes.servings_yield: Makes 4 main-dish servings or 8 side-dish servings
notes: Broccoli Puff: Prepare as above, except substitute frozen chopped broccoli for the spinach. Cook broccoli in boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes or till crisp-tender; drain well.
Blue Cheese and Bacon Puff: Prepare as above, except add 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese with the shredded cheese. Stir in 4 slices crisp-cooked, crumbled bacon with the spinach.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Choose-a-Flavor Quiche
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Mix and match the meat and cheese to suit your fancy, or rely on the classic bacon and Swiss cheese combination in Quiche Lorraine.

ingredients.item: Pastry for Single-Crust Pie (see recipe, page 293)
chopped cooked chicken, crabmeat, or ham
shredded Swiss, cheddar, Monterey Jack, or Havarti cheese (6 ounces)

instructions.text: Prepare Pastry for Single-Crust Pie. Line the unpricked pastry shell with a double thickness of heavy-duty foil. Bake in a 450° oven for 5 minutes. Remove foil. Bake for 5 to 7 minutes more or till pastry is nearly done. Remove from the oven. Reduce oven temperature to 325°.
Meanwhile, in a bowl stir together eggs, milk, onion, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Stir in chicken, crabmeat, or ham. Toss together shredded cheese and flour. Add to egg mixture; mix well.

Pour egg mixture into hot pastry shell. Bake in the 325° oven for 35 to 40 minutes or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. If necessary, cover edge of crust with foil to prevent overbrowning. Let stand for 10 minutes.

notes: Quiche Lorraine: Prepare as above, except omit green onion and chicken, crabmeat, or ham. Cook 6 slices bacon till crisp. Drain, reserving 2 tablespoons drippings. Crumble bacon; set aside. Cook 1 medium onion, sliced, in drippings over medium heat till tender; drain. Add bacon, onion, and Swiss-cheese-flour mixture to egg mixture.

Individual Quiche Casseroles: Prepare as above, except omit pastry and chicken, crabmeat, or ham. Pour egg mixture into four 10-ounce custard cups. Place custard cups in a 13x9x2-inch baking pan on an oven rack. Pour boiling water around cups in the pan to a depth of 1 inch. Bake in a 325° oven for 20 to 25 minutes or till a knife inserted near centers comes out clean. Serves 4.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Spinach-Egg Casserole
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained
English muffins, split and toasted, or toast points

instructions.text: For sauce, in a medium saucepan melt margarine. Stir in flour and 1/8 teaspoon pepper. Add milk. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Add cheese. Cook and stir till cheese melts. Measure 2/3 cup sauce; set aside. Stir spinach and ham into sauce in the saucepan. Pour into a 1 1/2-quart casserole. Place eggs atop mixture, pressing lightly. Pour reserved sauce over eggs. Bake in a 350° oven about 30 minutes or till heated through. Serve over muffins or toast.

notes: To make ahead: Prepare as above, except do not bake. Cover casserole and refrigerate 2 to 24 hours. Bake, covered, in a 350° oven for 50 to 55 minutes or till heated through.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Breakfast Pizza
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: desired vegetables (sliced pitted ripe olives; sliced avocado, green onion, or mushrooms; or chopped tomato)
shredded cheddar, Swiss, or mozzarella cheese; diced fully cooked ham; or chopped cooked turkey or chicken

instructions.text: For crust, unroll crescent rolls; separate into triangles. Place triangles on a lightly greased 12-inch pizza pan with points toward center. Press triangles together to cover bottom and 1/2 inch up sides of pan. Bake in a 375° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or till lightly browned. (Do not remove crust from the oven.)

Meanwhile, combine beaten eggs, milk, oregano, and pepper. When crust is lightly browned, leave on oven shelf (if necessary, press down any high spots in crust). Carefully pour egg mixture onto crust. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes more or till egg mixture is almost set.
Sprinkle with desired vegetables. Sprinkle with cheese, ham, turkey, or chicken. Return to the oven and bake 3 to 5 minutes more or till cheese melts. Cut into wedges.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Cheesy Brunch Roll-Ups
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

instructions.text: In a saucepan cook mushrooms, onion, and green pepper in margarine till tender. Drain. Dividing mushroom mixture evenly, spoon along center of each tortilla. Divide the 1 1/2 cups cheese among the tortillas. Roll up tortillas and place, seam side down, in a greased 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish. In a bowl stir together eggs, milk, flour, garlic powder, and pepper sauce. Pour over rolled-up tortillas.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 to 40 minutes or till set. Sprinkle the 1/2 cup cheese over top. Let stand 10 minutes. Cut into 6 squares.

notes: To make ahead: Prepare as above, except do not bake. Cover and refrigerate 2 to 24 hours. Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 45 to 50 minutes or till set.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Welsh Rarebit Breakfast
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The tangy cheese sauce also is good served over broccoli, cauliflower, and burgers.

ingredients.item: English muffins, split and toasted, or 4 slices bread, toasted
slices Canadian-style bacon, warmed, or 4 poached eggs (see recipe, page 144)
shredded cheddar or American cheese (6 ounces)

instructions.text: For English muffin or toast stacks, place muffin halves or toast slices on plates. Top each with a slice of Canadian-style bacon, then a tomato slice; or, if using poached eggs, top muffins or toast with tomato slices, then eggs. Set aside.
For cheese sauce, in a heavy medium saucepan combine cheese, milk, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and red pepper. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, till cheese melts.
Slowly stir about half of the hot cheese sauce into beaten egg; return all to the saucepan. Cook and stir over low heat till cheese sauce thickens slightly and just bubbles.
Serve cheese sauce immediately over English muffin or toast stacks.

notes: Beer Rarebit: Prepare as above, except substitute 8 slices crisp-cooked bacon, drained and halved crosswise, for the Canadian-style bacon or poached eggs. Substitute beer for the milk.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Meatless Tacos
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: 1 1/4- or 1 1/2-ounce envelope (5 teaspoons) taco seasoning mix
tofu (fresh bean curd), drained and finely chopped

instructions.text: Rinse lentils; drain. In a medium saucepan combine lentils, onion, and 1/2 cup water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 30 minutes or till tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir tomato sauce and seasoning mix into lentils. Simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Stir in tofu; heat through. Spoon into taco shells. Top with lettuce, tomato, cheese, and salsa.

notes: Bulgur Tacos: Prepare as above, except substitute bulgur for lentils. Cover and simmer bulgur, onion, and 3/4 cup water about 10 minutes or till tender and liquid is absorbed.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Garbanzo Sandwich Spread
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Serve this spread for lunch in pita bread or on bagels, or as appetizer on party rye bread.

instructions.text: In a blender container or food processor bowl combine beans, tahini, juice, oil, garlic, paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cover, blend or process till smooth, scraping sides as necessary. Transfer to a bowl. Stir in parsley and pimiento. Cover; chill 2 to 24 hours.

notes: Mediterranean Sandwich: Spread about 1/3 cup cold Garbanzo Sandwich Spread on 1 slice whole wheat bread. Top with 2 tomato slices, 1 slice Swiss or brick cheese, and another slice bread. Makes 1 serving.
Tahini Substitute: Stir together 3 tablespoons creamy peanut butter and 1 tablespoon sesame oil till well combined. Makes 1/4 cup.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Fried-Rice Supper
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The rice is chilled to keep it from sticking.

instructions.text: In a large skillet melt the 1 teaspoon margarine. Add beaten egg. Cook egg without stirring till set. Invert skillet to remove egg; cut into strips. In the skillet cook onions and garlic in the 1 tablespoon margarine till tender. Add rice; cook and stir for 3 minutes. Stir in beans, soy sauce, sherry, oil, and red pepper. Cook and stir till heated through. Toss with nuts and egg strips.

assumptions: Inferred 0.25 for ground red pepper (standard quantity)

recipes.title: Bean and Cheese Burritos
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

instructions.text: Stack six 8-inch flour tortillas and wrap in foil. Heat in a 350° oven for 10 minutes to soften. In a skillet cook 1 cup chopped onion in 1 tablespoon cooking oil till tender. Add one 16-ounce can refried beans. Cook and stir till heated through.

Spoon about 1/4 cup bean mixture onto each tortilla just below center. Divide 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar cheese among tortillas. Fold edge nearest filling up and over just till mixture is covered. Fold in 2 sides just till they meet; roll up. Place on a baking sheet. Bake in a 350° oven about 10 minutes or till heated through. Serve with shredded lettuce and salsa.

notes: Bean and Cheese Chimichangas: Prepare as above, except use 10-inch flour tortillas and omit baking. Secure rolled-up tortillas with wooden toothpicks. In a 3-quart saucepan fry tortillas, 2 or 3 at a time, in 1 inch hot cooking oil (375°) about 1 minute on each side or till golden. Drain. Keep warm in a 300° oven. Remove picks. Pass dairy sour cream and guacamole.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Marinated Salmon Steaks
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut steaks into serving-size portions. For marinating, in a shallow dish, combine lime peel, lemon or lime juice, oil, Worcestershire sauce, rosemary or thyme, garlic, and pepper.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen salmon (or halibut) steaks, 1 inch thick
finely shredded lemon, lime or orange peel

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut steaks into serving-size portions. For marinating, in a shallow dish, combine lime peel, lemon or lime juice, oil, Worcestershire sauce, rosemary or thyme, garlic, and pepper.

Place fish in marinade, turning to coat. Cover; marinate fish in the refrigerator for 30 minutes or till fish is opaque, turning steaks occasionally. Add 1 tablespoon water, if necessary, to keep fish moist.

Drain fish, reserving marinade. Place fish steaks on a greased unheated rack of a broiler pan. Brush with marinade. Broil 4 inches from the heat for 5 minutes. Using a wide spatula, carefully turn fish over. Brush with marinade. Broil for 3 to 7 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

notes: Grill directions: Place fish steaks on a greased grill rack. Grill directly over medium-hot coals for 5 minutes. Using a wide spatula, carefully turn fish. Grill for 3 to 7 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

recipes.title: Herbed Sauce for Fish
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Here's an easy sauce to brush over fish during baking or broiling (see chart, page 185). In a small saucepan melt 3 tablespoons margarine or butter.

ingredients.item: dried dillweed or dried basil, rosemary, or oregano, crushed; and/or snipped parsley

instructions.text: In a small saucepan melt 3 tablespoons margarine or butter. Stir in lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon dried dillweed or dried basil, rosemary, or oregano, crushed, and/or 1 tablespoon snipped parsley, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Brush with margarine mixture. Grill for 3 to 7 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

recipes.servings_yield: Makes about 1/4 cup (enough for 1 pound of fillets)

recipes.title: Halibut with Sherry Sauce
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen halibut or other fish steaks, cut 1 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Place fish on the greased unheated rack of a broiler pan. Sprinkle with pepper. Broil 4 inches from the heat 5 minutes. Turn fish. Brush with remaining margarine. Broil 3 to 7 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork.
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan stir together sour cream, milk, mustard, chives, and a dash pepper. Cook till hot (do not boil). Serve over fish.

recipes.title: Dijon-Mustard Fillets
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish. Place fish on the unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from the heat till fish flakes easily per 1/2-inch thickness (Allow 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness). Turn once if more than 1 inch thick.
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan stir together sour cream, milk, mustard, chives, and a dash pepper. Cook till hot (do not boil). Serve over fish.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Shark
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Use 1 pound fresh or frozen shark, swordfish, tuna, or halibut steaks, cut 1 inch thick.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen shark, swordfish, tuna, or halibut steaks, cut 1 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Place fish on greased unheated rack of broiler pan. Combine seasoning; rub onto fish. Cover; chill for 30 minutes to 2 hours. Brush with melted margarine or butter.
Broil 4 inches from the heat for 5 minutes. Turn fish. Brush with remaining margarine. Broil for 3 to 7 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

recipes.title: Swordfish Kabobs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Swordfish, tuna, or shark make great kabobs because of their firm, meatlike texture.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen swordfish, tuna, or shark steaks, cut 1 inch thick
large green onions, cut into 2-inch lengths
finely shredded orange or cherry tomato peel

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut into 1-inch cubes. Place fish, mushrooms, and onions in a plastic bag; set bag into a bowl. Combine oil, wine, garlic, orange peel, and 1/4 teaspoon salt; add to bag. Seal bag and marinate at room temperature for 2 hours, turning bag occasionally. Drain fish and vegetables for 30 minutes.

On eight 12-inch skewers alternately thread fish cubes, mushrooms, and onions, leaving about 1/4 inch between pieces. Place kabobs on the greased unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from the heat for 4 to 5 minutes. Turn kabobs over. Broil for 4 to 6 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Brush again with sauce during the last 2 minutes of grilling. Brush again with sauce before serving.

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Fish Kabobs
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Complete this Oriental-style meal with fried rice and buttered green peas.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen swordfish, sea bass, shark, or tuna steaks, cut 1 inch thick
medium green or sweet red pepper, cut into 6 or 8 medium-size chunks

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut fish into 1-inch cubes. Cook fish in a small amount of boiling salted water for 10 to 12 minutes or till nearly cooked. (Cook and stir for 10 minutes if the sauce is very thick). Drain.

For the sauce, in a small bowl combine 1/4 cup of pineapple juice, preserves, and lemon juice, leaving the rest for another use. Add fish cubes and 1/4 inch between alternately thread fish, leaving about 1/4 inch between pieces. Place kabobs on the greased unheated rack of a broiler pan. Broil 4 inches from the heat for 5 minutes. Turn pan. Broil for 4 to 5 minutes more or till fish flakes easily with a fork, brushing with sauce during the last 2 minutes of broiling. Brush again with sauce before serving.

recipes.title: Blackened Redfish
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Stand back! This Cajun specialty really smokes as it cooks. That's why it's best to grill it outdoors.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen redfish or other fish fillets (about 1/2 inch thick)

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish. Place some of the melted margarine on a cast-iron skilled grill rack; sprinkle evenly on both sides of fish for some of the melt 12-inch well-seasoned cast-iron skillet. Heat until very hot, about 5 minutes. Meanwhile, brush fish with remaining margarine.
Place fish in pan. Cook, uncovered, over high, for 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 minutes per side or till fish flakes easily with a fork, turning once. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Fish with Beer-Cheese Sauce
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The tangy cheese sauce tastes great over catfish, halibut, flounder, or sole fillets or steaks.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen fish fillets or steaks

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish. In a lightly greased 10x6x2-inch baking dish, arrange fish in a single layer, tucking under thin edges. Bake in a 450° oven for 4 to 6 minutes per 1/2-inch thickness or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

Meanwhile, for sauce, cook onion in margarine till tender. Stir in flour, a pinch salt, and pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Add cheese and, if desired, caraway seed. Stir till cheese melts. Stir in beer. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Add cheese and beer; cook and stir till cheese melts. Spoon over fish.

recipes.title: Citrus Baked Halibut
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen halibut steaks, chopped onion

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Arrange fish in an 8x8x2-inch baking dish. Cook onion and garlic in margarine till tender. Stir in paprika. Spread over fish. Pour lemon juice over all. Cover with vented plastic wrap or foil. Bake in a 400° oven for 7 to 9 minutes or till fish is done, giving dish a half-turn once. Serve as above.

recipes.title: Broccoli-Stuffed Sole
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen sole or other skinless fish fillets (about 1/4 inch thick)
cheese with chives and onion, softened

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. For stuffing, cook and drain broccoli. In a saucepan cook broccoli; milk, and wine till heated through. Stir in cheese; add to Parmesan cheese. Stir till end cheese melts. Spread stuffing onto end of each fillet. Roll up. Place, seam side down, in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or till fish is cooked and stuffing is hot. Serve with lemon wedges, if desired. Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

recipes.title: Baked Fish with Mushrooms
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen fish fillets or steaks, cut 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Arrange fish in a 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish, turning under thin edges. Sprinkle with mushrooms, onion, and tarragon in margarine till tender. Spoon over fish; sprinkle with paprika. Bake, covered, in a 450° oven for 6 to 10 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

recipes.title: Wild-Rice-Stuffed Fish
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Two mid-western delicacies—wild rice and whitefish—from the Great Lakes region. Combine them for a memorable entrée.

ingredients.item: dressed whitefish or other fish (about 2 to 2 1/2 pounds)

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Rinse rice thoroughly; drain. In a medium saucepan cook mushrooms, onion, and garlic in margarine or butter. Stir in broth, sherry, and lemon peel. Cover and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes or till rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Stir in pimiento.
Place fish in a well-greased large, shallow baking pan. Spoon stuffing into fish cavity; press lightly to flatten. Cover with foil.
Bake fish in a 350° oven for 30 to 40 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Use two large spatulas to transfer fish to a serving plate.

recipes.title: Fish en Papillote
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: En papillote (pah-pee-YOHT) is French for 'in paper.' It's a simple yet elegant way to cook fish.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen skinless pompano, perch, sole, or flounder fish fillets (about 1/2 inch thick)

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Cut 4 pieces of parchment paper into heart shapes, 12 inches wide and 9 inches long. In a large skillet bring water, lemon slices, bay leaf, and bouillon granules to boiling; add fish in a single layer. Return liquid to boiling. Simmer, covered, for 4 to 6 minutes or till fish flakes easily. Using a slotted spoon, remove fish.

For sauce, in the same skillet cook carrot and onion in margarine till tender. Stir in flour and mustard. Add reserved liquid. Cook and stir till bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Add milk. Cook and stir till mixture boils. Cook and stir 1 minute more.

To assemble each packet, place one fillet on half of each parchment heart. Top with one-fourth of the sauce. Fold the other half of the heart over fillet. Starting at the top, seal by turning up edges of heart and folding in tightly; twist tip of heart to seal. Place packets on a large baking sheet. Bake in a 400° oven for 10 to 12 minutes or till slightly puffed. Transfer to dinner plates. To serve, cut an X in top of each. Pull back the paper.

missing_inputs: Not in database: parchment paper or brown paper

recipes.title: Chilled Salmon Steaks
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Serve with Tartar Sauce (see page 367).

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen salmon or halibut steaks, cut 3/4 to 1 inch thick

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Add fish to boiling Court Bouillon or water. Return to boiling. Simmer, covered, 8 to 12 minutes or till fish flakes easily with fork.
Remove fish. For marinade, combine oil in a screwcap jar with milk. Shake well. Pour over fish and vegetables. Cover and chill 4 to 24 hours. Spoon marinade over fish occasionally. Drain.

Court Bouillon: Simmer 2 cups water, 1 sliced celery stalk, 1 medium carrot, sliced, 2 tablespoons sliced onion, 1 bay leaf, 3 whole peppercorns, and 1/4 teaspoon salt, covered, 8 cups water for 30 minutes. Strain.

recipes.title: Poached Fish with Dill Sauce
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. In a fish poacher or a large roasting pan that has a wire rack with handles, add enough water to almost reach the rack. Add bay leaf, tarragon, and 3 lemon slices. Place pan over two burners on range top. Bring to boiling.
Lower fish on rack into pan. Simmer, covered, for 35 to 40 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork. Remove fish. Keep warm. Reserve 1 cup cooking liquid.
For dill sauce, cooking liquid. Stir in 1/4 teaspoon dried dillweed, 1/2 teaspoon sugar, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and dash pepper. Stir in 1 beaten egg yolk; return to saucepan. Cook and stir till bubbly.

recipes.title: Vegetable-Topped Fillets
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Serve a colorful zucchini, squash, but use just summer squash if you wish.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen sole, orange roughy, or other fish fillets (about 1/2 inch thick)

instructions.text: In a large skillet bring chicken broth just to boiling. Carefully add fish. Return to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer 4 to 6 minutes or till fish flakes easily with a fork.

Meanwhile, in another skillet cook vegetables and savory over medium-high heat in oil till vegetables are tender-crisp. Drain. Add remaining vegetables. Cook 4 to 6 minutes more or till vegetables are crisp-tender. Sprinkle with pepper. Spoon vegetables over fish.

missing_inputs: Not in database: dried summer savory, crushed

recipes.title: Trout Amandine
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The perfect recipe for freshly caught pan-dressed fish—your catch of the day or frozen market fish.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen pan-dressed trout or other fish (about 8 ounces each)

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Bone fish, if desired. Stir together egg and milk. Stir together flour and salt. Dip fish into egg mixture, then into flour mixture.

Cook fish in hot oil for 5 to 6 minutes per side or till golden, skin side up. Fry fish on one side until golden. Turn and fry on the other side till golden. Remove fish to a serving platter; keep warm.
Melt margarine in same skillet; stir in almonds. Cook and stir till almonds are lightly browned. Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice. Spoon over fish.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Fish
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: The crispy coating seals in the fresh fish flavor.

ingredients.item: fresh or frozen fish fillets (1/4 to 1 inch thick)
cornmeal or fine dry bread crumbs
shortening or cooking oil for frying

instructions.text: Thaw fish, if frozen. Measure thickness of fish. Cut into serving-size portions. Pat dry. In a shallow dish combine egg and 2 tablespoons water. In another dish, mix cornmeal or bread crumbs, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and dash pepper. Dip fish into egg mixture, then coat with cornmeal mixture.

recipes.title: Boiled Lobster
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Simple boiled whole lobster with clarified butter

instructions.text: In a 12-quart Dutch oven bring 8 quarts water and 2 tsp salt to boiling. Use two 1 to 1 1/4-pound live lobsters. Grasp each lobster just behind the eyes; rinse lobsters under cold running water.
Quickly plunge lobsters headfirst into the boiling water. Return to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Drain lobsters.

Place each lobster on its back. With kitchen shears, cut the membrane on the tail to expose the tail meat. Cut through the underside from head to tail. Remove the black vein near the head and the small sac (found only in the head). Reserve any red roe or green tomalley.
Remove the meat from claws. Twist the large claws with the body; remove meat using a nutcracker. Serve with Clarified Butter. Makes 2 servings.

notes: Clarified Butter: Melt 3/4 cup butter over very low heat without stirring; cool slightly. Pour off clear top layer; discard milky bottom layer. Makes 1/2 cup.

recipes.title: Tomato Juice
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Home-canned tomato juice with optional freezing instructions

instructions.text: Thoroughly wash 8 pounds ripe but firm tomatoes. Remove stems. Core and cut into pieces; drain.
Place tomatoes in an 8- or 10-quart kettle. Bring to boiling over low heat, stirring frequently. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes or till soft; stir often to prevent sticking.
Press tomatoes through a food mill or sieve. Discard solids. Return tomato juice to the kettle and bring to boiling.
Boil gently, uncovered, for 5 minutes, stirring often. Discard solids.
Pour hot juice into hot, clean pint jar or 2 tablespoons lemon juice to each quart jar. Pour hot juice into jars, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace.
Process pints for 35 minutes, quarts for 40 minutes in a boiling-water canner.

notes: Boiling-Water Canning: Add 1 tablespoon lemon juice to each hot, clean pint jar or 2 tablespoons lemon juice to each quart jar. If desired, add 1/4 teaspoon salt to each pint or 1/2 teaspoon salt to each quart jar.
Freezing: Cool tomato juice. Pour into wide-top freezer containers, leaving a 1/2-inch headspace. Seal, label, and freeze.

ingredients.prep_note: thinly sliced and separated into rings

instructions.text: For dressing, mash half of the avocado. Stir together mashed avocado, sour cream, lemon juice, celery salt, and hot pepper sauce. Stir in milk till desired consistency. Cover and chill while preparing salad.
For salad, combine spinach, garbanzo beans, tomatoes, cucumber, cauliflower, mushrooms, onion, and walnuts. Slice one hard-cooked egg.

Slice remaining avocado half; brush with additional lemon juice, if desired. Add sliced egg and avocado to salad. Top with dressing; toss to mix. Cut the remaining egg into wedges. Garnish salad with egg wedges. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Marinated Vegetable Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Colorful mixed vegetables in herb-oregano marinade

instructions.text: Cook 2 cups small cauliflower flowerets, 2 cups bias-sliced green beans cut into 1-inch pieces, 2 medium carrots, thinly sliced; 1 cup coarsely chopped green pepper; and 1 medium onion, sliced and separated into rings, in a small amount of boiling water for 5 minutes or till crisp-tender.
Drain; transfer to a bowl. Stir in 1 small zucchini, thinly sliced, and 1/4 cup halved pitted ripe olives.

For marinade, in a screw-top jar combine 1/2 cup white wine vinegar; 1/3 cup salad oil; 2 teaspoons sugar; 1 1/2 teaspoons dried oregano, crushed; 1/2 teaspoon salt; and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Cover and shake well. Pour marinade over hot vegetables. Cover; chill for 4 to 24 hours, stirring occasionally. Serve with a slotted spoon. Makes 8 side-dish servings.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Wilted Spinach Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Warm spinach salad with hot bacon dressing

instructions.text: Combine spinach, mushrooms, and green onion. If desired, sprinkle with pepper. Set aside.

In a 12-inch skillet cook bacon till crisp. Remove bacon, reserving drippings in skillet. Crumble bacon; set aside. Stir vinegar, sugar, and 1/4 teaspoon salt into drippings. Heat to boiling; remove from heat. Add the spinach mixture. Toss till coated.
Transfer to a serving dish. Top with chopped egg and bacon. Serve immediately. Makes 4 side-dish servings.

notes: Microwave directions: Combine spinach, mushrooms, and onion. If desired, sprinkle with pepper. Set aside. In a 2-quart casserole microwave bacon, covered, on 100% power (high) for 3 to 5 minutes or till crisp. Remove bacon, reserving drippings in casserole. Crumble bacon; set aside. Stir vinegar, sugar, and salt into drippings. Cook, covered, for 30 to 45 seconds or till boiling. Add spinach mixture. Toss till coated. Top with chopped egg and bacon. Serve immediately.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Creamy Cucumbers
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Cool cucumber slices in creamy sour cream dressing

ingredients.item: dairy sour cream or plain yogurt

ingredients.prep_note: halved lengthwise and thinly sliced (about 3 cups)
thinly sliced and separated into rings

instructions.text: Stir together sour cream; vinegar; sugar; dillweed, if desired; 1 teaspoon salt and dash pepper.
Add cucumber and onion slices; toss to coat. Cover; chill for 2 to 48 hours, stirring often. Stir before serving. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

notes: Marinated Cucumbers: Prepare as above, except omit sour cream and dillweed. Increase vinegar or lemon juice to 1/4 cup and sugar to 2 tablespoons. If desired, stir 1/2 teaspoon celery seed into vinegar mixture. Cover and chill for 2 hours or up to 5 days, stirring occasionally.

recipes.title: Pea-Cheese Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Colorful salad with peas, cheese, and hard-cooked eggs

ingredients.item: diced pimiento or sweet red pepper

instructions.text: Cook frozen peas according to package directions. Thoroughly drain the cooked or canned peas. Cool cooked peas.
In a large bowl combine peas, cheese cubes, hard-cooked eggs, celery, onion, and pimiento or sweet red pepper. Combine mayonnaise or salad dressing, salt, and pepper. Add to pea mixture; toss to mix.

Cover and chill for 4 to 24 hours. Stir mixture well. If desired, cut each tomato into 8 wedges, cutting to, but not through, the bottom. Place tomatoes atop lettuce. Fill tomatoes with pea mixture. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: 24-Hour Vegetable Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Layered make-ahead salad with vegetables, bacon, and cheese

ingredients.item: torn iceberg lettuce, romaine, leaf lettuce, Bibb lettuce, or fresh spinach
sliced fresh mushrooms or broccoli flowerets, or frozen peas
shredded Swiss, American, or cheddar cheese

instructions.text: Place lettuce or spinach in the bottom of a bowl, about 8 inches in diameter. If desired, sprinkle with salt and pepper. Layer mushrooms, broccoli, or peas atop. Then layer carrots. Arrange egg slices and bacon over vegetables.

Top with 1/2 cup of the cheese and the green onions. For dressing, combine mayonnaise, lemon juice, and, if desired, dillweed. Spread dressing over top of salad, sealing to edge of bowl. Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Cover and chill for 2 to 24 hours. Before serving, toss to coat the vegetables. Sprinkle with additional sliced green onion, if desired. Makes 6 to 8 side-dish servings.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: Carrot-Raisin Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Sweet and crunchy carrot salad with raisins and apples

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl combine carrots, apple, and raisins. Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Add mayonnaise or salad dressing. Stir gently to coat well. Cover and chill for 2 to 24 hours. (If dressing becomes too thick, stir in a little milk.)
Before serving, sprinkle with toasted almonds, if desired. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

recipes.title: Creamy Potato Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Classic American potato salad with eggs and mustard

instructions.text: In a covered saucepan cook potatoes in boiling water for 20 to 25 minutes or till just tender; drain well. Peel and cube potatoes.
In a very large bowl combine celery, green pepper, onion, mayonnaise or salad dressing, vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper. Add potatoes and eggs. Toss lightly to mix.
Cover and chill for 6 to 24 hours. Makes 12 side-dish servings.

recipes.title: Marinated Potato Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Elegant potato salad with artichoke hearts and vinaigrette

ingredients.prep_note: see recipe, page 358, or other oil and vinegar dressing

instructions.text: In a covered saucepan cook potatoes in boiling salted water for 15 to 20 minutes or just till tender; drain well. Cut potatoes into quarters.
In a large bowl pour dressing over potatoes. Add artichoke hearts, green pepper, tomatoes, onion, olives, and parsley. Toss gently to mix.
Cover and chill for 4 to 24 hours, stirring occasionally. Transfer to a serving bowl. Garnish with kale leaf, if desired. Makes 4 or 5 side-dish servings.

nutrition.source: Better Homes and Gardens cookbook nutrition analysis

recipes.title: German-Style Potato Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Warm potato salad with bacon and tangy dressing

ingredients.prep_note: chopped; 2 slices bacon, cooked, drained, and crumbled, optional

instructions.text: In a covered saucepan cook potatoes in boiling salted water for 20 to 25 minutes or till just tender; drain well. Cool slightly. Peel and slice potatoes. Set aside while preparing dressing.
For dressing, in a large skillet cook 4 slices bacon till crisp. Drain and crumble, reserving 2 tablespoons drippings. Set the bacon aside. Add chopped onion to reserved drippings. Cook till tender.

Stir in flour, sugar, salt, celery seed, and pepper. Stir in water and vinegar. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in potatoes and bacon. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes more or till heated through, stirring gently. Season to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl. Garnish with hard-cooked egg, parsley, or additional bacon, if desired. Makes 4 side-dish servings.

recipes.title: Cajun-Style Rice Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Spicy rice salad with shrimp and Cajun seasonings

instructions.text: In a mixing bowl gently stir together rice, green pepper, shrimp, mushrooms, hard-cooked egg, and parsley. Set aside.
For dressing, in a screw-top jar combine salad oil, vinegar, water, paprika, horseradish, onion salt, and red pepper. Cover and shake well. Pour dressing over rice mixture. Toss to coat.
Cover and chill for 4 to 24 hours. Serve on lettuce leaves. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

assumptions: Used standard can size (0.5 cups) for shrimp

recipes.title: Barley Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Nutty grain salad with barley, carrots, and lemon

ingredients.item: fresh snipped basil or dried basil
chopped peanuts or cashews, or toasted slivered almonds

instructions.text: In a saucepan combine chicken broth and barley. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes or till liquid is absorbed.
In a mixing bowl combine barley, carrot, and parsley. For dressing, in a screw-top jar combine water, salad oil, lemon juice, basil, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Cover and shake well.
Pour dressing over barley mixture. Toss to coat. Cover and chill for 4 to 24 hours. Stir in nuts before serving. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Fruit Salad
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Warm fruit salad with cinnamon-apricot dressing

instructions.text: For dressing, in a blender container or food processor bowl place undrained apricots. Cover and blend or process till smooth.
In a saucepan combine blended apricots, sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove cinnamon.
Meanwhile, in a mixing bowl stir together orange slices and pineapple chunks. Add dressing; stirring carefully to coat. Cover and chill for several hours.
Just before serving, stir in strawberry halves. Spoon fruit mixture onto 6 lettuce-lined plates. If desired, garnish with fresh mint sprigs. Makes 6 side-dish servings.

assumptions: Assumed 1.5 cup can for unpeeled apricot halves
Used standard can size (1.5 cups) for pineapple chunks
Assumed 1 unit for fresh mint sprigs

recipes.title: Fruit-Filled Melons
recipes.attribution: Better Homes and Gardens New Cook Book
recipes.description: Cantaloupe bowls filled with fresh fruit and ginger dressing

instructions.text: Cut each cantaloupe in half and remove the seeds. Use a melon baller to scoop out pulp, reserving shells. Set aside 2 cups melon balls; reserve remaining melon for another use. Trim a thin slice from the bottom of each melon shell.
In a bowl mix the 2 cups melon balls, orange, apple, peach, blueberries, and strawberries. For dressing, stir together yogurt, mayonnaise, brown sugar, and gingerroot.
Line each melon shell with lettuce leaves. Divide fruit among melon shells. Top each with one fourth of the dressing. Makes 4 side-dish servings.
Note: If desired, sprinkle with lemon juice to keep fruit from darkening (see tip, page 351).
Mix the biscuit mix, margarine, and milk well; refrigerate 1/2 hour.
Meanwhile, mix the sausages and green chiles and let stand to room temperature.

Divide the dough in half. Roll out each piece to a large rectangle about 1/4 inch thick. Spread half of the sausage mixture completely over each piece of dough; roll up as for a jelly roll. Wrap in plastic wrap and freeze for 1 hour.
Remove from freezer and slice 1/4 inch thick. Freeze until ready to use. Then place the frozen slices on a cookie sheet and bake in preheated 400-degree oven for 20 minutes.
This is the perfect accompaniment to breakfast eggs, and it also makes a terrific appetizer.
Saute the onion in heated butter. Add the tortillas and chile powder, stirring well to coat the tortillas with powder. Cook until browned.
Add the eggs, green chiles, salt, and pepper; scramble.
Sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese and parsley.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Melt the butter in a skillet and saute the garlic and ham for 2 minutes. Add the mushrooms and green chiles and saute 2 more minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sour cream, parsley, and oregano. Allow the mixture to stand for 10 minutes to blend flavors; then turn it into a buttered 1-quart casserole.
With a mixing spoon, make 6 rounded hollows in the chile mixture; break an egg into each hollow. Season with salt and pepper.

Bake about 20 minutes or until the egg whites are set. Sprinkle the grated cheese over the casserole and return it to the oven until the cheese is bubbling and the yolks are set, about 5 to 10 minutes more.
Garnish with olive slices.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Butter custard cups and break an egg into each. Add 2 tablespoons green chile sauce or salsa and top with a small slice of cheese.
Place cups in a pan of hot water and bake until eggs are set.

recipes.title: Baked Eggs with Cheese and Chile

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
Whirl the eggs, milk, and cheese in a blender until mixed. Add the green chiles, salt, and pepper and pour into a buttered 9-inch square baking dish.
Bake for 25 minutes. Great for brunch or lunch or cold as an appetizer.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.

Butter an 8-inch square baking dish. Fry the bacon until almost done and drain off the excess grease. Mix the bacon with the corn, chiles, sugar, garlic powder, and salt. Spread the mixture evenly in the baking dish.
Mix the cream, eggs, and salt to taste and pour over the chile mixture. Sprinkle the cheese on top. Place on the center rack of oven and bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until the eggs are set.

recipes.title: Egg and Chile Omelet

instructions.text: Butter the bread and cut the slices in cubes. Layer the bread cubes, grated cheese, and chopped chiles in a 9-inch square baking dish.
Combine the remaining ingredients and pour over the bread cubes, cheese, and chiles. Let stand in the refrigerator overnight.
Cover and bake for 1 hour at 325 degrees. Remove the cover and bake 5 minutes more or until puffy and set.

notes: Make ahead - refrigerate overnight before baking

instructions.text: Prepare the pancake or waffle mix according to the package directions and set aside.

Crumble the sausage and saute it until well done. Drain off the fat. Reserve 3 tablespoons of the sausage and mix the rest along with 1/2 cup green chiles and 1/8 teaspoon of each of the spices into the pancake or waffle mix.

Empty the soup into a pan and add the milk, remaining chiles, and remaining spices. Add the salt and stir together. Heat the mixture to boiling and simmer 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and keep warm.
Prepare either pancakes or waffles and serve them hot with the cheese-chile sauce and sprinkled with reserved sausage. Great for breakfast or dinner.
In a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, combine all the ingredients except the parsley and heat to boiling. Reduce the heat; simmer, covered, for 5 minutes.
Strain the mixture into an 8-inch square pan; stir in the parsley. Cover and freeze until solid.

When ready to serve, let the mixture stand at room temperature 15 to 20 minutes, loosening it up with a spoon. Beat the mixture with an electric mixer until smooth, but not melted. Spoon it into sherbet glasses or appetizer dishes. Garnish each serving with a sprig of parsley.
Blend the cheeses together. Add all the other ingredients and mix well. Divide the mixture into 2 or 3 pieces and form each into a roll or form the mixture into 1 large ball.
Coat it with chili powder, crushed peanuts, or chopped nuts. Wrap in waxed paper and refrigerate; slice and serve on crackers.
Mix all the ingredients and serve with tostados or chips.

recipes.title: Chicken Livered Cheese 'n Chile Puffs

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Pat the chicken livers dry; then fry them in heated oil until brown and well cooked. Cool them and chop finely.

Heat the butter and saute the onion and garlic until limp. Add the tomato, chicken bouillon, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook until very soft and mushy. Remove from the heat and cool. Add the livers and stir well.
Blend the softened cream cheese with the mayonnaise. Add the chiles and horseradish and mix thoroughly. Stir in the parsley flakes.
Combine the cheese and liver mixtures and pour into a shallow 1-quart casserole. Bake, uncovered, for 15 minutes or until slightly browned. Remove from the oven and cool.
Prepare Cornmeal Puffs (see recipe on next page).

notes: Serve with Cornmeal Puffs

recipes.title: Cornmeal Puffs

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Bring the water to a boil. Mix the dry ingredients together and add the margarine to the boiling water and stir until melted. Turn the heat to low.
Add the dry ingredients all at once, stirring vigorously. Cook until the mixture draws away from the sides of the pan as you stir.
Remove from heat and cool for 1 minute. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition until the batter is smooth.
Drop the batter by 1/2 teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheets, 1 1/2 inches apart. Sprinkle each lightly with paprika. Bake for 15 minutes or until golden.

Allow the puffs to cool completely. Then gently slice off the top half of each puff, fill with the cooled chile-liver mixture, and replace the top. Refrigerate the puffs from 1 to 5 hours before serving.

notes: Serve with Chicken Livered Cheese 'n Chile Puffs filling

recipes.title: Seviche

instructions.text: Place the scallops in a glass or ceramic bowl and add the remaining ingredients. If you have any concern about the source or freshness of the scallops, they may be poached lightly before marinating.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours, stirring occasionally, before serving.

notes: If concerned about freshness, poach scallops lightly before marinating

ingredients.prep_note: shredded (or any cheese that melts well)

instructions.text: Cook the broccoli according to the package directions. Drain well.
Add the soup, garlic, cheese, and green chiles. Heat until the cheese melts.
Serve warm with corn chips.
Simmer the tomatoes and onions about 20 minutes. Cool the mixture until it is only warm. Add the rest of the ingredients and stir to the desired consistency for a dip.
Serve with tostados.
Mix all the ingredients. Serve with tortilla chips or potato chips.
Combine all ingredients and chill.
Roast, peel, and chop the green chiles. Cut the onion, avocado, and tomato in pieces and put in a blender with the chiles, cheese, cumin, and salt.
Blend at high speed 4 or 5 minutes until well blended.
Serve with corn chips, potato chips, or crackers.
Mix the cream cheese, mayonnaise, cottage cheese, garlic salt, and salt in a blender.
Stir in the chives and green chiles. Serve with potato chips or corn chips.

recipes.title: Traditional Chile con Queso

instructions.text: Saute the onion and garlic in butter until soft. Add the tomato, green chiles, and seasonings and cook over low heat or in the top of a double boiler.
Stir in the cheese and cook until it melts.
Serve with tortilla chips.

notes: Variation: Add 1 1/2 lbs ground beef, browned.

Variation: Omit the tomatoes and add 1 16-oz can tomatoes with green chiles, 8 drops Tabasco sauce, 2 teaspoons flavor enhancer, and 2 tablespoons hot butter. At the last minute add 1/2 can (5 oz) evaporated milk or enough so that the mixture is the right consistency. Serve with corn chips or vegetables.

ingredients.prep_note: seeds and pulp removed and minced

instructions.text: Place all the ingredients in the top of a double boiler. Melt slowly, stirring, until the mixture is smooth. Serve with chips.

recipes.title: Mrs. Mondragon's Cocktail Meatballs

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees.
Mix the first 6 ingredients together in a large mixing bowl until well blended. Shape the mixture into 1-inch balls. Bake them for 10 minutes.
Saute the mushroom slices in 2 tablespoons butter. Melt 1/4 cup margarine in a saucepan and blend in the flour. Cook a few minutes, stir in the milk, and continue stirring constantly until thickened.
Add the salt, sour cream, mushrooms, green chiles, and pimentos, stirring to blend. Spoon the red chile sauce over the meatballs.

notes: Includes Red Chile Sauce recipe

recipes.title: Red Chile Sauce

instructions.text: Melt the shortening, add the flour, and stir. Add the chile powder and continue to stir until mixed.
Gradually add the chicken broth and stir until there are no lumps.
Season with salt and garlic powder and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.

notes: Use with Mrs. Mondragon's Cocktail Meatballs

recipes.title: Chile-Cheese Squares

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Layer the cheese and chiles in a buttered baking dish. Pour the eggs over and dust with the paprika. Bake for 30 minutes or until it tests done.
Cut into small squares and serve as an appetizer.

notes: Variation: Use 1 lb cheddar cheese and 1 lb Monterey Jack cheese. Garnish with black olives and pimentos.

Variation: Use whole green chiles to line a pie pan. Spread 1/2 lb grated cheddar cheese over the chiles. Beat 6 eggs with 2 tablespoons cream and salt and pepper to taste. Pour the mixture over the cheese and chiles and bake as above.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Prepare the hot roll mix following the directions on the box. Break up the bacon, chop the onion, and mix together with the green chiles.
Divide the roll mix into 48 equal parts. Using your hands, spread out each piece and fill it with 1/2 to 3/4 teaspoon of the above mixture.
Pinch the rolls together and bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: Chile-Izzas

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Brown the ground beef and drain. Salt to taste.
Separate the biscuits and roll them out into circles. Place them on a greased cookie sheet and spread tomato sauce on them.
Add a layer of meat, then chiles, top with cheese. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes. Cut each circle into quarters and serve hot.

notes: Variation: Add sour cream or substitute pork sausage for the ground beef.

instructions.text: Wrap the franks in strips of green chile or slice them partially through and fill the openings with green chile sauce.
Wrap tortilla strips around the franks and secure them with toothpicks.
Fry them briefly in hot deep fat until crisp.
Combine the vinegar and salad oil. Rub a bowl with the cut garlic and add the diced tomato, onion, and green chiles. Let stand 5 minutes.
Add the vinegar and salad oil and toss gently. Serve on leaves or in the center of scoops of small curd cottage cheese.
Toss together the tomatoes, green chiles, onions, and lemon slices.
Add oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, and oregano. Cover and marinate in refrigerator at least 2 hours.
At serving time, remove the lemon slices and serve the salad in lettuce cups.
Dissolve the gelatin in 1 cup hot water in an 8 X 10-inch pan.
When lightly thickened, add the remaining ingredients. Chill.
Dissolve the gelatin according to the package directions. Stir in the remaining ingredients.
Place 12 large paper baking cups in muffin tins and spoon the gelatin mixture into cups in muffin tins.
Cook the bacon until crisp. Drain. Pour off all but 3 tablespoons of bacon drippings. Add the onion and potato and cook over medium heat, stirring, until the onion is lightly browned.
Add water, cover, and simmer until the potato is just tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the corn, soup, mushrooms, milk, and salt. Heat to boiling, lower the heat, add the chiles, and simmer a few minutes.
Serve in soup bowls or a tureen. Crumble bacon on top.
Mix all the ingredients in a bowl and chill for 6 to 8 hours.
Serve with crackers or French bread.

recipes.title: Fire Chief's Hot Stew

instructions.text: Roast, peel, and chop the fresh green chiles in 2 cups of water; cover the chiles, garlic, onion, and tomatoes for 1 hour.
Pressure cook the stew meat in 1 quart water for 15 minutes (or simmer, covered, for 1 hour). Reserve the meat liquid and add it to the chile mixture.
Add the diced potatoes and simmer 30 minutes longer.
Spoon into serving bowls and top with grated longhorn cheese, if desired.

notes: Variation: Add 2 cans (16 oz each) pinto beans or 2 cans (16 oz each) yellow hominy.
Variation: Substitute 2 lbs lean ground round (or cubed round steak).
Variation: Omit 1 can of tomatoes with green chiles and add 2 cups canned tomatoes, chopped.
Variation: For a heartier stew add 2 medium potatoes, diced, and 2 carrots, sliced.
Variation: Substitute 1 large can (46 oz) cocktail vegetable juice for the can of tomatoes with green chiles.

recipes.title: Chile con Carne de Venado (Chile with Venison)

instructions.text: Dredge the meat in flour and brown well. Add the onion and green pepper and cook until the onion is tender. Drain.
Add the remaining ingredients and simmer for 1 hour.
Rinse the beans and drain. Cover the beans with water and soak them for 2 hours, adding water to keep beans covered.
Cook the beans in the soaking water until soft, adding more water as necessary.
About 40 minutes before serving add the remaining ingredients and simmer. Serve with corn bread.

recipes.title: Chile Gumbo

instructions.text: Saute the onions and garlic with the salt pork until limp. Add the chopped tomatoes with their juice. Saute 10 minutes more.
Add the beef, stirring until it is browned. Add the vegetable juice, okra, green chiles, and bay leaf. Cook over medium heat 45 to 50 minutes, adding water if necessary.
Then add the black-eyed peas, parsley, and more water to maintain a soup-like consistency. Cook 20 minutes more, stirring occasionally.
Add the salt and chile powder. Cook 10 minutes more. Stir in the file powder and cook 3 to 5 minutes only. File powder loses its effect if heated. Serve in large bowls or with rice.

notes: File powder loses its effect if heated too long

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
In a large mixing bowl, combine all the ingredients except the bacon; mix thoroughly. Pour into a 2- or 3-quart ovenproof casserole or bean pot.
Top with the bacon and in 1-inch pieces. Bake for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Saute the onion and celery in oil; add the thawed broccoli. Simmer over low heat 15 minutes.
Add the soup, milk, water, rice, cheese, and chiles; bring the mixture to a boil.
Pour into a buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole. Bake for 25 minutes or until well heated.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Clean and cook the cauliflower until tender. Mash the cauliflower into a smooth paste. Add the butter, 1/4 cup wheat germ, cream, egg yolks, chiles, onion, and salt. Blend well.
Fold in the egg whites.
Pour the mixture into a buttered 2-quart casserole. Sprinkle with a small amount of wheat germ. Top with the grated cheese. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Combine all the ingredients and pour into a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Bake 50 minutes.

ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a heavy skillet and add the garlic and onion. Cook until the onion is translucent.
Using a sharp knife, cut the corn kernels off the cobs; then scrape the cobs to remove the corn milk. Add the kernels and corn milk to the pan.
Sprinkle with the curry powder, salt, and pepper; add the cream. Partially cover and simmer 20 to 30 minutes over very low heat. Stir in the chiles; cook 3 minutes longer and serve.

recipes.title: Cornfetti Casserole

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Mix together all the ingredients except the cheese and chiles and pour the mixture with chiles in a greased 2-quart casserole.
Top with the grated cheese. Bake for 1 hour or until set.

notes: Variation: Add 1 cup sour cream and 1 jar (2 oz) chopped pimentos to the mixture.

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a skillet and add the corn, chiles, and garlic. Cover and cook until the corn is tender, 10 to 15 minutes.
Add the seasonings. If the corn is too dry, add several tablespoons of boiling water while cooking.

recipes.title: Eggplant Olé

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees.
Grease two pizza pans. Dip the eggplant slices in butter, then in cornflake crumbs; sprinkle with salt. Place the slices on pans and cover each slice with strips of green chile.
Spoon enchilada sauce over each slice and generously sprinkle with grated cheese. Bake 15 minutes.
Freeze well.

notes: Freezes well

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a skillet and saute the onion, garlic, oregano, tomato, chiles, and chile powder over low heat about 10 minutes.
Add the garbanzos and salt; simmer 20 minutes.
