Add the berries to 3 cups good vinegar in a crock or large jar.
Cover the crock with cheesecloth and let stand three or four days, stirring daily.
When ready, strain without crushing the berries.
Measure, and add one pound sugar for each pint juice.
Boil gently for five minutes.
Put in bottles or jars and seal.

notes: When serving, dilute with water and crushed ice.
Use less sugar if a tart drink is preferred.

recipes.title: Blackberry Shrub
recipes.description: Traditional shrub drink made from blackberries and apple vinegar.

ingredients.prep_note: washed and selected, no sour or imperfect ones

instructions.text: Gather the blackberries, wash and select so that there will be no sour or imperfect ones.
Cover with apple vinegar (two years old) and cook until soft.
Strain, and sweeten the juice to taste.
Boil down until it is about the consistency of thick syrup.
Bottle and put in a cool, dark place.

notes: When serving, use three or four tablespoonfuls to a glass cold water.

recipes.title: Raspberry Pickles
recipes.description: Spiced pickled raspberries preserved in sweetened vinegar.

instructions.text: Wash 1/2 gallon fresh, almost ripe berries.
Place them in self-sealing jars with a half teaspoon each of cloves and allspice, and one stick of cinnamon.
Boil 1 1/2 pints of good apple vinegar with a half cup of sugar.
Pour over the berries.
Seal while hot.

recipes.title: Raspberry Vinegar
recipes.description: Sweetened raspberry-infused vinegar, a traditional Appalachian condiment.

instructions.text: Put two gallons ripe raspberries in a stone jar.
Pour a gallon cider vinegar over them and let stand twenty-four hours.
Drain, then pour the liquor over a gallon fresh berries and let stand overnight.
Strain and add one measure of sugar for every measure of juice.
Boil and skim.
Bottle when cold.

recipes.title: Sumac and Elderberry Jelly
recipes.description: Unique jelly combining wild sumac berries and elderberries.

instructions.text: Boil one pint sumac berries in three pints water until there is one quart juice.
Separately, boil one quart elderberries in three pints water until fruit is soft.
Mash the elderberries.
Strain juice from both through a thick white cloth.
Mix the juices together.
Add one cup sugar for each cup juice and cook into jelly.

recipes.title: Elderberry Wine
recipes.description: Traditional homemade wine from wild elderberries.

instructions.text: Use five quarts of berries to six quarts of water.
Mash the berries and let stand in a crock two weeks, stirring every day.
Strain.
Add as much sugar as you have juice.
Let stand two weeks and then bottle.

recipes.title: Elderberry Jam
recipes.description: Simple jam made from wild elderberries with vinegar.

instructions.text: Crush and measure the berries.
Add sugar and vinegar.
Boil until thick.
Pour boiling into scalded jars and seal.

recipes.title: Elderberry-Apple-Orange Jam
recipes.description: Rich jam combining elderberries with apples and citrus.

instructions.text: Cook apples until mushy.
Add the berries, oranges, and lemon chopped fine.
Grate the rinds of one orange and the lemon.
Mix together with sugar.
Boil thirty minutes.
Pour into sterilized jars and seal.

recipes.title: Steamed Elderberry Pudding
recipes.description: Traditional steamed pudding made with wild elderberries.

instructions.text: Sift dry ingredients (flour, baking powder, salt) together.
Work in the butter.
Add milk and mix well.
Combine sugar, berries, and lemon juice.
Mix these with the batter.
Pour into a buttered baking dish.
Cover tightly and steam forty-five minutes.
Serve with cream.

recipes.title: Ham with Pineapple Sauce
recipes.description: Baked ham glazed with a sweet pineapple sauce.

instructions.text: Place ham in a shallow baking pan.
Bake in 325°F oven for 1 1/4 to 2 1/4 hours.
Meanwhile combine pineapple juice, marmalade, and mustard.
Brush ham with glaze during last 30 minutes of baking.

recipes.title: Ham Caribbean
recipes.description: Ham baked with tropical fruit flavors including pineapple, orange juice, and rum.

instructions.text: Trim fat from ham. Place ham on rack in shallow baking pan.
Slash edges of ham at 1-inch intervals.
Bake in 350°F oven for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain pineapple; combine juice with brown sugar, cornstarch, and cloves.
Add orange juice, and if using, rum. Cook and stir till thickened.
Add pineapple chunks. Simmer in pineapple mixture and cloves.
Spoon over ham during last 10 minutes of baking.

recipes.title: Meat and Corn Bread Squares
recipes.description: Ground beef topped with cornbread, baked until golden.

instructions.text: In skillet cook beef and onion till brown. Drain fat.
Stir in chili powder and garlic salt.
Add undrained tomatoes and beans. Bring to boiling.
Transfer to 9x9x2-inch baking dish. Top with cheese.
Combine cornmeal, flour, and baking powder.
Mix milk, egg, and oil; add to dry ingredients. Stir just till moistened.
Spread over meat mixture.
Bake at 425°F for 20 to 25 minutes or till golden.

recipes.title: Meat and Pasta Bake
recipes.description: Easy casserole with ground beef, pasta, and cheese.

ingredients.item: condensed cream of mushroom or celery soup

instructions.text: Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain.
In large skillet cook meat and onion till meat is brown. Drain.
Stir in soup, half the cheese, milk, Worcestershire sauce, and herb.
Stir in cooked macaroni.
Transfer to 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Bake, covered, at 350°F for 30 minutes.
Uncover; top with remaining cheese. Bake 5 minutes more.

recipes.title: Hamburger Pie
recipes.description: Classic comfort food with seasoned ground beef and mashed potato topping.

instructions.text: In skillet cook beef and onion till meat is brown. Drain.
Add salt and pepper.
Stir in beans and soup. Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Combine mashed potatoes and egg.
Spoon potato mixture in mounds over meat.
Bake at 350°F for 25 to 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese. Bake 2 to 3 minutes more till cheese melts.

recipes.title: Chili-Mac Skillet
recipes.description: One-skillet meal combining chili and macaroni.

instructions.text: In large skillet cook meat and onion till meat is brown. Drain.
Stir in undrained tomatoes, tomato sauce, undrained beans, uncooked pasta, chili powder, garlic salt, and 1/4 cup water.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover; simmer 20 minutes, stirring often.
Top with cheese. Cover; heat 2 minutes or till cheese melts.

recipes.title: Stuffed Green Peppers
recipes.description: Bell peppers stuffed with seasoned ground beef and rice mixture.

instructions.text: Cut tops from peppers; remove seeds and membranes.
Precook peppers in boiling salted water for 5 minutes; drain.
For filling, in skillet cook meat and onion till meat is brown. Drain.
Add half the tomatoes, rice, Worcestershire, and salt.
Stuff peppers with meat mixture. Place in baking dish.
Pour remaining tomatoes around peppers.
Bake, uncovered, at 375°F for 35 to 40 minutes.
Top with cheese; bake 5 minutes more.

recipes.title: Deep-Dish Meat Pie
recipes.description: Hearty meat and vegetable pie with pastry crust.

instructions.text: In large saucepan combine meat, potatoes, and 1 cup broth.
Add thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover; simmer 45 minutes or till meat is tender.
Add peas; cook 5 minutes.
Combine flour and cold water; stir into meat mixture.
Cook and stir till thickened. Pour into 2-quart casserole.
Roll pastry to fit top of casserole. Place over filling; seal and flute.
Cut slits for steam. Bake at 425°F for 20 to 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Ham-Potato Scallop
recipes.description: Creamy scalloped potatoes layered with ham.

ingredients.item: cream of mushroom or celery soup

instructions.text: In 1 1/2-quart casserole layer half of the ham, half of the onion, and half of the potatoes. Repeat layers.
Mix soup and milk; pour over layers.
Cover; bake at 350°F for 1 hour.
Combine crumbs, parsley, and margarine.
Sprinkle atop casserole. Bake, uncovered, 15 minutes more.

recipes.title: Meaty Noodle Casserole
recipes.description: Easy casserole with ground beef, noodles, and sour cream sauce.

instructions.text: Cook noodles according to package directions; drain.
In skillet cook meat till brown; drain.
Stir in soup, milk, sour cream, pimiento, and parsley.
Fold in noodles. Transfer to 2-quart casserole.
Bake, covered, at 375°F for 35 to 40 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese; bake 5 minutes more.

recipes.title: Corned Beef Hash
recipes.description: Classic hash made with corned beef, potatoes, and onion.

instructions.text: Stir together corned beef, potato, onion, salt, pepper, and milk.
In large skillet melt margarine over medium heat.
Spread hash evenly in skillet.
Cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning occasionally.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Meaty Stuffed Potatoes
recipes.description: Baked potatoes stuffed with ham and cheese.

ingredients.item: diced cooked ham, beef, or pork
shredded American, Swiss, or Monterey Jack cheese

instructions.text: Scrub potatoes; prick with a fork. Bake in 425°F oven for 50 to 60 minutes or till tender.
Cut a lengthwise slice off tops of potatoes; scoop out insides.
Mash potato; mix in meat, sour cream, milk, onion, salt, and pepper.
Pile mixture back into potato shells.
Place in baking dish. Bake at 425°F for 20 to 25 minutes.
Top with cheese; bake 2 to 3 minutes more till cheese melts.

recipes.title: Creamed Dried Beef
recipes.description: Classic SOS (creamed chipped beef) served over toast.

instructions.text: If using dried beef, rinse and drain well. In a large skillet cook dried beef and, if desired, green pepper in margarine about 3 minutes or till edges curl.
Stir in flour and pepper. Add milk all at once.
Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly.
Cook and stir 1 minute more.
Serve over toast points.

recipes.title: Reuben Sandwiches
recipes.description: Classic grilled Reuben with corned beef, sauerkraut, and Swiss cheese.

ingredients.item: slices dark rye or pumpernickel bread

instructions.text: Spread one side of bread slices with dressing.
Top 4 slices with corned beef, cheese, and sauerkraut.
Cover with remaining bread, dressing side down.
Butter top and bottom of sandwiches.
Grill in skillet over medium heat till bread is golden and cheese melts, turning once.

recipes.title: Barbecue-Style Sandwiches
recipes.description: Sloppy Joe-style sandwiches with tangy barbecue sauce.

ingredients.item: thinly sliced cooked beef, pork, or lamb

instructions.text: In medium saucepan combine tomato sauce, onion, green pepper, brown sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire, mustard, celery seed, garlic, and chili powder.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover; simmer 15 minutes.
Stir some of the meat mixture onto bottom half of each roll.
Spoon some of the meat mixture onto bottom half of each roll. Top with other half of roll.

recipes.title: Meat-Stuffed Pita Pockets
recipes.description: Pita bread stuffed with seasoned ground beef and fresh vegetables.

ingredients.item: skinny worcester cream or salad dressing
cooked ground beef, pork, or lamb

instructions.text: Stir together sour cream and horseradish.
Combine meat, carrot, and celery with half the sour cream mixture.
Cut pita rounds in half; open pockets.
Line each half with lettuce.
Spoon in meat mixture. Drizzle with remaining sour cream mixture.

recipes.title: Chicken with Papaya
recipes.description: Stir-fried chicken with tropical papaya and ginger.

ingredients.prep_note: halved, seeded, peeled, and cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.item: macadamia nuts or toasted blanched whole almonds

instructions.text: For marinade, in a bowl stir together orange peel, orange juice, soy sauce, honey, and gingerroot.

Rinse chicken; pat dry. Cut into 1-inch pieces. Add chicken to marinade, stirring to coat. Cover and marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes or in the refrigerator for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Drain chicken, reserving marinade. Combine cornstarch and reserved marinade. Set aside.
Preheat a wok or large skillet over high heat; add cooking oil.
Stir-fry celery in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes or till crisp-tender. Remove from wok.
Add chicken to wok; stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes or till no longer pink. Push from center of wok.
Stir marinade mixture; add to center of wok. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly.
Return celery to wok; add papaya. Stir to coat well. Cook, covered, about 1 minute or till heated through.
Stir in nuts. Serve with hot cooked rice.

recipes.title: Beer Batter-Fried Chicken
recipes.description: Crispy deep-fried chicken coated in light beer batter.

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse chicken. In a large saucepan cover chicken with lightly salted water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Drain. Pat dry with paper towels.
For batter, in a bowl combine biscuit mix, onion salt, garlic powder, and ground red pepper. In another bowl stir together egg and beer; add to biscuit mixture. Beat till smooth.
Meanwhile, in a heavy 3-quart saucepan or deep-fat fryer heat 1 1/4 inches shortening or oil to 365°.

Dip chicken pieces, one at a time, into batter, gently shaking off excess batter. Carefully lower into the hot oil. Fry, two or three pieces at a time, for 2 to 3 minutes or till golden, turning once.
Drain well. Keep warm.

recipes.title: Cornmeal Batter-Fried Chicken
recipes.description: Deep-fried chicken with crispy cornmeal coating.

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse chicken. In a large saucepan cover chicken with lightly salted water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Drain. Pat dry with paper towels.

For batter, in a mixing bowl combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder, garlic salt, poultry seasoning, and red pepper. Stir together egg, milk, and the 2 tablespoons oil. Add to flour mixture; beat till smooth.
Meanwhile, in a heavy 3-quart saucepan or deep-fat fryer heat 1 1/4 inches shortening or oil to 365°.

Dip chicken pieces, one at a time, into batter, gently shaking off excess batter. Carefully lower into the hot oil. Fry, two or three pieces at a time, for 2 to 3 minutes or till golden, turning once. Carefully remove; drain well. Keep warm while frying remaining chicken.

notes: Variations: Herbed Batter-Fried Chicken - omit poultry seasoning, add 1 tsp dried thyme, savory, marjoram, Italian seasoning, or sage. Taco Batter-Fried Chicken - omit poultry seasoning, add 1 1/4 oz envelope taco seasoning mix, increase milk to 2/3 cup. Parmesan Batter-Fried Chicken - omit garlic salt and poultry seasoning, add 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 2 tbsp snipped parsley, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, increase milk to 2/3 cup.

recipes.title: Turkey-Rice Skillet
recipes.description: Quick one-skillet meal with ground turkey, rice, and cheese.

instructions.text: In large skillet cook 1 pound ground raw turkey till brown. Drain well.
Stir in one 14 1/2-ounce can stewed tomatoes, undrained, 1 cup water, 1/2 cup long grain rice, 2 teaspoons chili powder, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 20 minutes or till rice is tender.
Stir together 3/4 cup milk and 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour; add to skillet. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more.
Add 1/2 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese; stir till melted.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken and rice dish with chorizo, olives, and peas reminiscent of paella.

ingredients.item: bulk chorizo or bulk Italian sausage

instructions.text: Rinse chicken; pat dry. In a 4 1/2-quart Dutch oven cook chicken in hot oil, uncovered, over medium heat about 15 minutes, turning to brown evenly. Remove chicken and set aside. Discard drippings.
In the same pan cook sausage, onions, and garlic over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes or till sausage is no longer pink. Drain; return to pan.

Add water, rice, bouillon granules, oregano, and pepper. Bring to boiling, scraping up the browned bits. Place chicken pieces atop the sausage mixture. Reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes or till chicken is nearly tender, turning chicken once.
Add peas and green or red pepper to chicken mixture. Cook, covered, about 5 minutes more or till chicken is tender and no longer pink. Gently stir in tomatoes and olives.

recipes.title: Chicken Country Captain
recipes.description: Classic Southern curry-spiced chicken with tomatoes and raisins.

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse and pat dry. In a large skillet cook onion, green pepper, and garlic in margarine or butter till tender but not brown. Remove from heat.
Stir in undrained tomatoes, parsley, currants or raisins, curry powder, salt, mace, sugar, and pepper. Bring to boiling.

Add chicken pieces to the skillet, turning to coat. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 35 to 45 minutes or till tender and no longer pink, turning chicken once. Remove chicken from the skillet; keep warm.
For sauce, skim fat from tomato mixture. Stir together cornstarch and 1 tablespoon cold water; add to tomato mixture. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Serve gravy over chicken and dumplings. If desired, sprinkle with almonds.

recipes.title: Stewed Chicken
recipes.description: Basic stewed chicken that produces both cooked chicken and broth for other recipes.
recipes.servings_yield: About 5 1/2 cups broth and 2 1/2 cups chopped meat

ingredients.item: dried thyme, sage, or basil, crushed

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse. In a 4 1/2-quart Dutch oven combine chicken; celery; carrots; onion; parsley; salt; thyme, sage, or basil; pepper; and bay leaves. Add water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes.

Remove chicken. Strain broth through a large sieve lined with 2 layers of cheesecloth. Discard solids. If using broth while hot, skim off fat. (Or, if storing broth for later use, chill broth in a bowl for 6 hours. Lift off fat. Pour broth into airtight containers, discarding residue in the bottom of the bowl. Seal containers. Chill up to 2 days or freeze up to 3 months.)

When chicken is cool enough to handle, remove meat from bones; discard skin and bones. Chop meat and use immediately. (Or, if storing meat for later use, place in airtight containers; seal. Chill up to 3 days or freeze up to 3 months.)

recipes.title: Chicken and Dumplings
recipes.description: Classic comfort food with tender chicken and fluffy dumplings in gravy.

ingredients.item: poultry seasoning or dried sage or thyme, crushed

instructions.text: Skin chicken, if desired. Rinse. In a 4 1/2-quart Dutch oven combine chicken, onion, poultry seasoning, salt, and pepper. Add 3 cups water. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes. Add carrot and celery. Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes more.

Prepare Dumplings for Stew, omitting the herb. Drop from a tablespoon into six mounds directly onto chicken (do not drop batter into liquid). Cover; simmer about 12 minutes or till a toothpick inserted into dumplings comes out clean.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer chicken, dumplings, and vegetables to a platter; cover.

For gravy, skim fat from broth; discard fat. Measure 2 cups broth into the Dutch oven. Slowly stir 1/2 cup cold water into flour. Stir into broth. Cook and stir till bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Serve gravy over chicken and dumplings.

notes: Chicken and Noodles variation: Prepare as above, except pour 4 cups of the hot broth into the Dutch oven. (Freeze remaining broth for another use.) Bring to boiling. Add 6 ounces (2 1/2 cups) dried Homemade Pasta or 6 ounces (3 cups) packaged noodles, or one 8-ounce package frozen noodles. Stir in 1 cup thinly sliced carrots; 1/2 cup sliced celery; 1/2 cup chopped onion; 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, sage, or basil, crushed; and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Return to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes or till noodles and vegetables are tender.

recipes.title: Chicken Potpies
recipes.description: Individual chicken pies with flaky pastry topping.

ingredients.item: dried sage, marjoram, or thyme, crushed

instructions.text: Prepare pastry; set aside. Cook peas and carrots according to package directions; drain. In a saucepan cook onion and mushrooms in margarine or butter till tender. Stir in flour, salt, sage, marjoram, or thyme; and pepper.
Add chicken broth and milk all at once. Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Stir in drained peas and carrots, chicken or turkey, parsley, and pimiento; heat till bubbly.
Pour chicken mixture into six 10-ounce round casseroles.

Roll pastry into a 15x10-inch rectangle. Cut into six 5-inch circles and place atop the 10-ounce casseroles. (Or, roll pastry into a 13x9-inch rectangle. Place over the 12x7 1/2x2-inch baking dish.) Flute edges of pastry and cut slits in the top for steam to escape.
Bake in a 450°F oven for 12 to 15 minutes or till pastry is golden brown.

notes: Herb-Crumb-Topped Chicken Potpies: Prepare as above, except omit pastry. Stir together 1 cup herb-seasoned stuffing croutons and 2 tablespoons melted margarine or butter. Sprinkle atop chicken mixture in casseroles or dish. Bake in a 400°F oven about 15 minutes or till biscuits are golden.

Biscuit-Topped Chicken Potpies: Prepare as above, except omit pastry. Cut 6 refrigerated biscuits into quarters and arrange atop bubbly chicken mixture in casseroles or dish. Bake in a 400°F oven about 15 minutes or till biscuits are golden.

recipes.title: Chicken à la King
recipes.description: Classic creamy chicken dish served over toast points or patty shells.

ingredients.item: toast points or baked patty shells

instructions.text: In a saucepan melt margarine. If using fresh mushrooms, add mushrooms and cook, tender.
Stir in flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add milk and chicken broth all at once.
Cook and stir till thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir for 1 minute more.
Add canned mushrooms, if using. Stir in chicken or turkey, pimiento, and, if desired, dry sherry. Heat through.
Spoon atop toast points.

notes: Cheesy Chicken à la King: Prepare as above, except add 1 cup shredded American or process Swiss cheese to the thickened mixture before adding the chicken or turkey. Stir till cheese melts.

Curried Chicken à la King: Prepare as above, except add 1 teaspoon curry powder to melted margarine or butter; cook for 1 minute. Omit dry sherry. If desired, add 1 tablespoon chutney with chicken or turkey.

Herbed Chicken à la King: Prepare as above, except cook 2 tablespoons finely chopped green pepper or sliced green onion; 1 clove garlic, minced; and 1/2 teaspoon dried basil, crushed, in melted margarine or butter till tender.

recipes.title: To Skin or Not to Skin (Chicken)
recipes.description: Guide for when to leave chicken skin on or remove it during cooking.
recipes.content: Our recipes deal with chicken skin in three ways. In some recipes, we call for the skin to be left on, either because it is too difficult to remove or because it is necessary to keep the chicken from overcooking. In other recipes, we give you a choice. Remove the skin if you wish to save calories and cut down on fat. Finally, in still other recipes, we tell you to remove the skin. In these dishes, the skin develops an unpleasant texture if it is left on. Keep these guidelines in mind when you're trying to decide whether to skin chicken for your own recipes. One last tip: If you're micro-cooking skinned chicken, be sure to cover the baking dish with vented clear plastic wrap to keep the chicken moist.

recipes.title: Carving a Roasted Bird
recipes.description: Step-by-step instructions for carving whole roasted poultry.
recipes.content: To carve poultry with confidence, use a sharp knife and these directions. When the bird is done, remove it from the oven and cover it with foil. Let it stand for 15 to 20 minutes before beginning to carve. Standing lets the bird's flesh firm up, meaning the carved slices will hold together better. Place the bird on a cutting board. Remove the stuffing. Grasp the tip of one drumstick and pull it away from the body. Cut through the skin and meat between the thigh and the body. Repeat on the other side. With the tip of the knife, separate the thighbone from the backbone by cutting through the joint. Repeat on other side. To separate the thighs and drumsticks, cut through the joints where the drumstick bones and thighbones meet. To carve the meat from the drumsticks, hold each drumstick vertically by the tip with the large end resting on the cutting board. Slice the meat parallel to the bone and under some tendons, turning the leg to get even slices. Slice thigh meat the same way. To carve the breast meat, make a deep horizontal cut into the breast above each wing. This cut marks one end of each breast meat slice. Beginning at the outer edge of one side of each breast, cut slices from the top of the breast down to the horizontal cut. Cut the final smaller slices following the curve of the breastbone. Remove wings by cutting through the joints where the wing bones and backbone meet.

recipes.title: Brown-Bag Pointers
recipes.description: Tips for packing lunches safely.
recipes.content: Here are three-bag tips to keep your lunch fresh: Most bag lunches are easy to keep at room temperature. Pack cold foods in an insulated lunch box with ice packs. Seal cold foods in clean airtight containers. For sandwiches, pack meats separate from bread. Fill hot thermoses only with foods at temperatures of 165°F or higher. Pack foods that can stay at room temperature safely in paper bags. Keep your lunch in a cool, dry place.

recipes.title: Food Safety and Storage
recipes.description: Comprehensive guide to keeping food safe and storing it properly.
recipes.content: Keeping food safe to eat is as simple as keeping hot foods hot, cold foods cold, and all foods clean. Keeping Foods Hot: To prevent the buildup of illness-causing bacteria, cook foods thoroughly, especially meat, poultry, and dishes containing eggs. Since bacteria grow at room temperature, discard any cooked or chilled food that has been left out longer than two hours. Cover leftovers while reheating to retain moisture. Be sure, too, to heat the food completely. Keeping Foods Cold: Keep your refrigerator at about 40°F and your freezer at 0°F or less. Check them both periodically with an appliance thermometer. Thaw meat and poultry in the refrigerator overnight. For faster thawing, place frozen packages in a watertight plastic bag under cold water. Change the water often. Do not thaw meat on the kitchen counter. Store leftovers in the refrigerator as soon as possible. Do not let food cool on the counter. When shopping, pick up perishables last. Be sure frozen foods are solid and refrigerated foods are cold. If you live more than 30 minutes from the store, you may want to stow frozen, refrigerated, and perishable foods in an ice chest for the trip home. Keeping Foods Clean: Since bacteria live all around us, always wash and dry your hands with clean cloths before you begin to cook. When working with raw meat and poultry, wash hands, counters, and utensils in hot soapy water between each recipe step. Bacteria on raw meat and poultry can contaminate other foods. Never put cooked meat or poultry on the same plate that held the raw food.

recipes.title: Measuring Techniques
recipes.description: Guide to properly measuring ingredients for consistent results.
recipes.content: Correctly measuring ingredients is important for consistent results. 1. Measuring Liquids: Use a glass or clear plastic measuring cup. Place the cup on a level surface and bend down so your eye is level with the marking you wish to read. Fill the cup to the marking. Don't lift the cup off the counter to your eye; your hand is not as steady as the countertop. When using measuring spoons to measure a liquid, pour the liquid just to the top of the spoon without letting it spill over. Don't measure over the mixing bowl because the liquid could overflow from the spoon into the bowl. 2. Measuring Flour: Stir the flour in the canister to lighten it. (Sifting flours, except cake flour, no longer is necessary.) Then gently spoon the flour into a dry measuring cup and level off the top with the straight edge of a knife or a metal spatula. 3. Measuring Sugar: Press brown sugar firmly into a dry measuring cup so that it holds the shape of the cup when turned out. To measure granulated sugar, spoon the sugar into a dry measuring cup, then level it off with the straight edge of a knife or a metal spatula. 4. Measuring Solid Shortening: Using a rubber spatula, press the shortening firmly into a dry measuring cup. Level it off with the straight edge of a knife or a metal spatula. 5. Measuring Margarine or Butter: For stick margarine or butter, use an entire 1/4-pound stick for 1/2 cup, half of a stick for 1/4 cup, or an eighth of a stick for 1 tablespoon. With a sharp knife, cut off the amount needed, following the guidelines on the wrapper. For unwrapped margarine or butter, soften it, then measure as directed for solid shortening. 6. Measuring Dried Herbs: Lightly fill a measuring spoon just to the top with the dried herb (leveling with a spatula is not necessary). Then empty the spoon into your hand. Crush the herb with the fingers of your other hand. This breaks the leaves and releases their flavor. (Some of the harder dried herbs, such as rosemary and thyme, are best crushed with a mortar and pestle.)

recipes.title: Garnishing Techniques
recipes.description: Easy garnishing ideas to make everyday meals special.
recipes.content: Make even the most everyday meal seem special with these easy-to-do garnishes. 1. Radish Accordions: Make 8 to 10 narrow crosswise cuts 1/4 inch apart in long narrow radishes, cutting only partially through each radish. (To keep from cutting through the radishes, place them between two parallel wooden sticks when cutting.) Place the radishes in ice water so the slices fan out. Use with meats or salads. 2. Citrus Twists: Thinly slice lemons, limes, and oranges. Cut into center of each slice; twist ends in opposite directions. Use with fish and citrus or cream pies. 3. Fluted Mushrooms: With a paring knife held at an angle, and beginning at the top of each mushroom cap, make cuts in the form of an inverted V. Turn mushroom slightly; cut another inverted V; repeat around cap. For a similar effect, make a series of slight indentations in mushroom cap with a punch-type can opener. Use with salads and meats. 4. Tomato Roses: Cut a base from the stem end of each tomato (do not sever). Cut a continuous narrow strip in spiral fashion, tapering end to remove. Curl strip onto its base in a rose shape. Use with salads and dips. 5. Scored Cucumbers: Make a V-shape cut lengthwise down each cucumber (or run the tines of a fork lengthwise down each cucumber, pressing to break the skin). Repeat at regular intervals around cucumber. Slice or bias-slice. Use with salads and dips. 6. Onion Brushes: Slice roots from ends of green onions; remove most of green portion. Make slashes at both ends of the onion pieces to make fringes. Place in ice water to curl the ends. Use with steaks or roasts. 7. Carrot Curls/Zigzags: Using a vegetable peeler, cut thin lengthwise strips from carrots. For curls, roll up; secure with toothpicks. For zigzags, thread on toothpicks accordion-style. Put curls and zigzags in ice water; remove toothpicks before using. Use with salads, sauces, and thickened soups. 8. Chocolate Curls/Grated Chocolate: For curls, use a bar of chocolate at room temperature. Carefully draw a vegetable peeler across the chocolate, making thin strips that curl. To grate, rub a cool, firm square of chocolate across a hand grater. Use to garnish cakes, tortes, custards, or ice-cream drinks.

recipes.title: Dandelion Wine
recipes.description: Traditional homemade wine from dandelion flowers.

instructions.text: Pick fresh flowers and trim stalks, removing all green parts.
Place flowers in large bowl. Set aside one pint of water.
Boil remaining gallon and pour over flowers. Cover tightly with plastic wrap for two days, stirring twice daily.
Transfer to large pot and bring to low boil.
Add sugar and citrus peelings (thinly sliced, avoiding white pith). Boil for one hour.
Pour into fermenter and cool. Add yeast, nutrient, cover, and place in warm location for three days.
Strain into secondary fermenter with raisins and fit fermentation lock.
Rack after wine clears. After two months, rack and bottle.
Age six months to one year.

recipes.title: Dandelion Burgers
recipes.description: Vegetarian burgers made with dandelion petals.

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients until combined into goopy batter.
Form into patties.
Pan-fry in oil or butter, turning until both sides are crisp.

recipes.title: Dandelion Blossom Bread
recipes.description: Quick bread made with dandelion blossoms.

instructions.text: Combine dry ingredients including separated dandelion petals.
In separate bowl, mix milk, honey, oil, and beaten egg.
Add liquid to dry ingredients.
Pour into buttered bread or muffin tin.
Bake at 400°F for 20-25 minutes for muffins or longer for bread loaf.

recipes.title: Cream of Dandelion Soup
recipes.description: Creamy soup made with dandelion leaves, petals, and buds.

instructions.text: Gently boil dandelion leaves in 6 cups water. Pour off bitter water.
Boil gently a second time and drain.
In heavy-bottom soup pot, sauté leeks and garlic in butter until tender.
Add 4 cups water, dandelion leaves, flower petals, buds, and salt.
Simmer 45 minutes.
Add cream and simmer several minutes more. Garnish with flower petals.

recipes.title: Dandelion Blossom Syrup
recipes.description: Honey-like syrup made from dandelion blossoms.

instructions.text: Place blossoms and water in pot.
Bring just to boil, turn off heat, cover, and let sit overnight.
The next day, strain and press liquid from spent flowers.
Add sugar and citrus, then heat slowly, stirring occasionally.
Continue for several hours until reduced to thick, honey-like consistency.
Can in half-pint or pint jars.

recipes.title: Dandelion Baklava
recipes.description: Traditional baklava made with dandelion blossom syrup.

instructions.text: Combine nuts with sugar and spices.
Melt butter.
Layer 8 fillo sheets in buttered 9x13 pan, brushing every other sheet with butter.
Sprinkle half the nut mixture.
Layer 8 more sheets and remaining nut mixture.
Top with remaining fillo sheets, brushing top generously with butter.
Cut into 30 squares before baking.
Bake at 375°F for 30 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour room temperature syrup over hot baklava.

recipes.title: Dandelion and Burdock Beer
recipes.description: Traditional British herbal beer made with dandelion and burdock.

instructions.text: Put nettles, dandelion leaves, burdock, ginger, and thinly pared lemon rinds in large pan with water.
Bring to boil and simmer 30 minutes.
Pour lemon juice, sugar, and cream of tartar into large container and strain liquid through, pressing down on solids.
Stir to dissolve sugar. Cool to room temperature.
Sprinkle in yeast. Cover and leave to ferment in warm place for 3 days.
Pour off beer and bottle, adding 1 tsp sugar per pint.
Leave undisturbed about 1 week until clear.

recipes.title: Scalloped Cattails
recipes.description: Baked cattail tops in a creamy casserole.

instructions.text: Combine cattail tops with eggs, butter, sugar, nutmeg, and pepper in a bowl.
Gradually blend in the scalded milk.
Pour mixture into a greased casserole dish.
Top with cheese and butter.
Bake at 275°F for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Cattail Pollen Biscuits
recipes.description: Biscuits made with cattail pollen flour.

instructions.text: Mix pollen, flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in shortening.
Add milk and mix.
Form biscuits.
Bake at 425°F for 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Cattail Pollen Pancakes
recipes.description: Pancakes made with cattail pollen for a golden color.

instructions.text: Combine dry ingredients.
Mix with egg, milk, and bacon drippings.
Pour dollar-sized amounts onto a hot griddle.
Cook until bubbles form, then flip.

recipes.title: Kudzu Blossom Jelly
recipes.description: Purple jelly made from kudzu blossoms.

instructions.text: Wash blossoms and place in a large bowl.
Pour boiling water over blossoms; refrigerate 8 hours or overnight.
Strain blossoms and liquid through colander into Dutch oven.
Add lemon juice and pectin; bring to rolling boil over high heat, stirring constantly.
Stir in sugar; return to rolling boil and boil 1 minute while stirring.
Remove from heat; skim foam with spoon.
Pour into sterilized jars, filling to 1/4 inch from top.
Process in boiling water bath for 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Rolled Kudzu Leaves
recipes.description: Stuffed kudzu leaves similar to dolmas.

instructions.text: Gather leaves from unsprayed areas and wash them.
Boil leaves in salted water for 2-3 minutes, separating as needed.
Remove to plate to cool. Remove heavy center stems.
Combine rice, meat, 1 cup diced tomatoes, allspice, salt and pepper for stuffing.
Fill each leaf with 1 teaspoon stuffing and roll cigar-shaped.
Arrange rolls alternately in opposite directions in large pan.
Pour in remaining diced tomatoes, salt, and garlic.
Press down with inverted dish; add water to reach dish.
Cover and cook on medium for 30 minutes.
Add lemon juice and cook 10 minutes more.

recipes.title: Kudzu Quiche
recipes.description: Savory quiche made with young kudzu leaves.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix cream, eggs, kudzu, salt, pepper, and cheese.
Place mixture in pie shell.
Bake 35 to 45 minutes until center is set.

recipes.title: Beautyberry Jelly
recipes.description: Purple jelly made from American beautyberries.

instructions.text: Wash and clean beautyberries, removing all green stems and leaves.
Cover berries with 2 quarts water.
Boil for 20 minutes.
Strain to create infusion.
Use 3 cups of the infusion and bring to boil.
Add Sure-Jell and sugar.
Return to second boil and boil for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand until foam forms.
Skim off foam.
Pour into sterilized jars and cap.

recipes.title: Loquat Grappa
recipes.description: Italian-style liqueur made from loquat seeds.

instructions.text: Soak seeds in vodka for 1-6 months in a sealed jar.
Drain flavored vodka and divide between two bottles.
Heat equal parts sugar and water until dissolved.
Top off each bottle with sugar syrup.
Adjust sweetness as desired.

notes: Seeds contain cyanogenetic glycosides; consume sparingly, no more than 4 ounces at a time.

recipes.title: Loquat Wine
recipes.description: Fruit wine made from fresh loquats.

instructions.text: Chop fruit finely, pour over half sugar, Campden tablet, tannin, and water.
After 12 hours, add pectic enzyme.
After another 12 hours, add yeast.
Stir daily, adding remaining sugar after 3 days.
Ferment on pulp 4 more days.
Strain through jelly bag, pour into secondary with airlock.
Rack every 30 days until clear (3-4 additional rackings).
Bottle and age.

recipes.title: Loquat Jelly
recipes.description: Clear jelly made from loquat fruit.

instructions.text: Wash loquats, remove seeds and blossom ends.
Barely cover with cold water. Simmer covered 15 minutes until soft.
Strain through jelly bag.
Measure 3 1/2 cups juice and lemon juice.
Add pectin, stir well. Bring to boil, stirring constantly.
Add sugar, return to rolling boil for exactly 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, skim.
Pour into sterilized glasses, seal with paraffin.

recipes.title: Loquat Pie
recipes.description: Traditional fruit pie made with loquats.

instructions.text: Stem, wash, and cut loquats, leaving a few seeds for flavor.
Cook in water covered 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Combine sugar, flour, salt, ginger, and allspice.
Stir into loquats. Cook stirring until thickened, cool.
Pour into bottom crust, cover with top crust, prick or slash.
Bake at 450°F for 10 minutes, reduce to 350°F for 45 minutes.
Serve with vanilla ice cream and rum sauce.

recipes.title: Spiced Loquats
recipes.description: Pickled loquats with warm spices.

instructions.text: Wash loquats, remove stem and blossom ends.
Combine sugar, water, and vinegar.
Tie spices in cheesecloth, add to mixture. Boil 10 minutes.
Add fruit, cook gently until tender.
Remove fruit, pour syrup into sterilized jars, fill with hot syrup.
Seal immediately.

recipes.title: Mulberry Pie
recipes.description: Fruit pie made with fresh mulberries.

instructions.text: Combine sugar with mulberries in a saucepan.
Mix cornstarch with water separately.
Add cornstarch mixture and juice to berries.
Cook over medium heat until mixture thickens and juice becomes clear.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Cool and serve.

recipes.title: Mulberry Vinegar
recipes.description: Fruit vinegar made from mulberries.

instructions.text: Place mulberries in large bowl.
Mash berries and pour hot vinegar over them.
Cover with towel; stir with wooden spoon daily for 3 days.
Strain juice through jelly bag.
Add 1 cup sugar per cup juice.
Boil together for 5 minutes.
Pour into sterilized jars and seal.
To serve: Mix 2 tablespoons vinegar in 8-ounce glass with water and ice.

recipes.title: Mulberry Sauce
recipes.description: Spiced fruit sauce from mulberries.

instructions.text: Add sugar and spices to mashed berries.
Bring to boil.
Simmer until thick, stirring frequently.
Bottle and seal.

recipes.title: Chickweed Bread
recipes.description: Yeast bread made with sautéed chickweed.

instructions.text: Sauté onion and chickweed until tender (avoid browning).
Dissolve honey and yeast in warm water, then add salt.
Mix yeast mixture with cooled sautéed chickweed and onions.
Gradually incorporate flour until dough no longer adheres to fingers.
Form into a ball and allow to rise to double volume.
Shape into loaves and let rise again.
Bake at 375°F for 40-45 minutes.

recipes.title: Chickweed and Bacon Pie
recipes.description: Savory pie with chickweed, bacon, and sour cream.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Line 10-inch pie dish with crust, creating raised border to prevent overflow.
Remove chickweed leaves and twigs, keeping only greenest parts; rinse and dry.
Chop chickweed into confetti texture and measure.
Fry bacon until browning begins, add onion, cook 3 minutes until wilted.
Transfer bacon and onions to bowl with chickweed using slotted spoon.
Beat eggs until lemon-colored, mix with sour cream, flour, and nutmeg.
Combine egg mixture with chickweed, bacon, and onions.
Spread filling evenly in pie shell, press down firmly with spoon.
Bake 45-50 minutes until center sets and top turns golden.

recipes.title: Elderberry Schnapps
recipes.description: Elderberry-infused vodka liqueur.

ingredients.prep_note: half the weight of berries, or more to cover

instructions.text: Rinse and clean elderberries, removing all stems.
Weigh the prepared berries.
Place berries in a clean glass jar with tight-fitting lid.
Add vodka equal to half the berry weight (or more to fully cover).
Seal jar and store in a dark place at room temperature.
Shake occasionally.
After 1-4 weeks, strain and discard berries.
Transfer liquid to a new clean jar with tight lid.
Age for at least two months before consuming.

recipes.title: Elderberry Wine
recipes.description: Traditional homemade elderberry wine.

instructions.text: Wash elderberries and remove stems, discarding unsuitable ones.
Boil water and dissolve sugar into it.
Place berries in a nylon straining bag and tie it.
Put bag in primary fermentation container.
Mash berries while wearing sterilized gloves.
Pour hot sugar water over berries and cover.
When cooled to lukewarm, add acid blend, crushed Campden tablet, and yeast nutrient.
Cover and wait 12 hours.
Stir in pectin enzyme, cover and wait another 12 hours.
Add yeast and stir daily for 14 days.
Gently squeeze bag while wearing sterile gloves after each stirring.
Drip drain berries without squeezing; add juice to primary container.
Rack wine into secondary container with airlock.
Store in dark place and ferment for two months.
Rack again, top up, and refit airlock.
Repeat racking process two more times.
Stabilize wine and wait 10 days.
Rack final time, sweeten to taste, and bottle.
Store in dark place for one year before consuming.

recipes.title: Spicy Henbit
recipes.description: Curried henbit greens in sour cream sauce.

instructions.text: Chop four cups of shoots and cover with water, then boil for 10 minutes.
In a separate pan, melt butter and add curry powder, whole cloves, and cinnamon; stir and cook for one minute.
Stir in flour and cook for another minute.
Add half a cup of the boiling water from the henbit, stirring until smooth.
Drain the boiled henbit and add it to the pan along with sour cream.
Cook on low heat for 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Maypop Jelly
recipes.description: Jelly made from wild passion fruit (maypops).

instructions.text: Combine maypops and water, then boil gently for five minutes.
Strain the mixture, discarding the pulp.
Combine the liquid with sugar and bring to a full rolling boil.
Add pectin and return to rolling boil.
Remove from heat and pour into hot, sterilized jars.
Seal the jars.

recipes.title: Day Lily Jelly
recipes.description: Floral jelly made from daylily petals.

instructions.text: Bring petals and water to a boil, then remove from heat.
Cover and let steep for 10-15 minutes.
Pour mixture through jelly bag or doubled cheesecloth into strainer.
Allow liquid to drip into bowl overnight—do not squeeze.
Measure 5 cups of juice into pot.
Add sugar, lemon juice, and pectin.
Follow standard jelly-making procedures to set.

recipes.title: Pindo Palm Wine
recipes.description: Fruit wine made from pindo palm (jelly palm) fruit.

instructions.text: Cover fruit with water and use clean hands to rub out seeds.
Mash the fibrous fruit pulp.
Add crushed Campden tablet; let sit covered for 24 hours.
Prepare wine starter.
Add pectinase dissolved in water; let sit several hours.
Add sugar syrup, tannic acid, and yeast nutrient; make up to 5 liters total.
Add yeast and stir three times daily for 6 days.
Sieve into demijohn.
Rack and add sugar as needed for final gravity around 1.020.

recipes.title: Pindo Palm Jelly
recipes.description: Jelly made from pindo palm (jelly palm) fruit.

instructions.text: Cut and scrape fruit from seeds (aim for 3 cups cleaned fruit from 6 cups starting amount).
Cover fruit with 3 cups water.
Bring to boil and cook until approximately 3.5 cups infused juice remains.
Filter juice (optional for clarity).
Follow Sure Jell box recipe for three cups fruit juice.
Adjust sugar to taste and can jars.

recipes.title: Garlic Mustard Vichyssoise
recipes.description: Chilled potato soup with garlic mustard and goat cheese.

instructions.text: In a heavy bottomed pan add water and potatoes with salt and boil until potatoes soften. Set aside.
Melt butter in a medium saucepan. Add onion and cook until softened. Pour over boiled potatoes and water.
Blend in food processor until smooth. Add water as needed for consistency. Pass through a sieve.
Chill in refrigerator. Check seasoning.
Blanch garlic mustard for 10 seconds in salted boiling water and refresh in ice water.
Add garlic mustard and blend until smooth.
Add three cornered garlic and blend until smooth. Check seasoning.
Serve with crumbled goat's cheese, frothed milk, pinch of cumin, and white pepper.

recipes.title: Greek Cardune (Burdock Flower Stalks)
recipes.description: Mediterranean-style braised burdock flower stalks with rice.

instructions.text: Parboil flower stalks 1 minute in salted water to remove bitterness.
Combine all ingredients in covered saucepan.
Simmer over low heat 70 minutes until rice is tender.

recipes.title: Quick & Easy Hard Cider
recipes.description: Simple hard cider made in 5-7 days with natural fermentation.

instructions.text: Pour off 1/2 cup juice from cider gallon.
Add 1/2 cup starter culture to the jug.
Install fermentation lock (balloon, condom, or commercial airlock with pinhole).
Keep in warm location (65-75°F ideal).
Ferment 5 days for sweeter result; 7-14 days for drier.
Bottle in plastic seltzer bottles or capped containers.
Keep warm 1-2 days to carbonate (bottles become firm).
Refrigerate to stop fermentation and slow carbonation buildup.

notes: Avoid juice containing nitrates, sulfides, or potassium sorbate, which kills yeast

recipes.title: Wild Yeast Starter Culture
recipes.description: Reusable wild yeast starter for making cider and other fermented drinks.

instructions.text: Peel organic apple; place peeling in cider.
Cover loosely; keep in warm, dark place.
After 2-3 weeks, visible bubbles indicate active yeast.
Use 1/2 cup of this culture per batch of cider.
To maintain: After bottling each batch, save dregs (sediment + yeast + juice). Add 2 tbsp sugar and store in warm place (refresh every few days) or refrigerate long-term.

notes: Reusable for 2+ years before genetic drift requires starting fresh

recipes.title: Concord Grape Quick Ferment
recipes.description: Quick fermented grape beverage resembling semi-bubbly red Lambrusco.

instructions.text: Follow cider method but ferment only 3 days maximum.
Shorter fermentation preserves sweetness; longer fermentation produces harsh flavor.
Cap and carbonate for 1 day, then chill and serve.

notes: Results resemble semi-bubbly red Lambrusco when chilled

recipes.title: Elderberry Wine (1 Gallon)
recipes.description: Traditional homemade elderberry wine with detailed fermentation instructions.

instructions.text: Wash berries and remove stems, discarding unsuitable ones.
Boil water and dissolve sugar into it.
Place berries in a nylon straining bag and mash while wearing sterilized gloves.
Pour hot sugar water over berries and cover. Cool to lukewarm.
Add acid blend, crushed Campden tablet, and yeast nutrient. Cover and wait 12 hours.
Stir in pectin enzyme, cover again, and wait another 12 hours before adding yeast.
Stir daily for 14 days, gently squeezing the bag with sterile gloves.
Drain without squeezing and transfer juice to a secondary container with airlock.
Ferment in darkness for two months.
Rack again, top up, and refit airlock. Repeat racking two more times.
Stabilize after 10 days, rack once more, sweeten to taste, and bottle.
Store in darkness for one year.

notes: Freezing berry clusters makes them separate from branches more easily

recipes.title: Walnut Liquor (Nocino)
recipes.description: Traditional walnut liqueur made from green walnuts.

ingredients.prep_note: yellow part only, no white pith

instructions.text: Soak the walnuts overnight to draw out any worms and impurities.
Quarter them and place in a large jar with all other ingredients.
Place in a sunny spot, sealed, for at least 40 days (2 months is better).
Shake every few days.
Strain and bottle the liquid; let sit for another month or two minimum.
Best after aging 2-3 years.

notes: Optional: Combine filter solids with 2 cups alcohol, 1 cup sugar, and a bottle of cheap sparkling wine for a secondary liqueur

recipes.title: Hickory Nut Coffee
recipes.description: Coffee-like beverage made from roasted hickory nuts.

instructions.text: Roast nuts for 15 minutes at 350°F.
Cool completely. Do not cook longer or at higher temperature without first scoring them so heat can escape.
Split shells, add to water, bring to boil.
Strain when water turns golden and serve.

recipes.title: Hickory Nut Cake
recipes.description: Classic three-layer cake with hickory nuts.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cream butter and sugar together.
Alternate adding flour mixture and milk.
Add vanilla.
Fold in nuts and stiffly beaten egg whites.
Divide among three greased pans.
Bake 20 minutes until done.

recipes.title: Hickory Nut Filling
recipes.description: Creamy filling for cakes made with hickory nuts.

instructions.text: Cook sugar, cream, and syrup to 238°F (soft ball stage).
Remove from heat and cool.
Beat until creamy.
Stir in butter and nuts.

recipes.title: Hickory Nut Pie
recipes.description: Southern-style pie similar to pecan pie but with hickory nuts.

instructions.text: Preheat to 350°F.
Beat eggs, add syrup and butter.
Stir in sugar, maple syrup, and nuts.
Pour into pastry shell.
Bake 45-55 minutes until set.
Serve with whipped cream.

recipes.title: Hickory Nut Refrigerator Cookies
recipes.description: Slice-and-bake cookies with hickory nuts.

instructions.text: Cream butter, add egg and beat until fluffy.
Beat in sugar and vanilla.
Stir in flour, baking soda, salt, and nuts.
Shape into two logs, wrap and refrigerate 1-2 hours.
Slice thin, bake at 350°F for 10-15 minutes until golden.

recipes.title: Maple Hickory Apple Crisp
recipes.description: Apple crisp topped with hickory nuts and maple syrup.

instructions.text: Preheat to 375°F.
Toss apples with lemon juice, 1 tsp cinnamon, and 3 tbsp flour.
Layer in greased pan with liquid.
Mix oats, flour, sugar, remaining cinnamon, nuts, and butter until crumbly.
Spread over apples, drizzle with maple syrup.
Bake 45 minutes.

recipes.title: Hickory Wild Rice Stuffing
recipes.description: Savory stuffing with wild rice, sausage, and hickory nuts.

instructions.text: Cook rice per package directions until tender.
Cook sausage if using, add to rice.
Sauté celery and onion in drippings or butter.
Combine with rice, add salt, pepper, and nuts.
Use for poultry stuffing or bake in casserole at 325°F for 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Hungarian Cream of Chestnut Soup (Gesztenye Leves)
recipes.description: Rich Hungarian soup with chestnuts, ham, and cream.

ingredients.prep_note: peeled, cored, quartered and thinly sliced

instructions.text: Prepare chestnuts: Score fresh chestnuts with an X on the bottom. Boil in water 30 minutes, cool slightly, and peel. Chop finely once completely cooled.
Melt butter in a large saucepan. Add parsnips, carrots, apples, and leeks. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until nearly tender.
Mix in ham, chestnuts, and paprika. Cook one minute.
Add stock and bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer uncovered 20 minutes.
Whisk cream and egg yolks together. Temper by slowly adding hot soup broth while whisking.
Pour mixture back into soup, whisking constantly for one minute until thickened.
Season to taste. Serve with sour cream if desired.

recipes.title: Swamp Cabbage Slaw (Heart of Palm)
recipes.attribution: Eat the Weeds - Green Deane (from Marian Van Atta's Wild Edibles)
recipes.description: Simple slaw made from fresh heart of palm.

instructions.text: Optionally soak shredded palm hearts in ice water for an hour.
Mix with mayonnaise and pickle relish.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.

recipes.title: Roasted Palm Seed Beverage
recipes.description: Coffee-like drink made from roasted palm kernels.

instructions.text: Roast pulpless kernels at 350°F for 20-30 minutes.
Grind using an industrial coffee grinder and grain grinder.
Brew like coffee for a passable coffee-like drink, especially aromatic.

recipes.title: Grilled Cactus Pads (Nopales)
recipes.description: Simple grilled prickly pear cactus pads.

instructions.text: Scrub pads thoroughly and remove all spines.
Cut around spiny nodules completely.
Brush with oil while grilling.
Grill over charcoal 10-12 minutes per side (thicker pads need longer).
Serve hot.

notes: Select the best pads when shiny and not too thick
Remove glochids by spraying with water, burning off, or using duct tape

recipes.title: Prickly Pear Cactus Jelly
recipes.description: Beautiful pink-red jelly from prickly pear cactus fruit.

instructions.text: Place fruit in large saucepan, cover with boiling water, let stand 2-3 minutes, drain.
Peel fruit, cut into pieces, cover with water and boil 5 minutes.
Pour through cheesecloth, drain thoroughly, discard seeds.
Combine juice, sugar, and lemon juice in large saucepan.
Bring to rolling boil, reduce heat to medium-high.
Add pectin, cook 8-12 minutes until thickened.
Skim foam, pour into sterilized jars.
Process in boiling water bath 5 minutes.

notes: Ripe fruit flesh tastes similar to raspberries
Eating ripe fruit can turn urine reddish (normal)

recipes.title: Cactus Monterey
recipes.description: Savory cactus dish with tomatoes, peppers, and cheese.

instructions.text: Steam cactus until softened, drain.
Lightly fry remaining ingredients (except cheese).
Combine fried ingredients with cactus.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Top with cheese before serving.

recipes.title: Cactus Flower Wine
recipes.description: Delicate wine made from prickly pear cactus flowers.

instructions.text: Wash flowers, place in nylon straining bag with dozen marbles for weight.
Heat 1 quart water, dissolve sugar.
Cool with frozen grape concentrate and remaining water, add to primary fermenter.
Add remaining ingredients except yeast, stir well.
Cover and wait 10-12 hours before adding activated yeast.
Stir daily until specific gravity drops to 1.020.
Drip-drain bag, transfer to secondary with airlock.
Rack after 45 days, then again after another 45 days.
Final rack 60 days after clearing, age 90-120 days.
Stabilize, sweeten to taste, bottle.
Taste after 6 months in bottle.

recipes.title: Roasted Ginkgo Nuts
recipes.description: Traditional roasted ginkgo nuts for snacking or adding to dishes.

instructions.text: Roast cleaned seeds at 350°F for one hour.
Crush seeds between towels while tapping gently with a hammer.
Shell and serve.

notes: Ginkgo nuts can be used in soups, stuffings, desserts, meat dishes, poultry dishes and vegetarian dishes

recipes.title: Boiled Ginkgo Nuts
recipes.description: Simple boiled ginkgo nuts as a snack.

instructions.text: Crack seeds raw using a nutcracker.
Boil seeds in salty water until tender.
Rub with a ladle to remove the brown membrane.
Salt and serve.

recipes.title: Sautéed Banana Tree Stem
recipes.description: Indian-style sautéed banana stem with coconut and spices.

instructions.text: Peel outer fibers from stem and chop finely.
Heat half the oil, add mustard seeds until crackling.
Add stem pieces, curry, salt, and chili powder.
Cover and simmer until soft (approximately one hour).
Grind coconut and garlic together.
When stem is almost cooked, add coconut-garlic mixture and continue cooking covered.
Finish with remaining coconut oil and let rest before serving.

recipes.title: Banana Flower Stir Fry
recipes.description: Indian-style banana flower stir fry with lentils.

instructions.text: Cook lentils separately.
Remove outer petals from flower; chop inner cream portion finely.
Apply coconut oil to palms and rub chopped flower to remove lumps.
Heat oil and splutter mustard seeds. Add chillies, onion, curry leaves; sauté until onions brown.
Add flower, garlic, spices, and salt. Cook covered 5 minutes without water.
Stir in lentils and cook 5 more minutes until dry.

notes: Optional: soak chopped flower in milk to reduce bitterness

recipes.title: Juneberry Pie
recipes.description: Classic pie made with foraged juneberries (serviceberries).

instructions.text: Combine all filling ingredients together.
Pour into pastry-lined pie plate.
Top with pastry strips and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 450°F for 15 minutes then at 350°F for 25 minutes more.

recipes.title: Juneberry Jam
recipes.description: Simple jam made with juneberries and rhubarb.

instructions.text: Grind berries and combine with sugar and rhubarb.
Bring to simmer.
Stir and cook until thick. Burns easily - watch carefully.
Pour into jars and seal.

recipes.title: Juneberry Muffins
recipes.description: Muffins studded with fresh juneberries.

instructions.text: Combine dry ingredients with egg, shortening, salt, and milk. Blend well.
Stir in berries.
Fill muffin cups two-thirds full.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°F.

recipes.title: Amaranth Tabouli
recipes.description: Middle Eastern-style grain salad made with amaranth instead of bulgur.

instructions.text: Simmer amaranth in equal volume of water for 12-15 minutes and cool completely.
Combine all ingredients except lettuce and olives in a bowl, tossing gently.
Refrigerate at least one hour to blend flavors.
Line a serving bowl with washed, dried lettuce leaves.
Add the amaranth mixture and garnish with olives.

notes: Soak amaranth overnight in water to reduce saponin content before cooking

recipes.title: Hawthorn Jelly (No-Cook Method)
recipes.description: Simple no-cook jelly from single-seed hawthorn berries.

instructions.text: Crush berries thoroughly by hand in a bowl.
Resulting liquid should be pudding-like consistency (add water if dry year).
Work quickly: squeeze seeds from berries.
Filter thick slurry into bowl.
In about five minutes, mixture will jell.
Flip onto plate; eat as-is, slice, or sun-dry.

notes: Keeps for many years when dried
Do not eat the seeds - they contain cyanide bonded with sugar (amygdalin)

recipes.title: Hawthorn Jelly (Euell Gibbons' Recipe)
recipes.attribution: Eat the Weeds - Green Deane (from Euell Gibbons)
recipes.description: Traditional cooked hawthorn jelly from the famous forager.

instructions.text: Crush fruit, add water.
Bring to boil, cover, simmer 10 minutes.
Strain through jelly bag, discard pulp/seeds/skins.
Add pectin and lemon juice if needed.
Boil 4 cups juice, add sugar.
Return to boil until perfect jelly test achieved.

notes: Do not eat the seeds - they contain cyanide bonded with sugar (amygdalin)

recipes.title: Hawthorn Schnapps
recipes.description: Hawthorn berry-infused vodka schnapps.

instructions.text: Rinse and dry berries.
Fill jar 2/3 full with berries.
Cover completely with vodka.
Seal tightly.
Steep 5-6 weeks in dark place at 64-68°F, shaking occasionally.
Strain and filter.
Age 2 months in dark before serving.

recipes.title: Haw Sauce
recipes.description: Tangy condiment sauce made from hawthorn berries.

instructions.text: Wash berries.
Cook with vinegar for 30 minutes.
Press pulp through sieve.
Return to pan with sugar and seasonings.
Boil 10 minutes.
Bottle and seal.

recipes.title: Hawthorn Berry Soup
recipes.description: Sweet spiced soup from hawthorn berries.

instructions.text: Add berries to pot with water.
Simmer gently 30 minutes, covered.
Cool and pass through sieve (discard seeds).
Transfer to pan, add sugar, cinnamon, chili.
Cook until sauce thickens.
Serve.

notes: Do not eat the seeds

recipes.title: Hawthorn Berry Catsup
recipes.description: Tangy ketchup-style condiment from hawthorn berries.

instructions.text: Remove berries from stalks, rinse.
Place in saucepan with vinegar and water.
Simmer 25 minutes until skins split.
Cool, push through sieve to remove pits.
Return to pan, add sweeteners.
Slowly heat, stir frequently, add spices.
Low boil 5-10 minutes until syrupy.
Add cherry juice gradually for consistency.
Pour into sterilized bottles.
Refrigerate, use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Sautéed Lion's Mane Mushroom
recipes.description: Simple sautéed lion's mane mushroom with crab-like flavor.

instructions.text: Clean mushroom and slice or tear into pieces.
Sauté in real butter until golden and tender.
Serve immediately.

notes: Has a texture and flavor reminiscent of crab or lobster

recipes.title: Maple Beer
recipes.attribution: Eat the Weeds - Green Deane (from F.A. Michaux, 1853)
recipes.description: Historical fermented maple beverage from 1853.

instructions.text: Pour the maple molasses into boiling water.
Add yeast to trigger fermentation.
Stir in the spruce essence.
Allow to ferment until a pleasant and salutary drink is obtained.

recipes.title: Redbud Blossom Muffins
recipes.description: Delicate muffins made with foraged redbud blossoms.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In bowl #1, combine redbuds, herb, sugar, and zest. Let sit 30 minutes.
In bowl #2, sift flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
In bowl #3, combine egg, yogurt, milk, oil, and lemon juice.
Pour bowl #1 contents into bowl #2 and toss.
Add wet ingredients from bowl #3, stirring until just moistened (avoid overmixing).
Fill muffin tins 3/4 full.
Combine 1 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp cinnamon; sprinkle on each muffin.
Bake 25 minutes until tops spring back when lightly touched.
Cool on wire rack.

notes: The light colored upper part of the blossom is sweet, the darker lower part is bitter

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Lotus Root
recipes.description: Asian-style stir-fried lotus root with sesame and sake.

instructions.text: Slice lotus root crosswise into quarter-inch pieces.
Soak in water and change until water runs clear, then dry thoroughly.
Heat sesame oil and add lotus roots, tossing briefly.
Add remaining ingredients and stir continuously for approximately 10 minutes until the mixture reduces.
Serve warm. Reheats well.

notes: Lotus root discolors quickly - place cut pieces in water with lemon juice immediately

recipes.title: Bulrush Broth
recipes.description: Hearty broth with bulrush shoots, roots, and oxtail.

instructions.text: Roll meat in flour-salt mixture.
Sauté in hot fat until browned.
Add water, shoots, onions, cover, and simmer 1.5 hours until rice is tender.

recipes.title: Bulrush Casserole
recipes.description: Comfort food casserole with bulrush sprouts and ground beef.

instructions.text: Mix meat with finely chopped onion, season.
Layer sprouts and meat in greased casserole.
Pour tomato soup over mixture.
Bake at 425°F for one hour until tender, adding tomato juice as needed.
Top with potato chips, bake 10 minutes more.

recipes.title: Creamed Bulrush
recipes.description: Tender bulrush shoots in a creamy white sauce.

instructions.text: Rinse shoots, steam with salt and water until limp. Drain, saving juice.
Chop shoots finely.
Melt butter in double boiler, stir in flour.
Gradually add juice and milk to reach 3 cups liquid, stirring constantly until smooth.
Season to taste. Garnish with egg slices.

recipes.title: Hunter's Stew with Bulrush
recipes.description: Hearty stew with beef, wild rice, bacon, and bulrush.

instructions.text: Boil bulrush roots in salted water for 30 minutes, drain, scrape and slice into 1/4-inch pieces.
Cook bacon until crisp, remove to paper towels.
Cook onions in fat until transparent.
Add beef, chives, roots, and bacon. Cook 15 minutes.
Stir in water and wine, season, simmer covered one hour.
Cook rice separately (30 minutes).
Add rice, shoots, and beef stock to skillet, bring to boil, simmer covered 30 minutes.
Add remaining stock if needed. Garnish with leeks and parsley.

recipes.title: Dandelion and Burdock Syrup
recipes.description: Sweet syrup concentrate for making soft drinks.

instructions.text: Heat water and add all ingredients except sugar.
Simmer 15-20 minutes, then strain.
Dissolve sugar while hot.
To serve: Dilute with soda (1:4 ratio).
Garnish with borage flowers in summer.

recipes.title: Begonia Tartlet
recipes.description: Unique tart with sour begonia leaves and cream.

ingredients.item: pastry or graham cracker tartlet shell

instructions.text: Chop the leaves and cook in a pot with approximately 1/2 cup water over medium-low heat until reduced to a thick paste.
Stir the sour cream and sugar into the paste.
Transfer mixture to tartlet and bake at 300°F for 30-60 minutes until the filling bubbles gently.
Cool before serving.

notes: This preparation also works with sorrel

recipes.title: Begonia Spread
recipes.description: Cream cheese spread with strawberry jam and begonia petals.

instructions.text: Combine cream cheese and jelly in a food processor or mixer.
Add chopped begonia petals and blend until well combined.
Adjust flower quantity based on personal preference.

recipes.title: Alligator Nuggets
recipes.attribution: Eat the Weeds - Green Deane (Bobby Flay method)
recipes.description: Crispy fried alligator bites with dipping sauces.

instructions.text: Heat oil to 360°F in a deep pot.
Coat meat with fish batter.
Fry 2-3 minutes until it floats.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with dipping sauces.

notes: Soak alligator meat in milk three hours before prepping to reduce swamp notes

recipes.title: Alligator Sauce Piquant
recipes.attribution: Eat the Weeds - Green Deane (Rouses Louisiana's Best)
recipes.description: Classic Louisiana alligator stew in spicy tomato sauce.

instructions.text: Create roux by cooking flour in oil until medium brown.
Add onion until wilted.
Mix in garlic, pepper, tomatoes, sauce, and water; simmer 30 minutes.
Add alligator, salt, pepper, and onion tops.
Cook 30-45 minutes until tender.

notes: Remove all yellow fat from alligator before cooking

recipes.title: Baked Armadillo
recipes.description: Whole armadillo baked with fruit stuffing.

instructions.text: Wash meat thoroughly.
Salt and pepper the armadillo.
Stuff cavity with fruit chunks.
Coat with butter, wrap in foil, place in roasting pan.
Bake at 325°F until internal temperature reaches 180°F (approximately 30-45 minutes per pound).

notes: Wear gloves when cleaning due to potential leprosy bacteria risk

recipes.title: Armadillo Fricassee
recipes.description: Slow-simmered armadillo with vegetables.

instructions.text: Dust meat in flour, salt, and pepper.
Brown both sides in butter.
Add water to cover vegetables.
Add potatoes, onions, carrots, celery, bay leaf, and thyme.
Cover and simmer approximately 2 hours until tender.
Thicken sauce with seasoned flour and water mixture.

recipes.title: Armadillo Chili
recipes.description: Hearty chili made with armadillo meat.

instructions.text: Remove stem and seeds from chili pod. Toast pod over medium-low heat until crisp. Cool, then crumble into powder.
Heat oil, brown meat in batches, remove.
Sauté onions, peppers, garlic, and powdered chili until tender.
Add remaining ingredients and browned meat.
Bring to boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 1 hour, stirring frequently until tender.
Serve with hot sauce, salsa, and cheese garnish.

recipes.title: Armadillo Meatloaf
recipes.description: Classic meatloaf made with ground armadillo.

instructions.text: Soak meat overnight in salted water. Remove from bones and grind.
Mix thoroughly with all ingredients.
Place in loaf dish in hot water bath.
Bake at 350°F for 1.25 to 2 hours.

recipes.title: Karela Bhaji (Pan-fried Bitter Melon)
recipes.description: Indian-style pan-fried bitter melon with aromatic spices.

instructions.text: Halve melon lengthwise; scrape out seeds and pith. Slice into 1/4-inch pieces.
Sprinkle with 1 tsp salt in a colander; drain 30 minutes. Squeeze and blot dry.
Warm ghee and oil until shimmering; toast cumin and fennel seeds ~30 seconds.
Add garlic and ginger; sauté 30 seconds.
Reduce heat to medium; add onion, coriander, turmeric, chili, pepper, and remaining salt. Sauté 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in melon and stock; sauté until tender and liquid mostly evaporates (~10 minutes), stirring often.
Add amchur and sugar; increase heat to high.
Pan-fry until liquid evaporates and melon crisps (~3 minutes), stirring frequently.
Season to taste; serve with cilantro.

recipes.title: Bitter Melon Salad (Philippine Style)
recipes.description: Fresh Philippine-style bitter melon salad with tomatoes.

instructions.text: Halve gourds lengthwise and scoop out seeds with a spoon.
Cut into half-moon pieces and toss with salt; let sit to remove bitterness.
Slice tomatoes into wedges and onion thinly.
Rinse salt from melon and combine with tomatoes and onions.
Dress with vinaigrette and chill before serving.

recipes.title: Chaya Soup
recipes.description: Creamy soup made with chaya (tree spinach) leaves.

instructions.text: Place chopped chaya leaves, onions, and garlic in a pot with vegetable bouillon.
Cook 10 minutes on medium heat until leaves are blanched.
Add milk and allow to cool slightly.
Blend remaining ingredients until smooth, return to pot.
Heat 5-10 minutes until hot (do not boil).
Serve with cream drizzled on top and optional crushed dried red chili.

notes: Cook chaya for at least 10-20 minutes to eliminate hydrogen cyanide
Avoid aluminum cookware - use glass or pottery

recipes.title: Japanese Knotweed Purée
recipes.description: Sweet purée from Japanese knotweed, similar to rhubarb.

instructions.text: Gather stalks and remove all leaves and tips.
Slice stems into 1-inch pieces and place in a pot.
Add sugar and let stand 20 minutes to extract juices.
Add water to prevent scorching.
Cook until pieces soften, adding more water if needed.
Mix thoroughly once cooked.
Season with lemon juice and additional sugar to taste.
Serve chilled as dessert, over vanilla ice cream, or in a pie shell.

notes: Can be refrigerated or frozen for later use
Similar to rhubarb sauce

recipes.title: Japanese Knotweed Bread
recipes.description: Quick bread made with sweetened knotweed purée and hazelnuts.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Beat egg white with oil and orange juice, then combine with hazelnuts and purée.
Add to dry ingredients, mixing gently until just moistened.
Transfer to buttered 9½-by-5-by-3-inch loaf pan.
Bake approximately 1 hour until a tester inserted in the center comes out dry.
Cool on a rack.

notes: For muffins, use muffin tins and bake about 25 minutes

recipes.title: Groundnut and Olive Stew
recipes.description: Hearty stew with American groundnuts, olives, and tomatoes.

ingredients.prep_note: California or Kalamata; reduce salt if using Kalamata

instructions.text: Cook large-cut groundnuts in abundant water until done (approximately 40 minutes). Drain thoroughly.
Combine all ingredients in a pot.
For a meatless version, simmer on medium heat until flavors meld, typically about an hour.
If including meat, use low heat until the meat becomes tender, requiring two to three hours.
Serve with hearty bread and red wine.

notes: Avoid aluminum cookware - latex smears and sticks badly
Groundnuts must be cooked; raw versions can taste bitter

recipes.title: Nasturtium Bouquet Salad
recipes.description: Elegant salad with radicchio, spinach, and nasturtium blossoms.

instructions.text: Whisk vinegar and mustard together in a bowl.
Gradually add oils while whisking. Add lime juice and zest.
Season with salt and pepper.
Just before serving, toss greens, chives, and flowers with sufficient dressing to coat.

recipes.title: Nasturtium Bundles
recipes.description: Cream cheese and pineapple wrapped in nasturtium leaves.

ingredients.prep_note: thyme, lemon verbena, lemon-scented geranium, basil, chives, or rose petals

instructions.text: Mix cream cheese, pineapple, and chosen herbs.
Spread generously on each leaf.
Roll up and arrange on a serving platter.
Garnish with nasturtium flowers.

recipes.title: Steamed Beets with Nasturtium
recipes.description: Tender beets with peppery nasturtium leaves and balsamic dressing.

instructions.text: Steam peeled beets until fork-tender (about 30 minutes).
Cool and cut into bite-sized wedges.
Whisk olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and salt together.
Sprinkle shredded nasturtium leaves over beets.
Drizzle with dressing and decorate with flowers.

recipes.title: Acorn Bread
recipes.description: Nutritious bread made with acorn flour and maple syrup.

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into a greased pan.
Bake at 400°F for 30 minutes or until done.

notes: Acorn flour contains no gluten; mix 50/50 with wheat flour for better binding

recipes.title: Acorn Muffins
recipes.attribution: Eat the Weeds - Green Deane (from BSteele, California)
recipes.description: Hearty muffins with acorn pulp, cornmeal, and walnuts.

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into well-greased muffin pans.
Bake at 400°F for 15 minutes.

notes: Store acorn flour carefully to prevent rancidity due to high oil content

recipes.title: Cattail Casserole
recipes.description: Savory cattail casserole with cheese.

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients in casserole dish.
Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Akebi Pod Miso Itame
recipes.description: Japanese stir-fried chocolate vine pods with miso.

instructions.text: Optionally soak pod halves in warm water for 30-60 minutes to reduce bitterness; pat dry.
Combine all liquid ingredients in a bowl, dissolving the miso paste and sugar together.
Heat oil in a fry pan. Add sliced akebi pod and sauté covered until softened, approximately 2 minutes.
Pour in the liquid mixture, reduce heat, and simmer until most liquid evaporates (1-2 minutes). Monitor closely to prevent burning.
Serve on a plate; garnish with chopped shiso leaf if desired.

recipes.title: Candied Eryngo Roots (Elizabethan)
recipes.source_note: Historical wild foraging recipe from eattheweeds.com
recipes.description: Traditional Elizabethan candied sea holly roots, once famous as an aphrodisiac.

instructions.text: Boil fresh roots in spring water until they reach the consistency of cooked parsnips.
Cut lengthwise and remove the pith with a knife.
Peel and soak in fresh water, then wring dry with cloth.
Bundle 3-4 roots together, tying at each end.
Create a syrup from sugar, rose water, and fair water.
Boil bundled roots in syrup until liquid nearly evaporates.
Shake in basin to distribute syrup coating.
Dry by fire and store in boxes.

notes: Famous in Colchester, England in Elizabethan times
Considered an aphrodisiac

recipes.title: Sea Lettuce Soup
recipes.description: Light Asian-style soup with sea lettuce (ulva) seaweed.

instructions.text: Bring stock to a boil.
Add sea lettuce and stir until soft.
Stir in beaten eggs and boil briefly, then remove from heat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add sesame oil, garnish with scallions, and serve.

notes: Wash sea lettuce well and optionally soak 2 hours before using

recipes.title: Toasted Sea Lettuce
recipes.description: Crispy toasted sea lettuce with sesame, similar to Korean nori.

instructions.text: Mix salt and sesame oil, rubbing thinly onto the sea lettuce.
Stack 6 sheets and roll; marinate 5 minutes.
Unroll and cook each sheet separately in a hot pan over low heat until crisp.
Cut into pieces and serve with hot rice.

notes: Refrigerate 2-3 days or freeze for six months
Can also toast over charcoal

recipes.title: Surinam Cherry Chiffon Pie
recipes.description: Light and airy chiffon pie with tropical Surinam cherries.

instructions.text: Soften gelatin in cold water.
Beat egg yolks with half the sugar, add fruit pulp.
Cook over medium heat until thick, stirring constantly.
Add softened gelatin and stir until dissolved. Cool.
Whip egg whites until frothy, gradually add remaining sugar, beating until peaks form.
Fold whites into cherry mixture.
Fill pie shell and chill until firm.
Top with whipped cream before serving.

notes: Only use ripe berries - one unripe berry can taint the rest
Select deep blood-red fruits

recipes.title: Spiced Tindora Curry (Ivy Gourd)
recipes.description: Indian-style spiced ivy gourd (tindora) curry.

instructions.text: Heat oil in medium non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds; allow to pop.
Add cumin seeds; let sizzle.
Add asafoetida, turmeric, green chilies, and tindora; mix well.
Season with salt, red chili powder, coriander, and cumin powder.
Cover and cook until tindora becomes tender, stirring every few minutes.
Uncover and cook additional minutes to lightly brown.

notes: Use the slicer blade of your food processor to quickly slice the tindora
Cleaned, cut tindora freezes well

recipes.title: Eel Stifle
recipes.description: Traditional layered eel and potato casserole.

instructions.text: Layer potatoes/onions, eel, and salt pork in buttered casserole.
Top with remaining potatoes/onions and salt pork.
Add milk.
Bake at 350°F for one hour until tender.

notes: Eels must be thoroughly cleaned - remove all traces of slime

recipes.title: Grilled Eel with Sage
